rows.english: Now the principal habitat for animals is supplied by the Great Outer Sea: their numbers here are great, their suffering limitless. Those that live in the lands of men and pleasure beings are spread all over, with no one particular location. The main place for craving spirits lies beneath the area of Rajagirha here on our continent, some five hundred yojana [about 2,250 miles] deep. Here lives the Lord of Death, known also as the Lord of All Things. He has the body of a craving spirit, for the past deeds that have thrown him into this place were non-virtuous. The deeds that determined the finishing details of his life, though, were virtuous--so he enjoys a kind of eminence, like one of the greater pleasure beings.

rows.english: This being the case, you should never let yourself think, "This is one of those practices meant for people who have nothing more profound to meditate upon." And you should never let yourself think that, "It is admittedly something we should meditate upon, but only at the beginning of our practice, and only for a bit at that; it's not something that warrants a continual effort to put into practice." Rather you should try to develop a true understanding, from the depths of your heart, where you realize that this is a meditation which you need at the start, at the end, and all throughout the path. With this understanding established within you then, you must meditate upon your death. 29 What Death Awareness Really Is

rows.acip: ,GSON PA'I TSE LA YANG CHOS BYA BA'I LONG MED PAR NGES PAR 'CHI BA BSAM PA NI, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I RING MTHA' DE TZAM THUB TU CHUG KYANG LONG YOD BYAR MI RUNG STE, DON MED DU TSE MANG PO ZHIG NI SNGAR 'DAS 'DUG PA DANG LHAG MA LA'ANG GNYID KYIS PHYED 'DA' ZHING , GZHAN YANG RNAM PAR G-YENG BA GZHAN GYIS KYANG DU MA ZHIG DON MED DU 'DA' BA DANG , LANG TSO YOL NAS RGAS PA'I GNAS SKABS SU SLEB NAS NI LUS DANG SEMS KYI STOBS NYAMS PAS CHOS BYED PAR 'DOD KYANG BSGRUB PA'I MTHU MED PAS CHOS BYED PA'I SKABS NI CUNG ZAD LAS MED DE, MNGAL DU 'JUG PA LAS, DE LAS KYANG PHYED NI GNYID KYIS KHEBS SO, , LO BCU NI BYIS PA'O, , LO NYI SHU NI RGAS PA STE, MYA NGAN DANG SMRE SNGAGS 'DON PA DANG SDUG BSNGAL BA DANG YID MI BDE BA DANG 'KHRUGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG BCAD, LUS LAS BYUNG BA'I NAD RNAM PA DU MA BRGYA PHRAG DU MAS KYANG BCAD DO, , ZHES PA DANG ,
rows.wylie: gson pa'i tshe la yang chos bya ba'i long med par nges par 'chi ba bsam pa ni, sngar bshad pa'i ring mtha' de tsam thub tu chug kyang long yod byar mi rung ste, don med du tshe mang po zhig ni sngar 'das 'dug pa dang lhag ma la'ang gnyid kyis phyed 'da' zhing , gzhan yang rnam par g-yeng ba gzhan gyis kyang du ma zhig don med du 'da' ba dang , lang tsho yol nas rgas pa'i gnas skabs su sleb nas ni lus dang sems kyi stobs nyams pas chos byed par 'dod kyang bsgrub pa'i mthu med pas chos byed pa'i skabs ni cung zad las med de, mngal du 'jug pa las, de las kyang phyed ni gnyid kyis khebs so, , lo bcu ni byis pa'o, , lo nyi shu ni rgas pa ste, mya ngan dang smre sngags 'don pa dang sdug bsngal ba dang yid mi bde ba dang 'khrugs pa rnams kyis kyang bcad, lus las byung ba'i nad rnam pa du ma brgya phrag du mas kyang bcad do, , zhes pa dang
rows.english: Next is contemplating (3) how certain it is that you will die without having had any time to practice the Dharma, even while you were alive. Suppose you were able to live to the end of one of those longest lives that we described above. Even so it would be wrong to think that you would have any free time all that time. So far in your life you have squandered a great deal of time meaninglessly; as for what remains, you will pass half of it in sleeping. The other half you will also spend meaninglessly, your mind filled with a great many other distractions. You will while away you days of good health and then arrive at old age, you body and mind worn out, and lacking any energy to do any Dharma, even if you wanted to. The point is that the window of opportunity during which we can undertake our spiritual practice is nothing more than a very brief period. As Entering the Womb relates, You spend half of it wrapped in sleep. Ten years is wasted by childhood, and another twenty in old age. From what's left you have to subtract the time you spend in grief, and the time you spend crying in anguish, and the time you spend in physical pain, and the time you spend in deep unhappiness, and the time you spend in strife. Subtract too the time that you spend going through all those thousands of different diseases which the body is subject to.

rows.acip: ,KA MA BA LA DMIGS PA SPO BAR ZHUS TZA NA SNGA MA SKYOR SKAD, 'PHRO NAS ZHUS TZA NA 'PHRO YE MA THOD PA ZHES GSUNG LO, , DE LTAR NA BLOS LCOGS NA SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN BSGOM ZHING , MA LCOGS NA RTZA BA GSUM LA RGYU MTSAN DGU JI LTAR 'TSAM PA RE BZUNG LA, GSOD SAR 'KHRID PA LA RGYAN BTAGS PA LTAR TSE 'DI'I BYA BA RNAMS LAS YID MA LOG GI BAR DU YANG DANG YANG DU BSGOM PAR BYA'O, , BSHES GNYEN BSTEN PA DANG DAL 'BYOR DANG MI RTAG PA'I SKOR RNAMS GSUNG RAB DGONGS 'GREL DANG BCAS PA GA NA 'DUG KYANG SKABS DE DANG DE'I NYAMS LEN DU SHES PAR BYAS NAS BSKYANGS NA RGYAL BA'I DGONGS PA RNAMS BDE BLAG TU RNYED PAR 'GYUR TE SKABS GZHAN DU 'ANG DE LTAR SHES PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: ka ma ba la dmigs pa spo bar zhus tsa na snga ma skyor skad, 'phro nas zhus tsa na 'phro ye ma thod pa zhes gsung lo, , de ltar na blos lcogs na sngar bshad pa bzhin bsgom zhing , ma lcogs na rtsa ba gsum la rgyu mtshan dgu ji ltar 'tsham pa re bzung la, gsod sar 'khrid pa la rgyan btags pa ltar tshe 'di'i bya ba rnams las yid ma log gi bar du yang dang yang du bsgom par bya'o, , bshes gnyen bsten pa dang dal 'byor dang mi rtag pa'i skor rnams gsung rab dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa ga na 'dug kyang skabs de dang de'i nyams len du shes par byas nas bskyangs na rgyal ba'i dgongs pa rnams bde blag tu rnyed par 'gyur te skabs gzhan du 'ang de ltar shes par bya'o
rows.english: They say too that when someone would ask Kamawa if they could move on to a new spiritual topic he would say, "Work again on the old one." When they asked if he could finish up the old one, he would say, "There is no finish to the old one." So if your mind can handle it, do the meditation as I have described it above. If your mind cannot handle it, then try to absorb as many of the nine reasons for the three principles as fits your capacity. Meditate over and over on your death until you gain a complete disgust for the activities of this life; until you can think of them like a man on his way to the site of his execution, stopping to put on some fine jewelry. The subjects of how to serve a spiritual guide, of the spiritual fortune and leisure of this life, and of our impermanence are found throughout the supreme form of speech, the word of the Buddha, and the commentaries upon it. You must come to realize that these are instructions to be put into practice at each point where they occur, and so you should actually undertake them at each step. If you do so, then you will be able to grasp the true intent of the victorious Buddhas quite easily. You should apply this advice to each of the other sections here as well. 205 The Asian Classics Institute Course XVII: The Great Ideas of Buddhism, Part Two Reading Seven: The Ethical Life, Part One 1 The Ethical Life Empowers You for Meditation and Wisdom The first reading for this class comes from Je Tsongkapa's Epistle to Ngawang Drakpa

rows.english: Because you have talked meaninglessly, fruits refuse to grow on the trees, or they start to grow at the wrong times, never at the right times, and seem ripe when they're still not ripe, or their roots are frail, or they can't stay long; there are no places to take your leisure, no parks, no glades, no pools of cool water, and many things around to make you afraid.

rows.english: Because you have wished bad things on others, you live in a world of chaos, where diseases spread, and evil is everywhere, and plague, and conflict, and fear from the armies of other nations; where there are many lions or leopards or other dangerous animals; where there are everywhere venomous snakes or scorpions or poison biting worms; surrounded by harmful spirits, and thieves or muggers, and the like.

rows.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, BSTAN PA THAMS CAD 'GAL MED SOGS BZHI STE, DE LTA BU'I GZHUNG 'DI NI, KHYAD CHOS SAM CHE BA BZHI DANG LDAN TE, GDAMS PA 'DI LA BRTEN NAS RGYAL BAS CHOS TSUL JI SNYED CIG GSUNGS PA THAMS CAD LAS, KHA CIG NI LAM GYI GTZO BO, KHA CIG NI DE'I YAN LAG STON BYED DU SHES NAS DNGOS DANG BRGYUD PA CI RIGS KYI SGO NAS 'TSANG RGYA BA'I CHA RKYEN DU GO BAR 'GYUR BAS NA, BSTAN PA THAMS CAD 'GAL MED DU RTOGS PA'I CHE BA DANG , MDO SNGAGS KYI GSUNG RAB RNAMS DANG DE'I DGONGS 'GREL GYI BSTAN BCOS RNAMS BSHAD CHOS TZAM DU BZUNG NAS NYAMS SU LEN RGYU DE DAG GI DON LAS GZHAN ZHIG NA YOD PAR 'DZIN PA'I LOG RTOG RNAMS LDOG STE, GSUNG RAB DGONGS 'GREL DANG BCAS PA'I BRJOD BYA MTHA' DAG NYAMS SU LEN GYI GO RIM DANG MTHUN PAR BSHES GNYEN BSTEN TSUL NAS ZHI LHAG GI BAR BSDUS NAS DPYAD SGOM DANG 'JOG SGOM CI RIGS KYI SGO NAS NYAMS SU LEN TSUL SHES PAR 'GYUR BAS NA, GSUNG RAB THAMS CAD GDAMS PAR 'CHAR BA'I CHE BA DANG , DE LTAR GSUNG RAB THAMS CAD GDAMS NGAG GI MCHOG YIN KYANG BLO MA SBYANGS PA'I LAS DANG PO BAS GZHUNG CHE BA DE DAG GI DGONGS DON RANG STOBS KYIS RTOGS NAS NYAMS SU LEN MI SHES PAS, DE DAG GI DGONGS DON RNAMS 'DUS PA'I BLA MA'I MAN NGAG BYANG CHUB LAM GYI RIM PA 'DI LTA BU LA BRTEN NAS GZHUNG CHE BA DE RNAMS KYI DGONGS DON LEGS PAR RTOGS PAR 'GYUR BAS NA, RGYAL BA'I DGONGS PA BDE BLAG TU RTOGS PA'I CHE BA DANG , DE LTAR RNYED PA'I TSE SANGS RGYAS KYI BKA' THAMS CAD DNGOS DANG BRGYUD PA CI RIGS KYI SGO NAS 'TSANG RGYA BA'I THABS SU GO NAS 'TSANG RGYA BA'I THABS MI STON PA'I SANGS RGYAS KYI BKA' MED PAR SHES TE, GSUNG RAB DE DAG LA GDUL BYA'I DBANG GIS BRJOD BYA CUNG ZAD RE MI MTHUN PA DANG MCHOG DMAN YOD KYANG , THAMS CAD 'TSANG RGYA BA'I THABS STON PA TZAM LA KHYAD PAR MED PAR NGES NAS CHOS SPONG BA'I LAS MI 'BYUNG BA STE, NYES SPYOD CHEN PO'I G-YANG SA LAS KYANG SRUNG BA'I CHE BA BZHI DANG LDAN PA'I PHYIR RO,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa ni, bstan pa thams cad 'gal med sogs bzhi ste, de lta bu'i gzhung 'di ni, khyad chos sam che ba bzhi dang ldan te, gdams pa 'di la brten nas rgyal bas chos tshul ji snyed cig gsungs pa thams cad las, kha cig ni lam gyi gtso bo, kha cig ni de'i yan lag ston byed du shes nas dngos dang brgyud pa ci rigs kyi sgo nas 'tshang rgya ba'i cha rkyen du go bar 'gyur bas na, bstan pa thams cad 'gal med du rtogs pa'i che ba dang , mdo sngags kyi gsung rab rnams dang de'i dgongs 'grel gyi bstan bcos rnams bshad chos tsam du bzung nas nyams su len rgyu de dag gi don las gzhan zhig na yod par 'dzin pa'i log rtog rnams ldog ste, gsung rab dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa'i brjod bya mtha' dag nyams su len gyi go rim dang mthun par bshes gnyen bsten tshul nas zhi lhag gi bar bsdus nas dpyad sgom dang 'jog sgom ci rigs kyi sgo nas nyams su len tshul shes par 'gyur bas na, gsung rab thams cad gdams par 'char ba'i che ba dang , de ltar gsung rab thams cad gdams ngag gi mchog yin kyang blo ma sbyangs pa'i las dang po bas gzhung che ba de dag gi dgongs don rang stobs kyis rtogs nas nyams su len mi shes pas, de dag gi dgongs don rnams 'dus pa'i bla ma'i man ngag byang chub lam gyi rim pa 'di lta bu la brten nas gzhung che ba de rnams kyi dgongs don legs par rtogs par 'gyur bas na, rgyal ba'i dgongs pa bde blag tu rtogs pa'i che ba dang , de ltar rnyed pa'i tshe sangs rgyas kyi bka' thams cad dngos dang brgyud pa ci rigs kyi sgo nas 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs su go nas 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs mi ston pa'i sangs rgyas kyi bka' med par shes te, gsung rab de dag la gdul bya'i dbang gis brjod bya cung zad re mi mthun pa dang mchog dman yod kyang , thams cad 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs ston pa tsam la khyad par med par nges nas chos spong ba'i las mi 'byung ba ste, nyes spyod chen po'i g-yang sa las kyang srung ba'i che ba bzhi dang ldan pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: This teachings possesses four special features, or you could say four great qualities. The first is that if you rely on this teaching you will come to realize that all of the Buddha's teachings are totally lacking any inconsistency. Of all the teachings spoken by the Victorious Buddhas, however many there may be, some of them teach the principal paths and others teach that which branches off from them. Once you know this, you will come to understand that they are all either direct or indirect factors in reaching enlightenment. You will not have the wrong view which considers the open and secret teachings of the Buddha--those highest of all words--and the classical commentaries which comment upon their true intent to be mere explanations. You will not think that you have to look somewhere other than in the content of these books for something to use for your personal practice. Rather you will come to see that the entire subject matter of the Buddha's supreme speech along with its classical commentaries is perfectly in keeping with the progressive structure through which you do your actual practice. You will come to understand how it is that every step from taking yourself to a Spiritual Guide all the way up to the practices of developing quietude and special vision can be put into your personal practice, either through analytical meditation or through fixation meditation. If you understand these points, then all of the high speech of the Buddha will strike you as personal advi

rows.acip: ,DE NAS 'DI PHYI'I LEGS TSOGS JI SNYED PA'I, ,RTEN 'BREL LEGS PAR 'GRIG PA'I RTZA BA NI, ,LAM STON BSHES GNYEN DAM PA 'BAD PA YIS, ,BSAM DANG SBYOR BAS TSUL BZHIN BSTEN PA RU, ,MTHONG NAS SROG GI PHYIR YANG MI GTONG BAR, ,BKA' BZHIN SGRUB PA'I MCHOD PAS MNYES PAR BYED, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
rows.wylie: de nas 'di phyi'i legs tshogs ji snyed pa'i, ,rten 'brel legs par 'grig pa'i rtsa ba ni, ,lam ston bshes gnyen dam pa 'bad pa yis, ,bsam dang sbyor bas tshul bzhin bsten pa ru, ,mthong nas srog gi phyir yang mi gtong bar, ,bka' bzhin sgrub pa'i mchod pas mnyes par byed, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
rows.english: After having done this, see that the very foundation Of an excellent start for all the good in this and your future lives Is the holy Spiritual Guide who teaches you the path. Make efforts to rely on Him properly in your thoughts and in your actions; Please Him with the offering of carrying out His every instruction. And never give it up, not even at the cost of your life. I, the master meditator, lived my life this way; You, who seek for freedom, must try to do the same.

rows.english: First you must contemplate the points above, such as the great benefits that come from putting into practice all, or even just a part of, the steps of the path. After having done this, says Je Tsongkapa, you should begin the actual practices which are to follow. He uses these words to lead the reader into the actual steps of the path.

rows.english: This life's difficult to find, and easily destroyed, like lightning in the sky. Think this over carefully and come to realize: All the activities of the world are chaff blown in the wind. To take the essence of this life, you must strive night and day. I, the master meditator, lived my life this way; You, who seek for freedom, must try to do the same. 17 The Contemplation on the Lower Realms

rows.english: Polluted by downfalls and the stench of bad deeds committed through all three doors, It's crucial to purify yourself, especially of the obstacles these deeds create. You must then with great reverence depend on the four forces, continually. I, the master meditator, lived my life this way; You, who seek for freedom, must try to do the same. 19 The Four Truths

rows.acip: ,RTZE GCIG BSAM GTAN TZAM LA 'KHOR BA YI, ,RTZA BA GCOD PA'I NUS PA MA MTHONG ZHING , ,ZHI GNAS LAM DANG BRAL BA'I SHES RAB KYIS, ,JI TZAM DPYAD KYANG NYON MONGS MI LDOG PAS, ,YIN LUGS PHU THAG CHOD PA'I SHES RAB DE, ,G-YO MED ZHI GNAS RTA LA BSKYON NAS NI, ,MTHA' BRAL DBU MA'I RIGS PA'I MTSON RNON GYIS, ,MTHAR 'DZIN DMIGS GTOD THAMS CAD 'JIG BYED PA'I, ,TSUL BZHIN DPYOD PA'I YANGS PA'I SHES RAB KYIS, ,DE NYID RTOGS PA'I BLO GROS RGYAS PAR MDZAD, ,RNAL 'BYOR NGAS KYANG NYAMS LEN DE LTAR BGYIS, ,THAR 'DOD KHYED KYANG DE BZHIN BSKYANG 'TSAL LO,
rows.wylie: rtse gcig bsam gtan tsam la 'khor ba yi, ,rtsa ba gcod pa'i nus pa ma mthong zhing , ,zhi gnas lam dang bral ba'i shes rab kyis, ,ji tsam dpyad kyang nyon mongs mi ldog pas, ,yin lugs phu thag chod pa'i shes rab de, ,g-yo med zhi gnas rta la bskyon nas ni, ,mtha' bral dbu ma'i rigs pa'i mtshon rnon gyis, ,mthar 'dzin dmigs gtod thams cad 'jig byed pa'i, ,tshul bzhin dpyod pa'i yangs pa'i shes rab kyis, ,de nyid rtogs pa'i blo gros rgyas par mdzad, ,rnal 'byor ngas kyang nyams len de ltar bgyis, ,thar 'dod khyed kyang de bzhin bskyang 'tshal lo
rows.english: It's impossible that single-pointed concentration by itself could ever have The power to cut the very root of the cycle of suffering life; And wisdom which is separated from the path of quietude Could never stop your mental afflictions, no matter how much you analyzed. Mount then the wisdom that rips apart the reality of how things are On the horse of meditative quietude that cannot ever sway. Next use the razor sword of the logic of the middle way free of extremes To destroy all tendencies to think in a way that holds an extreme. Take this far-spreading wisdom that examines things in the proper way To bring the knowledge that perceives simple suchness to prosper ever further. I, the master meditator, put this into practice; You, who seek for freedom, must try to practice this way.

rows.english: The path that's commended for reaching the perfection of the deeds of the children Of the Victors is combining the two of method and wisdom having meditated On both the emptiness of absorption, the one like empty space, And the emptiness of the aftermath: the one like an illusion. The way of those blessed by goodness is to understand this fact, And never be satisfied with only a piece or a part of the path. I, the master meditator, put this into practice; You, who seek for freedom, must try to practice this way. 30 The Path of the Secret Way

It is a paraphrase of sections from the Life Stories of the Lineage Teachers of the Steps of the Path (Lam-rim bla-ma brgyud-pa'i rnam-thar) written by Yongdzin Yeshe Gyeltsen (1713-1793), the teacher of the eighth Dalai Lama. 1 The Life of Master Shantideva, in Brief Master Shantideva was born to the west of Bodhgaya, the Seat of the Diamond, in a place called Yulkor Mosang. His father was a king named Armor of Virtue, and his mother was said to be an emanation of Vajra Yogini, the Angel of Diamond. He was able to choose the details of his birth, and when he was born he was given the name Armor of Peace. rows.acip: ,DE NAS BYAMS PA DANG SNYING RJE'I RTZA BA CAN GYI BYANG CHUB KYI MCHOG TU SEMS BSKYED PA LA 'KHOR LO SGYUR BA'I RGYAL PO SPYAN 'DREN PA'I GNAS KHANG SOGS BYI DOR BYED PA BZHIN DU 'GAL RKYEN SGRIB PA BSHAGS PA DANG , MTHUN RKYEN TSOGS BSAGS NAS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS GZUNG DGOS PA'I SNGA MA LE'U GNYIS PA DANG , PHYI MA LE'U GSUM PAS BSTAN TO,
rows.wylie: de nas byams pa dang snying rje'i rtsa ba can gyi byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa la 'khor lo sgyur ba'i rgyal po spyan 'dren pa'i gnas khang sogs byi dor byed pa bzhin du 'gal rkyen sgrib pa bshags pa dang , mthun rkyen tshogs bsags nas byang chub kyi sems gzung dgos pa'i snga ma le'u gnyis pa dang , phyi ma le'u gsum pas bstan to
rows.english: You must go about developing the wish to achieve supreme enlightenment, that wish whose very root is love and compassion, in the same way that you would go about preparing to welcome a King who ruled the entire world by cleaning your house, and so on. You will be able to acquire this wish by purifying all of the factors which obstruct your spiritual realizations, and gathering together the power of good deeds which promote them. These two subjects are covered respectively in the second and third chapters.

rows.english: Give flowers, and fruits, as many as exist; And all the different herbs, as many as there may be. Give each and every precious substance contained in the planet, All the pure and lovely water that exists. Give the precious mountains, and so too The forests, quiet places of refuge, and lovely spots; Give the plants, studded with flowers, and adorned, The trees whose branches are bent low under fine ripe fruit. Give fragrances and incenses, even those which are found In the worlds of pleasure beings and the like; The wishing tree, and the tree of precious substances. Give grain that grows without ever being planted, And any other lovely object which is worthy of presenting-- Lovely lakes and bathing ponds bedecked with lotus blossoms And water birds of beauty, singing their splendid songs. ************

rows.english: I imagine in my mind each and every one Of those objects owned by no one Which may exist in all the infinite expanse Of all of myriad space. I offer these In an excellent way, to the highest Of all living beings, to the Able Ones, Along with their sons and daughters. May all of these beings of highest spiritual qualities, Who possess the ultimate form of compassion, Look upon me with love, and accept all I offer. ************

rows.acip: ,DE YANG LTUNG BA PHYIR BCOS NI SDOM PA GONG 'OG SO SO NAS GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA LA SDIG PA PHYIR BCOS PA NI STOBS BZHI'I SGO NAS BYA STE, CHOS BZHI BSTAN PA'I MDO LAS, BYAMS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' SEMS DPA' CHEN PO CHOS BZHI DANG LDAN NA SDIG PA BYAS SHING BSAGS PA YANG ZIL GYIS GNON PAR 'GYUR RO, , BZHI GANG ZHE NA, 'DI LTA STE, RNAM PAR SUN 'BYIN PA KUN TU SPYOD PA DANG , GNYEN PO KUN TU SPYOD PA DANG , NYES PA LAS BZLOG PA'I STOBS DANG , RTEN GYI STOBS SO ZHES GSUNGS TE BYAS SHING BSAGS PA'I LAS NI MYONG NGES YIN PAS DE ZIL GYIS GNON NUS NA MA NGES PA LTA CI SMOS,
rows.wylie: de yang ltung ba phyir bcos ni sdom pa gong 'og so so nas gsungs pa ltar bya la sdig pa phyir bcos pa ni stobs bzhi'i sgo nas bya ste, chos bzhi bstan pa'i mdo las, byams pa byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po chos bzhi dang ldan na sdig pa byas shing bsags pa yang zil gyis gnon par 'gyur ro, , bzhi gang zhe na, 'di lta ste, rnam par sun 'byin pa kun tu spyod pa dang , gnyen po kun tu spyod pa dang , nyes pa las bzlog pa'i stobs dang , rten gyi stobs so zhes gsungs te byas shing bsags pa'i las ni myong nges yin pas de zil gyis gnon nus na ma nges pa lta ci smos
rows.english: Instances in which you have committed some transgression of your vows, at whichever level of vows you may have, should be repaired according to the methods prescribed for those particular vows. For repairing the damage caused by other kinds of bad deeds you should utilize the four powers. As the Sutra on the Four Practices states, If, oh Loving One, some great bodhisattva has succeeded in the four practices, then even those bad deeds which have been both committed and collected can be overcome. What are the four practices? They are as follows: the activity of destruction; the activity of applying the antidote; the force of restraining from the particular bad deed; and the force of the foundation. The expression "committed and collected" refers to actions whose karmic results are "certain to be experienced." If even these types of karmic results can be overcome by the four practices, then there is no need to mention those which are not certain to be experienced.

rows.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, DPER NA RMI LAM DU BDE BA CUNG ZAD CIG NYAMS SU MYONG BA SAD PA'I TSE DRAN PA'I YUL TZAM DU 'GYUR PA BZHIN DU SNGAR BDE BAR RLOM PA'I DNGOS PO GANG DANG GANG LONGS SPYAD PA DE DANG DE 'CHI BA'I TSE DRAN PA'I YUL TZAM DU 'GYUR BAS DA LTA NYID NAS CHOS 'BA' ZHIG BYA BAR THAG GCOD PA LAN MANG DU BYA'O, , GANG DANG GANG 'DAS PA THAMS CAD MTHONG BAR MI 'GYUR BAR DRAN PA'I YUL TZAM DU ZAD PA'O,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa ni, dper na rmi lam du bde ba cung zad cig nyams su myong ba sad pa'i tshe dran pa'i yul tsam du 'gyur pa bzhin du sngar bde bar rlom pa'i dngos po gang dang gang longs spyad pa de dang de 'chi ba'i tshe dran pa'i yul tsam du 'gyur bas da lta nyid nas chos 'ba' zhig bya bar thag gcod pa lan mang du bya'o, , gang dang gang 'das pa thams cad mthong bar mi 'gyur bar dran pa'i yul tsam du zad pa'o
rows.english: Think of some minor pleasure that you might experience during a dream. When you wake up, the pleasure is no longer anything but a memory. All the objects that you might deceive yourself into thinking are pleasant in this life, and which you use, are the same. When you die they are soon nothing but some memory. Therefore you should resolve, from this moment on, and time and time again, that you will only practice the Dharma. All those things that have passed are no longer here, and so they become nothing more than a memory.

rows.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, DRAN PA DE LAS GANG GI TSE DRAN PA YID KYI SGO NAS NYON MONGS BSRUNG BA'I DON DU GNAS PAR GYUR PA DE'I TSE BYA BA DANG BYA BA MA YIN PA'I GNAS SKABS LA RTOG CING JI LTA BA BZHIN DU SHES PA'I SHES BZHIN YOD PAR 'GYUR ZHING , LAN CIG NYAMS NAS SONG BA DAG KYANG PHYIR 'ONG BAR 'GYUR BAS BSGRUB PA NYAMS LEN LA MKHAS MI MKHAS NI, DRAN PA DANG SHES BZHIN GYI SKYED TSUL LA RAG LAS PAS DES DE LA MKHAS PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa ni, dran pa de las gang gi tshe dran pa yid kyi sgo nas nyon mongs bsrung ba'i don du gnas par gyur pa de'i tshe bya ba dang bya ba ma yin pa'i gnas skabs la rtog cing ji lta ba bzhin du shes pa'i shes bzhin yod par 'gyur zhing , lan cig nyams nas song ba dag kyang phyir 'ong bar 'gyur bas bsgrub pa nyams len la mkhas mi mkhas ni, dran pa dang shes bzhin gyi skyed tshul la rag las pas des de la mkhas par bya'o
rows.english: Here is the second point. Suppose a person reaches a point where he or she is able to keep their recollection very solid--is able to use their mind to protect themselves against mental afflictions. At this point then the recollection will lead this person to gain a kind of awareness, where they are able to watch themselves and grasp properly the distinction between occasions when their actions are proper, and when they are improper. It is also the case that, even should these two attitudes slip and disappear at some point, they nonetheless return. Therefore the question of whether one becomes a master of Buddhist practice or not hinges upon how well one can maintain their recollection and awareness; and thus one should seek to become a master of these two attitudes. 19 The Idea of Freezing on the Spot

rows.acip: ,DANG PO NI, DON MED PAR PHYOGS SU G-YENG BAR BLTA BA NI DUS NAM YANG BDAG GIS MI BYA STE SEMS NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO, , DGE BA'I DMIGS PA LA NGES PAR SEMS PAS DUS RTAG TU NI BLTA BA'I TSE GNYA' SHING GANG TZAM DU MIG NI PHAB STE BLTA BAR BYA'O, , LTA BA NGAL BSO'I CHED DU NI, , RES 'GA' PHYOGS SU BLTA BAR BYA,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, don med par phyogs su g-yeng bar blta ba ni dus nam yang bdag gis mi bya ste sems nyams par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro, , dge ba'i dmigs pa la nges par sems pas dus rtag tu ni blta ba'i tshe gnya' shing gang tsam du mig ni phab ste blta bar bya'o, , lta ba ngal bso'i ched du ni, , res 'ga' phyogs su blta bar bya
rows.english: Here is the first. I should never, at any time, look around from side to side meaninglessly, with my mind distracted. This is because of the fact that, should I do so, my mind will get worse. Rather I should be sure to fix my mind on a virtuous object: whenever I look around, I should always keep my eyes lowered, looking ahead no farther than the length of a plowshare, [which is explained in scripture as one armspan].

rows.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, SBYIN PA'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA LA SOGS PA SHES RAB KYI BAR DU GONG NAS GONG DU KHYAD ZHUGS SHING 'PHEL BA SPYAD PAR BYA'O, , SBYIN PA DANG TSUL KHRIMS SOGS DGOS PA DANG DGE BA CHUNG NGU'I PHYIR NI CHE BA MI BTANG ZHING CHEN PO LA 'BAD PAR BYA'O, , SHUGS KYIS GNYIS KA CIG CAR MI NUS SHING NANG 'DOMS NA CHEN PO BSRUNG BA'I DON DU CHUNG NGU BTANG BAR BSTAN TO, , CHE CHUNG GANG GIS 'JOG CE NA TSE 'DI'I RANG DON DANG GZHAN DON LTA BU GCIG BYAS PAS CIG SHOS NYAMS PAR 'GYUR NA, GTZO CHER GZHAN GYI DON BSAM MO,
rows.wylie: gsum pa ni, sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa la sogs pa shes rab kyi bar du gong nas gong du khyad zhugs shing 'phel ba spyad par bya'o, , sbyin pa dang tshul khrims sogs dgos pa dang dge ba chung ngu'i phyir ni che ba mi btang zhing chen po la 'bad par bya'o, , shugs kyis gnyis ka cig car mi nus shing nang 'doms na chen po bsrung ba'i don du chung ngu btang bar bstan to, , che chung gang gis 'jog ce na tshe 'di'i rang don dang gzhan don lta bu gcig byas pas cig shos nyams par 'gyur na, gtso cher gzhan gyi don bsam mo
rows.english: Here is the third. I will perform the perfections of giving and "the rest," meaning all of those up to wisdom, in such a way that they are heightened ever further; that is, so they increase in strength. Whenever I engage in the perfections of giving, an ethical way of life, or any of the others, I should never give up activities which are of greater virtuous power for those which are of less--I should rather concentrate my efforts on the greater. These lines are indicating, by implication, the following: where one is unable to perform both the action of lesser power and the one of greater power--where a time has come where one must choose between the two--then we should give up the deed of lesser virtue to prevent the greater one from being lost. How do we establish which deeds are greater, and which are lesser? If for example there is a choice between accomplishing one's own aims or someone else's aims in this present life--if by bringing about one you would lose the other--then you should concentrate on others' aims. 27 The Principles of Greater Good

rows.english: Here is the second. I should not teach the profound and far-reaching aspects of the Dharma to those of lesser minds, to those who are not fit to receive these teachings. Nor should I teach the Dharma to a woman alone, without another male present. It is further stated that one has committed the bad deed of rejecting the Dharma if one discriminates between different parts of the teaching, by saying for example that the teachings of the greater and lesser ways are, respectively, superior and inferior kinds of Dharma--one better than the other; one more proper than the other; one a way to enlightenment, and the other not; or anything of the like. I should therefore follow a code of behavior where I respect all of them equally, and put each of them into practice. 31 We Must Teach to a Person's Level

rows.acip: ,GSUM PA LA GNYIS, YID MI BDE BSKYED MI RIGS PA DANG , DE'I RGYU MTSAN NO, , DANG PO NI, 'O NA YID MI BDE JI LTAR SPANG ZHE NA, SDUG BSNGAL DANG DU BLANGS PA'I PHAN YON BSAMS NAS CI LA BAB KYANG BDAG GIS NI RANG GI DGA' BA'I YID NI DKRUG PAR MI BYA SNYAM DU LEGS PAR BSAMS TE, YID DGA' BA NI YID MI BDE BA'I GNYEN PO YIN PAS MI 'DOD PA CI BYUNG YANG DE LA MI DGE BA BA BYAS KYANG 'DOD PA'I DON MI 'GRUB CING 'DOD PA'I 'BRAS BU 'BYIN PA'I DGE BA DAG NI NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BAS SDUG BSNGAL MTHA' DAG BSKYED PAR 'GYUR RO,
rows.wylie: gsum pa la gnyis, yid mi bde bskyed mi rigs pa dang , de'i rgyu mtshan no, , dang po ni, 'o na yid mi bde ji ltar spang zhe na, sdug bsngal dang du blangs pa'i phan yon bsams nas ci la bab kyang bdag gis ni rang gi dga' ba'i yid ni dkrug par mi bya snyam du legs par bsams te, yid dga' ba ni yid mi bde ba'i gnyen po yin pas mi 'dod pa ci byung yang de la mi dge ba ba byas kyang 'dod pa'i don mi 'grub cing 'dod pa'i 'bras bu 'byin pa'i dge ba dag ni nyams par 'gyur bas sdug bsngal mtha' dag bskyed par 'gyur ro
rows.english: The third point, on the actual methods for stopping anger, has two parts: a description of how very wrong it is to become upset, and then the reasons why it is so wrong. Here is the first. "How can I get rid of the emotion of being upset?" you may ask. You should first contemplate the benefits of learning to accept suffering gladly. Then you must learn to think to yourself, clearly, "No matter what happens, I will never allow my joy to be disturbed." Joy is the antidote for feeling upset; and no matter what happens that you don't like, doing something which is non-virtuous in return cannot accomplish your hopes, and only makes you lose the goodness that you do have, the goodness that can in fact produce the result you are hoping for. If this happens, then every other sort of suffering will come as well.

rows.english: Here is the first. Consider the hardships that one must undertake to achieve enlightenment. The Supreme Physician, the Lord of the Able Ones, does not perform these treatments of his in a way that's like those other, ordinary ones that are used to cure some illness. Rather he uses a particular kind of technique or method that's gentle in the extreme, a blissful path to reach a blissful goal. It is a path which avoids both extremes: it neither leaves one spent and exhausted, nor leads to the thoughtless consumption of resources. He uses it to cure the massive and infinite ills of the mental afflictions, which force us to continue wandering in the circle of suffering. It could never be right then for you to fear these spiritual hardships.

rows.english: Here is the third point, which is how recollection and awareness leave no opening for problems to arise. Imagine now that someone has shot you with a poison arrow, and that the poison is making its way throughout your entire body, riding upon the blood as it courses through your veins. Just so do the various mental afflictions, such as losing your recollection, act should they find any opening to do so. And when they do find an opening, then the different negativities of anger and the rest make their way throughout the entire mind. For this reason you must try to stop even the slightest mental affliction whenever it should arise.

rows.acip: BDAG GZHAN GYI BDE SDUG LA DMIGS NAS 'DOR LEN MTSUNGS PAR BYED RIGS PAR THAL, GANG GI TSE BDAG DANG GZHAN GNYIS KA BDE BA 'DOD DU MTSUNGS PA LA BDAG DANG GANG ZAG GZHAN KHYAD PAR CI YOD NA CI YANG MED PA'I PHYIR, RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA BDAG GCIG BU BDE BAR BRTZON PAR BYED CING GZHAN GYI BDE BA LA MI BRTZON PA MI RIGS SO, , GANG GI TSE BDAG DANG GZHAN GNYIS KA SDUG BSNGAL MI 'DOD PAR MTSUNGS PA LA BDAG DANG GZHAN KHYAD PAR CI YOD NA STE CI YANG MED PA'I PHYIIR RO, , RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR GZHAN GYI BDE BA BSRUNG BA MIN PAR BDAG GI BDE BA CHED DU BSGRUB CING MI NYAMS PAR SRUNG BAR BYED, GNYIS KA MTSUNGS PAR BSGRUB RIGS SO,
rows.wylie: bdag gzhan gyi bde sdug la dmigs nas 'dor len mtshungs par byed rigs par thal, gang gi tshe bdag dang gzhan gnyis ka bde ba 'dod du mtshungs pa la bdag dang gang zag gzhan khyad par ci yod na ci yang med pa'i phyir, rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na bdag gcig bu bde bar brtson par byed cing gzhan gyi bde ba la mi brtson pa mi rigs so, , gang gi tshe bdag dang gzhan gnyis ka sdug bsngal mi 'dod par mtshungs pa la bdag dang gzhan khyad par ci yod na ste ci yang med pa'i phyiir ro, , rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir gzhan gyi bde ba bsrung ba min par bdag gi bde ba ched du bsgrub cing mi nyams par srung bar byed, gnyis ka mtshungs par bsgrub rigs so
rows.english: It is right that I should act exactly the same towards the happiness and sufferings of others as I do towards those of my own, for the following reasons. Given the fact that both myself and others are exactly the same in how we want happiness, what difference then could there ever be between us--between myself and others? There is no difference at all. And for what reason then do I work only for happiness for myself--what is my justification? Why do I not work the same for the happiness of others? What I'm doing now is not right. Given the fact that both myself and others are exactly the same in how we do not want any pain, what difference could there ever be between us, between myself and others? There is no difference at all. And for what reason then do I fail to protect the happiness of all others, and concentrate instead on reaching my own happiness, and protecting it from ever being lost? The two happiness are exactly the same, and it is right for me to work to achieve them both. Contemplation Fifteen Being beyond oneself

rows.acip: ,TSUL KHRIMS DANG LTA BA NYAMS PA SOGS KYI DBANG GIS BYANG SEMS LHA SBYIN LAS KHYOD DMAN NO ZHE NA, TSUL KHRIMS DANG LTA BA NYAMS PA DANG 'TSO BAS RGUD PA SOGS LTA BA DANG SPYOD PA NYAMS PA NI GLO BUR BA'I NYON MONGS PA'I STOBS KYIS YIN GYI BDAG NYID KYI 'DOD PA'I RANG DBANG DU GYUR PA'I SKYON MIN NO, , YANG NA RKANG PA 'DI LA GLO BUR NYON MONGS RNAMS KYIS MIN ZHES 'DON NO,
rows.wylie: tshul khrims dang lta ba nyams pa sogs kyi dbang gis byang sems lha sbyin las khyod dman no zhe na, tshul khrims dang lta ba nyams pa dang 'tsho bas rgud pa sogs lta ba dang spyod pa nyams pa ni glo bur ba'i nyon mongs pa'i stobs kyis yin gyi bdag nyid kyi 'dod pa'i rang dbang du gyur pa'i skyon min no, , yang na rkang pa 'di la glo bur nyon mongs rnams kyis min zhes 'don no
rows.english: Suppose someone comes and says, "You are inferior to this bodhisattva John, due to the fact that your morality and your worldviews are degenerate, and the like." But the degenerate state of our morality and worldviews, and the fact that we have troubles making a living and all the rest--all this degeneration of both the way we think and the way we act--is forced upon us by temporary factors, by mental affliction. The problem here is not that we have chosen to be this way, not that we want to be this way. The relevant part of the root text here can also be read as "are rather forced by the temporary factor of affliction." 86 The Asian Classics Institute Course XVIII: The Great Ideas of Buddhism, Part Three Reading Three: The Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life, Fifth of Six Parts The following contemplations are based on the Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life (Bodhisattvacharyavatara; Byang-chub-sems-dpa'i spyod-pa la 'jug-pa) of the Buddhist master Shantideva (circa 700 AD), and the commentary upon it by Gyaltsab Je Darma Rinchen (1364-1432) entitled Entry Point for Children of the Victorious Buddhas (rGyal-sras 'jug-ngogs). The relevant sections are found at folios 30B-31A and 114A-117A, respectively, in the ACIP electronic editions TD3871 and S5436. The content of the contemplations is translated directly from the root text and commentary; the names of the contemplations are not a part of the original text, but are based on the divisions of Gyaltsab Je's commentary a

rows.acip: ,STONG NYID LA YID 'GYUR BA'I MYONG BA SKYE BA LA YANG DE DAG SNGON DU 'GRO DGOS PA'ANG MIN TE, DE LTA NA MI RTAG PA RTOGS PA LTA BU'I NYAMS MYONG LA'ANG DE DAG SNGON DU 'GRO DGOS PA MTSUNGS SO,
rows.wylie: stong nyid la yid 'gyur ba'i myong ba skye ba la yang de dag sngon du 'gro dgos pa'ang min te, de lta na mi rtag pa rtogs pa lta bu'i nyams myong la'ang de dag sngon du 'gro dgos pa mtshungs so
rows.english: Neither is it the case that, in order to have an experience of emptiness that would lead to a deep conviction in it, these other perfections would have to come first. If this were so, then they would also have to come first in order for a person to have a deep experience of something like the realization of impermanence--the two causes would be just the same.

rows.acip: ,SANGS RGYAS LA RTOG PA MED KYANG MCHOD PA BYAS PAS BSOD NAMS 'BYUNG BA 'THAD PAR THAL, RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA SANGS RGYAS SKU DNGOS SU BZHUGS PA'AM MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS RJES KYI SKU GDUNG LA MCHOD PA GNYIS BSOD NAMS MTSUNGS PA NYID DU BYAMS PA SENG GE SGRA'I MDO LAS BSHAD PA'I PHYIR RO,
rows.wylie: sangs rgyas la rtog pa med kyang mchod pa byas pas bsod nams 'byung ba 'thad par thal, rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na sangs rgyas sku dngos su bzhugs pa'am mya ngan las 'das rjes kyi sku gdung la mchod pa gnyis bsod nams mtshungs pa nyid du byams pa seng ge sgra'i mdo las bshad pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Isn't it though the case that, even though Buddhas have no conceptual state of mind, we can still obtain merit through making offerings to them? You may ask our reason for saying so; it is because of the explanation, found in the Sutra on the Lion's Roar of Loving One, that whether a person makes an offering to a Buddha who is actually present, or else makes the same offering to their tomb after they have passed into nirvana, the merit from the act is exactly the same.

rows.acip: SHOGDNG PO NI, BSTAN BCOS RTZOM PA PO BDAG GIS GSUNG RAB MTHA' DAG GI BRJOD PAR BYA BA'I DON GANG ZAG GCIG SANGS RGYAS THOB PA'I LAM 'BRAS BU DANG BCAS PAR BSDUS TE SKYES BU GSUM GYI LAM GYI RIM PA RDZOGS PAR NYAMS SU LEN PA'I TSUL BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SPYOD PA LA 'JUG PA ZHIB TU PHYE NAS BRTZAMS PA'I DGE BA GANG THOB PA DE DANG , BSTAN BCOS 'DI 'CHAD PA DANG NYAN PA DANG DON SEMS PA'I DGE BA GANG YOD PA DES 'GRO BA KUN BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SPYOD PA TSUL BZHIN NYAMS SU LEN PA LA 'JUG PAR SHOG CIG PA'O,

rows.english: Here is the first. "I," meaning the author of this commentarial classic, "have thus finished composing a very thorough guide to the way of life followed by bodhisattvas. It expresses the entire contents of the highest of all spoken words: it incorporates a description of the entire path for reaching Buddhahood, including an explanation of this result itself; that is, it shows how to actually put into practice every one of the steps of the path designed for people of three different scopes. I hereby dedicate all the virtue that I have achieved through this act, as well as all the virtue that anyone may ever obtain through teaching, or learning, or thinking about the meaning of this book. Through this virtue, may every living being engage in--that is actually practice, properly--the bodhisattva's way of life."

rows.english: The causes that create the Buddha are consummate thoughts and actions. Proving that these constitute a totally pure path that we should practice is accomplished by using the eight different forms of logic. As such there is but one main way of keeping the teachings of the victorious Buddha safe in the world, and this is to become a master of the logical forms used to prove some things and to disprove others. As the Goldmine of Reasoning [by the Sakya Pandita, Kunga Gyeltsen (1182-1251)] says, Suppose a person comes to understand The scriptural tradition for how to reason: This art of proving or disproving things. A master like this is a person who keeps The teachings of the totally enlightened Buddhas safe here in the world. *************** The second selection is a very famous quotation from scripture which is memorized by every young monk who begins the geshe course in a Tibetan monastery. It describes one of the ultimate reasons for studying the art of reasoning:

rows.wylie: mdo las, gang zag gis gang zag gi tshod gzung bar mi bya ste, nyams par gyur te re, zhes rang la mi snang ba tsam gyis gzhan la yon tan de lta bu med ces 'chad mi rigs pa'i don ston pa la, rnam 'grel las, tshad ma rnams ni mi 'jug pa, med la mi 'jug 'bras bu can, zhes sogs kyis bstan
rows.english: There is a sutra where it says, No person should ever judge another; those who try will fall. The point of these words is to show us how wrong it is for us to say that someone else lacks any particular good quality, only because it does not appear to us that they do. This same point is made in the Commentary with lines such as the following: In a case where valid perception has yet To engage in the object, the result obtained Is that they don't: they didn't engage. *************** Formal logic subject: The definition of a reason The selections on formal logic that follow are also taken for the most part, from the Key to the Logic Machine.

rows.english: Here is the first. Now there is a sutra where it says, No person should ever judge another; those who try will fall. The point of these words is to show us how wrong it is for us to say that someone else lacks any particular good quality, only because it does not appear to us that they do. This same point is made in the Commentary with lines such as the following: In a case where valid perception has yet To engage in the object, the result obtained Is that they don't: they didn't engage.

rows.english: Keep these seven Dharma teachings in your heart, and let your Dharma practice be something that you do inside yourself: 1) This sickness didn't just happen by itself; so use the medicine and get rid of it. 2) On the level of appearances, karma and its consequences never fail; so clean away your bad karma, your bad deeds and your obstacles. 3) The reality of things is beyond the mind; so reside in a state where you hold to nothing. [This statement should not be taken literally, but rather interpreted in light of the teachings of the Middle Way.] 4) Grasping to things as self-existent is what forces you to take birth; so cut the ties of all your hopes and dreams. 5) Your inner nature is the Body of Voidness; so recognize how sick you are. 6) Whatever happens is a holy blessing; so think of everything that happens as an attainment. 7) Think whatever you want; but don't think of anything as pain.

rows.english: Now there are a great many ways of teaching those advices for training oneself in the greater way--the lojong, or instructions for developing the good heart. In the tradition of the spiritual friend, the geshe, Chekawa, these instructions are organized into a seven-part practice. These seven are: 1) Instructions on the foundation Dharma, the preliminary practices; 2) The actual practice for developing the Wish for Enlightenment [bodhichitta]; 3) Learning to use problems as a path to Enlightenment; 4) A summary of an entire lifetime's practice; 5) The point at which one can say that he or she has successfully developed the good heart; 6) Pledges to keep for developing the good heart; and 7) Certain advices on developing the good heart.

rows.acip: DRUG PA BLO SBYONG GI DAM TSIG BSTAN PA NI, SPYI DON GSUM KHAS BLANG DANG MA 'GAL BA, THO COR MA SONG BA, PHYOGS RER MA LTUNG BA STE, MCHAN, LA RTAG TU BSLAB, 'DUN PA BSGYUR LA RANG SOR BZHAG, YAN LAG NYAMS PA BRJOD MI BYA, , GZHAN PHYOGS GANG YANG MI BSAM MO, NYON MONGS GANG CHE SONG LA SBYANG , , 'BRAS BU RE BA THAMS CAD SPANG , , DUG CAN GI ZAS SPANG , , GZHUNG BZANG PO MA BSTEN, , SHAG NGAN MA RGOD, 'PHRANG MA BSGUG, GNAD LA MI DBAB, MDZO KHAL BLANG LA MI 'BYO, , MGYOGS KYI RTZE MI GTOD, GTO LOG MI BYA, LHA BDUD DU MI DBAB, SKYID KYI YAN LAG TU SDUG MA TSOL,
rows.wylie: drug pa blo sbyong gi dam tshig bstan pa ni, spyi don gsum khas blang dang ma 'gal ba, tho cor ma song ba, phyogs rer ma ltung ba ste, mchan, la rtag tu bslab, 'dun pa bsgyur la rang sor bzhag, yan lag nyams pa brjod mi bya, , gzhan phyogs gang yang mi bsam mo, nyon mongs gang che song la sbyang , , 'bras bu re ba thams cad spang , , dug can gi zas spang , , gzhung bzang po ma bsten, , shag ngan ma rgod, 'phrang ma bsgug, gnad la mi dbab, mdzo khal blang la mi 'byo, , mgyogs kyi rtse mi gtod, gto log mi bya, lha bdud du mi dbab, skyid kyi yan lag tu sdug ma tshol
rows.english: Part Six: Pledges to Keep for Developing the Good Heart Keep to the three laws. Change your mind and stay the same. Speak not of what was broken. Never worry about what they're doing. Rid yourself of the biggest affliction first. Never hope for any reward. Stop eating poison food. Don't let the stream flow smooth. Forget repaying criticism. Give up laying ambushes. No going for the jugular. Load your own truck, no passing the buck. Don't get fixed on speed. Don't feed the wrong face. Don't turn the sweet angel to a devil. Don't look for crap to make yourself happy. Note by the Tibetan commentator: The three laws are never acting in a way that contradicts what you have committed yourself to; never placing yourself in a dangerous situation; and never falling into the habit of discriminating between others.

rows.wylie: dka' ba gsum nyon mongs pa skyes pa na, dran pa, bzlog pa, rgyun chod pa gsum, la bslab par bya, , rgyu yi gtso bo rnam gsum bla ma mjal, chos nyams su len, chos kyi mthun rkyen 'dzom pa ste, blang , , nyams pa med pa rnam gsum mos gus, spro ba, bslab bya, bsgom, lus ngag yid gsum dge ba dang , 'bral med gsum dang ldan par bya
rows.english: Train yourself in the three kinds of hardship. Take to yourself the three main causes. Live in three ways that never get weaker. Keep the three that should never be lost. Note by the Tibetan commentator: The "three hardships" are learning to detect the start of a mental affliction; to stop it; and to stop the habit. The "three main causes" are finding a Lama, practicing the Dharma, and having all the support you need to practice the Dharma come together. The "three ways" are feeling devotion [for your Lama], joy [for practicing the lojong or instructions for developing a good heart], and keeping your various vows and commitments [through strong awareness and recollection]. The "three that should never be lost" are virtuous actions in your actions, your words, and your thoughts.

rows.english: And the Sachen thought carefully about the meaning of these words. And he came to realize that the entire practice of the path of the perfections could all be found here, in these words for developing the good heart, called "Freedom from the Four Attachments." And thus did he come to an extraordinary level of understanding all the things there are.

rows.english: Discounting things is like this; it is saying that the following do not, all in all, exist: that which is the foundation, with the typical features, of the words used to make constructs--that which provides the basis, with the characteristics, of the words used to make constructs; that which exists ultimately, through an identity beyond all expression; and that which is a pure, functioning thing. They are, in short, things that waste one's opportunity; you should understand that these two will cause you to fall from this spiritual way of discipline. The beginning part of this second section constitutes a description of what it is to discount something; and the part including the words "waste one's opportunity" on down is describing how a person would then fall from the profound teaching of the greater way.

rows.english: You take as the object Of the way you look at things That absence of something there: The simple lack of anything Which could really exist When you look at body & mind And say “me.” You keep it up strong, Clear and vivid. rows.english: The protector Nagarjuna Said things like: “For those on the outside, There is no means To reach Peace. They have lost the truths Of the deceptive and of suchness; And no one who loses these two truths Can ever be free.” Those books by the way Were dedicated to me! The phrase “on the outside” most often refers to anyone who cannot comprehend any of the four classical Buddhist ways of explaining the world.  Technically though any group except the higher half of the fourth school—the Consequence Group—will be unable to reach a genuine state of peace, since on some level they still cling to a thing which could even in some small way come from its own side. Reference is also made in these lines to the idea of two divisions to reality itself: a “deceptive” division, and an “ultimate” division, here referred to as “suchness.”  The former refers to things as observed from the viewpoint of appearing to come from their own side, even though in the end they cannot.  “Ultimate” reality then is the very fact that nothing could ever come from its own side. If these pleasure beings Could begin to feel hate, Then that would contradict The idea that their lovely love Existed in reality, And depended on nothing else. When these temporarily god-like beings (who are, again, created by the karmic seeds of deep meditation, but without emptiness content) give birth to children in their realms, it should be a birth which does not cause them any kind of pain. rows.wylie: chos rnams rang rang ngo bos ni, ,stong par nyams 'og chud pa na, ,stong gzhi chos rnams ming rkyang tsam, ,btags tsam brda tsam tha snyad tsam
rows.english: Once we slide into The feeling of how Things are empty Of any nature Of their own, Then we see How the things That have the emptiness Exist only as names; Only imputed; Only in the signs, Only in the terms. The word “imputed” implies that something has been said to be a certain way, but is not really or entirely that way.  Normally as we are born into this world and go through our process of growing up, we never imagine that the things and the people around us are somehow coming from how we have treated anybody else, in the past. That is, we “impute” an existence to things that actually we have no justification or good reason for saying that they have: from their own side, independent of anything, existing in isolation from the ethical content of our life to date. Saying that things exist “only as names,” or “signs,” or “terms,” are all just different ways of saying that things have no trace of existence beyond the pictures coming out of our ethical or unethical seeds.

rows.english: And why is that? I myself am the king Within the hearts Of every single one Of the six types of beings. As such, I reign Over the three poisons, And guide people's practice Of the ten bad deeds. And I guide folks To the highlight Of them all: the five Immediate bad deeds. It is I who turns the wheel Of birth, of getting old, Of illness and of dying. This is the real farming Going on here In the world. All of us in this world are subject to the four facts of an extremely painful birth into this world; aging daily, until we are weak and exhausted; illness that comes more & more often as the years go by; and an inevitable death—losing everything, and everybody. But just how is it that misunderstanding runs this terrible show? If we could—with daily practice and study—get completely used to the idea of seed-pictures, then necessarily we would stop planting bad seeds with the people around us in life. We would plant only good seeds, and they would constantly reinforce what good seeds we all already have, and pretty soon the power of our good seeds will be sufficient to renew and refresh and transform our body & mind, day to day, until we live in permanent, perfect happiness—and provide a priceless example for everyone else at the same time. rows.acip: ,NYAMS LEN DE LTAR YOD PA NI, ,NGA NYID YOD LAS BYUNG BA YIN, ,YOD LA MED PA SGRO 'DOGS PA, ,CHAD PA'I MTHAR LHUNG KHYOD LA 'GAL,
rows.wylie: nyams len de ltar yod pa ni, ,nga nyid yod las byung ba yin, ,yod la med pa sgro 'dogs pa, ,chad pa'i mthar lhung khyod la 'gal
rows.english: That fact that this Is how people Do their practice All comes only from My blessed presence. This habit of yours Of seeing something Where nothing is there— Of saying that everything That exists cannot exist— Is a fall off the cliff Of saying that Everything there is Has discontinued; And thus you Contradict yourself. The reference to the “cliff” here is important, since it refers—again—to our habit of failing to walk a middle way between things existing as they seem to, and things not existing at all. In a way, Wisdom has been trying to teach us about a way of living that we never considered before, since we had no idea (and why would we?) that the sufferings of our life were coming from seeds in our own mind. Her idea of a perfect future must seem to the Devil—and to many of us—the equivalent of the grand mistake of thinking that, if things don't exist the way we always thought they did, from their own side, then they should not exist at all.

rows.wylie: chos par rlom pa la las ni, ,chos ni gzhan las gal che skad, ,rang gis cung zad nyams len tshe, ,rtags mtshan spu tsam byung ba la'ang, ,rang nyid bzang por rlom pa dang, ,gzhan dag rnams la thos sgrog byed, ,bstod ra cung zad byung ba la, ,nga rgyal khams gsum gang bar bsgom
rows.english: Some who entertain The delusion that they Are great practitioners Go and take teachings From others, and prattle on About how important those were. Then they go and put Those teachings into practice; And if they get the tiniest sign Of any progress, they begin To entertain the delusion That they are a special person. And then they run to others And advertise their achievements; When someone gives them The slightest amount of praise, The conceit they feel Is sufficient to fill All three realms Of the universe. It's one thing to fail in a spiritual path; say, if we are unable to maintain a regular meditation practice, and fail because of that.  But it's even worse to get a little bit of success in these efforts, and then develop pride or arrogance which sets us far back even from where we started.

rows.english: At some points In this process, We experience a bliss Like the one that Young lovers might feel; It is a state of being beyond All description at all. It's a dream that a deaf mute Suddenly enjoys. We experience a sensation Which is beyond All verbal description. Traditionally, the ages of 16 for a young lady and 17 for a young man are considered a point in physical and mental development where the inner winds are naturally moving with great facility—thus the intensity of "young lovers" such as our Romeo & Juliet. The image here is of a handicapped person who has never spoken, nor even heard others' speech, but who in a dream listens and converses fluently.  We are meant to imagine the sudden freedom of our deepest states of mind to perceive the deepest entity in the universe.

rows.acip: DES NA GANG NYAMS SU BLANG RGYU DE DANG POR GZHAN LAS THOS NAS GZHAN STOBS KYIS NGES PAR BYED, DE NAS THOS PA'I DON DE RANG GIS LUNG DANG RIGS PAS TSUL BZHIN DU BSAMS TE RANG STOBS KYIS NGES PAR BYED, DE LTAR THOS BSAM GYIS NGES PAR BYAS TE THE TSOM DANG BRAL BA NA YANG YANG DU 'DRIS PAR BYED PA LA BSGOMS PA ZHES ZER BAS, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: des na gang nyams su blang rgyu de dang por gzhan las thos nas gzhan stobs kyis nges par byed, de nas thos pa'i don de rang gis lung dang rigs pas tshul bzhin du bsams te rang stobs kyis nges par byed, de ltar thos bsam gyis nges par byas te the tshom dang bral ba na yang yang du 'dris par byed pa la bsgoms pa zhes zer bas, zhes gsungs pa ltar bya dgos pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: The practice you are going to have to undertake begins with reaching a certain level of understanding by relying on someone else: by learning at their feet. We then contemplate on our own the meaning of what we have learned, employing both scriptural authority and logical reasoning, and thus come to understandings gained through our own effort. At some point, this process of reaching understandings through learning and contemplation frees us of every possible doubt; and then it is time to accustom ourselves to these truths by reviewing them over and over again—a process which we call “meditation.”

rows.acip: THOS BSAM BSGOMS GSUM MANG NYUNG GIS NYAMS LEN KYANG MANG NYUNG 'ONG BAR GSUNGS TE, LAM RIM CHEN MO LAS, DES NA THOS PA JI TZAM MANG BA TZAM DU DE LAS BYUNG BA'I SHES RAB MANG LA, DE MANG BA TZAM DU BSAM PA MANG BA DANG DE MANG BA TZAM DU DE LAS BYUNG BA'I SHES RAB MANG BA DANG, DE JI TZAM MANG BA BZHIN DU BSGOM PAS NYAMS SU LEN PA MANG LA, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: thos bsam bsgoms gsum mang nyung gis nyams len kyang mang nyung 'ong bar gsungs te, lam rim chen mo las, des na thos pa ji tsam mang ba tsam du de las byung ba'i shes rab mang la, de mang ba tsam du bsam pa mang ba dang de mang ba tsam du de las byung ba'i shes rab mang ba dang, de ji tsam mang ba bzhin du bsgom pas nyams su len pa mang la, zhes gsungs pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: It's been stated that the question of whether these three—your learning, contemplation, and meditation—are less or more is what determines whether your putting the teachings into actual practice is less or more. As the Great Book on the Steps of the Path describes it: Thus we can say that the question of how much wisdom you will ever possess is something that depends on how much learning you ever undertake. And the question of how much contemplation you will ever be able to perform depends on that amount of learning. And the question of how much wisdom you will ever glean from this contemplation is a question, in turn, of that amount. And the more that wisdom ever becomes is what decides the total amount of Buddhist practice you will ever succeed in doing, based upon your meditation.

rows.acip: CHOS 'DI DAG THAMS CAD DON DAM PAR NA MA SKYES PA YIN YANG SGYU MA BZHIN DU RGYU DANG RKYEN SO SOR NGES PA SNA TSOGS 'DUS PA'I DBANG GIS MA BRTAGS NA NYAMS DGA' BA SNA TSOGS KHO NA DAG 'BYUNG STE, DES NA CHAD PAR LTA BAR YANG MI 'GYUR RO,,
rows.wylie: chos 'di dag thams cad don dam par na ma skyes pa yin yang sgyu ma bzhin du rgyu dang rkyen so sor nges pa sna tshogs 'dus pa'i dbang gis ma brtags na nyams dga' ba sna tshogs kho na dag 'byung ste, des na chad par lta bar yang mi 'gyur ro
rows.english: None of these things—none of the objects in the entire universe—ever started, in an ultimate sense. Nonetheless, they act like an illusion: when specific causes and conditions gather together, then due to this—if we don't look too closely—it appears that a whole variety of what are only impressions do arise. Thinking of it this way prevents the mistake of believing that the world has discontinued completely.

rows.english: And suppose, moreover, that the deep practitioner's senses degraded to the point where they could no longer think of anything; or that—due to some kind of mental darkness—they were unable to think of or attend to things. rows.acip: CI STE DE DRAN PA NYAMS PA YANG MA YIN, GLEN PA YANG MA YIN NA NI DE'I TSE YANG DAG PAR SO SOR RTOG PA MED PAR JI LTAR DRAN PA MED PA DANG, YID LA BYED PA MED PAR BYED NUS PAR 'GYUR, DRAN BZHIN DU YANG MI DRAN, MTHONG BZHIN DU YANG MI MTHONG NGO ZHES BYAR MI RUNG NGO,,

rows.english: And suppose you were to say that neither had their capacity to think degenerated; nor were they simply stupid—and yet still they were able to reach, without any careful examination of things, a state beyond thinking of, and a state beyond attending to, anything at all. And yet it would be wrong to say that a person was thinking while they were not thinking; and that they were seeing, while they were not seeing.

rows.acip: DE SKAD 'PHAGS PA CHOS THAMS CAD SHIN TU RGYAS PA LAS KYANG BKA' STZAL TE, BYAMS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' RNAMS KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA DRUG YANG DAG PAR BSGRUBS PA 'DI NI RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI PHYIR YIN NA, DE LA YANG MI BLUN PO DAG 'DI SKAD DU BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA KHO NA LA BSLAB PAR BYA'I, PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA LHAG MA RNAMS KYIS CI ZHIG BYA ZHES ZER ZHING, DE DAG PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA GZHAN DAG LA SUN 'BYIN PAR SEMS SO,,
rows.wylie: de skad 'phags pa chos thams cad shin tu rgyas pa las kyang bka' stsal te, byams pa byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi pha rol tu phyin pa drug yang dag par bsgrubs pa 'di ni rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi phyir yin na, de la yang mi blun po dag 'di skad du byang chub sems dpas shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa kho na la bslab par bya'i, pha rol tu phyin pa lhag ma rnams kyis ci zhig bya zhes zer zhing, de dag pha rol tu phyin pa gzhan dag la sun 'byin par sems so
rows.english: We see the same thought expressed in places like this one, from the exalted scripture entitled The Incredible Extant of Everything There Is: O Loving One, the way that the bodhisattvas practice the six perfections is all for the purpose of attaining a total enlightenment. And yet some fools say things like: “Oh, bodhisattvas only practice the one perfection—the perfection of wisdom. What use do they have with the other perfections?” In speaking thus, they propose to abolish all the other perfections.

rows.acip: ZHI GNAS RANG GI NGO BO NI, PHYI ROL PA DANG THUN MONG BA STE, PHYI ROL PA'I BSAM GZUGS KYI NYAMS LEN NAS DMA' SHOS YIN YANG RANG RES 'DIR NGES 'BYUNG GI BSAM PAS ZIN NA THAR PA'I RGYU DANG, SKYABS 'GROS ZIN NA CHOS SU 'GRO,
rows.wylie: zhi gnas rang gi ngo bo ni, phyi rol pa dang thun mong ba ste, phyi rol pa'i bsam gzugs kyi nyams len nas dma' shos yin yang rang res 'dir nges 'byung gi bsam pas zin na thar pa'i rgyu dang, skyabs 'gros zin na chos su 'gro
rows.english: The essence of the practice of quietude is something shared with the traditional non-Buddhist schools. That is, if you took even the very lowest practice of the meditations for the concentration and formless realms by one of these particular non-Buddhist schools, and then could imbue it with thoughts of true renunciation, then those meditations would act as a cause for freedom. If you could imbue that same practice with an attitude of going for refuge, then it would be Buddhist Dharma itself.

rows.english: And Tsongkapa, Je Rinpoche, composed a total of 18 entire volumes filled with different titles; but he never followed the tradition of writing the titles of his books in three lines with ornamental Sanskrit followed by Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, and then the Tibetan itself. This is not because he was ignorant of the finer points of Sanskrit grammar such as word formation or the treatment of nominal stems; rather, he was afraid that spending his time on such matters would be detrimental to his spiritual practice.

rows.english: We could use the metaphor of an enemy to describe this stage in our progress. At first, the enemy is extremely powerful. rows.english: This is a reference, our Lama noted, to a non-Buddhist sage by the name of Udraka, who spent many years in meditation on this level known as “Peak of Existence.” At some point he saw that his yogi's dreadlocks had been chewed on by a rat while he was in his meditation; and he got very angry. rows.english: There are a lot of scriptural references, and also logical proofs, in support of this idea that I could give you here at this point, but I will restrain myself.  Suffice to say that the exact manner in which this particular belief system describes how there are no outer objects is somewhat recondite.  It would seem the case that—if you really seek a proper understanding of these points—you can ascertain them through a study of presentations of the Mind Only system found in the Three Teachings of Maitreya, the Coming Buddha; or else in those of great masters such as Arya Asanga, or Master Vasubandhu.  It is absolutely clear though that—if you fail to seek such an understanding—you will never really grasp this system.

rows.acip: [E166] SKU LA 'KHRUL PA DANG, GSUNG LA CA CO DANG, THUGS LA DRAN PA NYAMS PA DANG, THUGS MNYAM PAR MA BZHAG PA DANG, 'KHOR 'DAS LA BDEN PA'I THA DAD PA NYID KYI 'DU SHES DANG, SO SOR MA BRTAGS PAR GDUL BYA YAL BAR 'DOR BA'I BTANG SNYOMS MI MNGA' BA'I SPYOD PA RNAM PA DRUG CHOS CAN, SPYOD PA MA 'DRES PA YIN TE, KHYOD KYI RIGS SANGS RGYAS KHO NA LA MNGA' BA'I SPYOD PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: [e166] sku la 'khrul pa dang, gsung la ca co dang, thugs la dran pa nyams pa dang, thugs mnyam par ma bzhag pa dang, 'khor 'das la bden pa'i tha dad pa nyid kyi 'du shes dang, so sor ma brtags par gdul bya yal bar 'dor ba'i btang snyoms mi mnga' ba'i spyod pa rnam pa drug chos can, spyod pa ma 'dres pa yin te, khyod kyi rigs sangs rgyas kho na la mnga' ba'i spyod pa yin pa'i phyir
rows.english: Consider then the following six unmixed qualities of behavior: (90) the bodily activities of an Enlightened Being, in which no error is ever displayed; (91) the fact that a Buddha never engages in chatter; (92) the fact that they are incapable of losing their awareness of what they are doing; (93) the fact that they are never out of a state of deep meditation; (94) the fact that they have no conception of the suffering world—and the state beyond it—as being separate in a self-existent way; and (95) the fact that the Buddhas never engage in a form of equanimity free of intellectual discrimination, where they would give up on any single one of their disciples. All these are unmixed sorts of behavior, Because their type of behavior is a kind that is possessed only by a Buddha.

rows.english: And then consider these six aspects of enlightenment: (96) the fact that a Buddha never loses their aspiration to be of service to others; (97) the fact that they never lose joyful effort in carrying out this service; (98) the fact that they never lose their awareness, in the sense of never losing sight of the methods to remain joyful in that service; (99) and never fall out of their meditative concentration, staying single-pointed on the true nature of things; (100) and never fall out of that wisdom which understands that their knowledge is now never-ending; (101) and, finally, never fall out of their total liberation, for as long as the cycle of suffering may remain. These then are unmixed sorts of realization, Because their type of realization is a kind that is possessed only by a Buddha.

rows.acip: [D24] NGAG DON NI SHES BYA CHOS CAN, BYANG CHUB SEMS DPAS MTHAR SHES BYA'I SGRIB PA MA LUS PAR SPANGS PAR 'THOB NUS TE, DES CHOS THAMS CAD BDEN MED DU RIGS PAS GTAM LA PHAB CING, SGOM BYUNG GIS NYAMS SU BLANGS PAS 'PHAGS LAM RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I YE SHES RIM CAN DU SKYES TE BDEN 'DZIN GYI SA BON MA LUS PAR SPONG NUS PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: [d24] ngag don ni shes bya chos can, byang chub sems dpas mthar shes bya'i sgrib pa ma lus par spangs par 'thob nus te, des chos thams cad bden med du rigs pas gtam la phab cing, sgom byung gis nyams su blangs pas 'phags lam rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes rim can du skyes te bden 'dzin gyi sa bon ma lus par spong nus pa'i phyir
rows.english: And then the following syllogism expresses what's being stated here: Consider each and every knowable thing in the universe. The bodhisattva is indeed able, in the end, to rid themselves of each and every obstacle to the state of omniscience; Because they first learn the logical conversation which allows them to establish that nothing in the universe is real; and then through their formal meditation practice they gradually make this understanding into a personal, meditational realization: they develop, step by step, the path of the realized ones—the wisdom which no longer imagines that things are real. [Incidentally, Kedrup Je then goes on in his text to demonstrate how these four levels of deep practice are problematic in the lower schools which still assert that the functionality of things is innate to them—a group of schools which includes the present, Mind Only School!] Appendix E: Eight arguments on the existence of foundation consciousness There are eight famous arguments used to support the belief of the Mind Only School that a foundation consciousness does indeed exist.  They are presented by Je Tsongkapa in both the root text and autocommentary of his Difficult Points in the Mind Only School, and thus commented upon by The Blade in his Golden Key. We have added the Key to this translation project precisely because it does make it easier for all of us to then make the deep jump into Je Tsongkapa's much more difficult treatment.  On some points though this means a much

rows.wylie: skyon 'di med de byang sems las sangs rgyas 'khrungs par rtsa bar bstan pa'i don ni, rgyu mtshan dang po'i skabs su slob lam gyi byang sems kyis, lam nyams su blangs pa las 'bras bu sangs rgyas thob pa la bshad pa na, byang sems des thob pa'i sangs rgyas kyi sras byang sems de min par shes pas, de la bden mod kyi zhes zer ba ga la yin
rows.english: And yet there is no such problem. When the root text states that Buddhas take their holy birth from bodhisattvas, it's understood that—in the context of the first way that they do so—when we speak of a bodhisattva who is on a path where they are still learning and who undertakes a practice of the spiritual path and then attains the goal of becoming a Buddha, then we are not saying that the bodhisattva who turned into the Buddha is the child of that particular Buddha. As such we would obviously not be referring to this particular bodhisattva and Buddha when we say “It is admittedly true” that bodhisattvas are children of the Buddhas.

rows.acip: 'O NA JI LTAR YIN SNYAM NA, SNGAR THEG CHEN LA 'JUG 'DOD PAS THOG MAR SNYING RJE CHEN PO SKYED DGOS PAR BSTAN KYANG, CI 'DRA BA ZHIG BSGOMS PAS SNYING RJE SKYED TSUL SNGAR MA BSTAN PAS, 'DIR SEMS CAN RNAMS RANG DBANG MED BAR 'KHOR BAR 'KHYAMS TSUL BSTAN PA LTAR BSGOMS PAS, SNYING RJE CHEN PO SKYED TSUL STON PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: 'o na ji ltar yin snyam na, sngar theg chen la 'jug 'dod pas thog mar snying rje chen po skyed dgos par bstan kyang, ci 'dra ba zhig bsgoms pas snying rje skyed tshul sngar ma bstan pas, 'dir sems can rnams rang dbang med bar 'khor bar 'khyams tshul bstan pa ltar bsgoms pas, snying rje chen po skyed tshul ston pa yin no
rows.english: And why not? We have already described how those who wish to enter the greater way must, at the outset, develop great compassion. But we haven't, at least to this point, explained what it is that a person should meditate upon in order to develop this compassion. As such, we are now showing how a person can develop great compassion, by meditating upon the way in which living beings wander, helplessly, here in the wheel of life.

rows.english: Consider rather the kind of person who has yet to give any serious thought about how they themselves are wandering through this cycle of pain—and so has yet to experience any kind of mental transformation. This kind of raw beginner then can hardly reach a state of mind where they can no longer bear the pain of these others because they have turned their attention to the situation that others face.

rows.acip: DE LA SANGS RGYAS GNYIS PA KLU SGRUB ZHABS LA SOGS PA'I LUGS THOS BSAM GYIS GTAN LA 'BEBS PA NI, RANG GIS YANG DAG PA'I LAM NYAMS SU LEN TSUL LA NGES PA CHEN PO RNYED NAS, LAM LTAR SNANG RNAMS KYIS BKRI BAR MI NUS PA'I CHED DU YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: de la sangs rgyas gnyis pa klu sgrub zhabs la sogs pa'i lugs thos bsam gyis gtan la 'bebs pa ni, rang gis yang dag pa'i lam nyams su len tshul la nges pa chen po rnyed nas, lam ltar snang rnams kyis bkri bar mi nus pa'i ched du yin no
rows.english: Now the whole purpose of undertaking learning & contemplation in order to come to an understanding of the system of that second Buddha, the great Nagarjuna, is so that—by reaching a deep place of certainty in our own practice of the correct path—we can assure that it is impossible for us ever to be misdirected to some mistaken path.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR SHING RTA CHEN PO RNAMS KYI LUGS KYI GZHUNG LA CI TZAM SBYANGS KYANG, RANG GI LAM NYAMS SU LEN PA'I TSUL LA NGES PA CI YANG MI RNYED PA'I THOS BSAM PA NI, THOS BSAM BYED TSUL GNAD DU MA SONG BA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir shing rta chen po rnams kyi lugs kyi gzhung la ci tsam sbyangs kyang, rang gi lam nyams su len pa'i tshul la nges pa ci yang mi rnyed pa'i thos bsam pa ni, thos bsam byed tshul gnad du ma song ba'i phyir
rows.english: Thus we can say that—no matter how much a person trains themselves in the classics of the schools of the great innovators—the way in which they undertake study & contemplation misses the mark if this learning & thinking doesn't at all result in their coming to some place of certainty in their own actual practice of the path.

rows.acip: 'DI NI MCHOD BRJOD KYI SKABS NYID DU BSHAD PAS, SKABS 'DIR MA BSHAD DO, ,DE'I DGOS PA NI GANG BSGOMS PA LA BRTEN NAS BYANG SEMS SU 'GYUR BA'I RGYU'I GTZO BO GSUM BSTAN PAS, THEG CHEN DU 'JUG PAR 'DOD PAS DE GSUM THOG MAR NYAMS SU BLANG DGOS PAR BSTAN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: 'di ni mchod brjod kyi skabs nyid du bshad pas, skabs 'dir ma bshad do, ,de'i dgos pa ni gang bsgoms pa la brten nas byang sems su 'gyur ba'i rgyu'i gtso bo gsum bstan pas, theg chen du 'jug par 'dod pas de gsum thog mar nyams su blang dgos par bstan pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: This question has already been covered, in the section on the offering of praise itself; as such, we will not go through it again here. The point of doing it this way though is that the text first presents the three principal causes which—once one meditates upon them—lead one to become a bodhisattva. This is in order to indicate that those who wish to enter the greater way must first put into practice these three.

rows.acip: DE GSUM NI SNGON DU NYAMS SU LEN DGOS PAR MA ZAD, BYANG SEMS SU GYUR NAS KYANG NYAMS SU BLANG DGOS PA LA, GNYIS LA MI RTEN PA'I YE SHES NI SPYOD PA'I GTZO BO YIN PAS, DES MTSON NAS SBYIN SOGS KYI SPYOD PA GZHAN LA SLOB PA YANG GO DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: de gsum ni sngon du nyams su len dgos par ma zad, byang sems su gyur nas kyang nyams su blang dgos pa la, gnyis la mi rten pa'i ye shes ni spyod pa'i gtso bo yin pas, des mtshon nas sbyin sogs kyi spyod pa gzhan la slob pa yang go dgos so
rows.english: Not only must one put these three into practice before becoming a bodhisattva—they must also be practiced even after a person has already become one. The primary practice within all the activities of a bodhisattva is that of the wisdom which no longer rests in the two extremes. The practice of this wisdom then represents the practice of all the other bodhisattva activities—giving & the rest. When the presentation is done as it is, it is meant to help us understand this fact.

rows.wylie: bya lta bu'i don dam pa'i sa rnams kyis, ,nam mkha' lta bu'i chos nyid la bgrod kyang, de'i bgrod tshul 'phags pas nyams su myong ba ji bzhin pa ni, 'chad pa po 'phags pas kyang brjod par mi nus na, nyan pa po rnams kyis gzigs pa ji bzhin pa mnyan par mi nus par gsungs so
rows.english: The ultimate levels are similar to the bird. They cross the expanse of the real nature of things, comparable to the sky—and yet even if the one trying to describe it is a realized being themselves, they could never describe how the crossing is accomplished, in just the same way as this is experienced by the realized being. How then could those listening to this person ever be able to hear what they are saying, in just the same way that they saw it? A brief presentation of Perfect Happiness

rows.english: We hear too from the Life of Loving One, O child of noble family, this is how it is. Imagine that the king of a land has given birth to a son or daughter. Within a short time after their birth, this child—the one who bears the name of “the king”—already outshines even all of those who are the most senior and foremost among the ministers of state, by force of the greatness of their family line.

rows.english: And when the bodhisattva cuts the flesh from their own body and gives it away to someone who asks them for it, the first words they say are “With this pain of mine”—meaning they pay no attention at all to their own pain, but rather see this same suffering they are undergoing themselves as a reason: as something whose purpose is to cut off the suffering of other living beings—those living in the hell realms, and so on. And so they immediately leap to do the deed.
