rows.wylie: de ltar bshad pa rnams la da lta nas nyams su len tshul ni, lus gzhan la ster ba dang, dga' ba skyed tshul khyad par can rnams ni mos yul du byas nas sbyong la, zang zing gi sbyin pa gzhan rnams ni yar mar gyi zhing la brten nas, chu yan chad gtong ba'i sgo nas rgyun ldan du sog pa dang, de'i tshe 'khor gsum mi dmigs par rtogs pa'i shes rab kyis zin par bya'o
rows.english: How do we put into practice, starting right now, all that we have explained here? Things like giving away our own flesh to others, and having some extraordinary feeling of joy about it, are practices that we can practice as aspirations. Things like giving material stuff away to others—to those who are both higher and lower objects of offering—are karmas that we can collect on a continual basis. As we do, we should make sure these practices are imbued with the wisdom which realizes that none of the three spheres exist.

rows.acip: 'DI LA SA DANG POR SBYIN PA LHAG PAR GSUNGS PA NI YAR LDAN DU YOD PAS, SBYIN PA LAS GZHAN PA'I PHAR PHYIN LHAG MA DGU'I NANG NAS, TSUL KHRIMS LAS BRTZAMS PA'I NYAMS LEN PHUL DU BYUNG BA'I TSOD TZAM BZOD PA SOGS LA MED PA'I PHYIR, TSUL KHRIMS LHAG PAR GSUNGS KYI, PHAR PHYIN LHAG MA RNAMS MED PA NI MIN NO,,
rows.wylie: 'di la sa dang por sbyin pa lhag par gsungs pa ni yar ldan du yod pas, sbyin pa las gzhan pa'i phar phyin lhag ma dgu'i nang nas, tshul khrims las brtsams pa'i nyams len phul du byung ba'i tshod tsam bzod pa sogs la med pa'i phyir, tshul khrims lhag par gsungs kyi, phar phyin lhag ma rnams med pa ni min no
rows.english: Now when we say that the giving of a person at the first bodhisattva level is “higher,” what we mean is that they are working their way up; and so here—from among the nine perfections other than giving—one has reached an exceptional practice of the perfection of an ethical way of life; but has not yet reached this same degree in their practice of patience & the rest. It is only in this context that we say their practice of an ethical way of life is “higher”; it is not to imply that they lack the remaining perfections.

rows.acip: DE NI, 'GRO BA NGAN PA NGAN 'GROR LHUNG BA'I NYI TSE BA'I DMYAL BA DANG, BA LANG DANG RTA DANG GLANG PO CHE DANG SPRE'U DANG, KLU LA SOGS PA DANG YI DVAGS RDZU 'PHRUL CHEN PO LA SOGS PAR SKYES PA LA, LONGS SPYOD PHUN SUM TSOGS PA SNA TSOGS PA 'BYUNG BA NI, SKYE BO TSUL KHRIMS KYI RKANG PA NYAMS PA STE BRAL BA LAS 'BYUNG NGO,,
rows.wylie: de ni, 'gro ba ngan pa ngan 'gror lhung ba'i nyi tshe ba'i dmyal ba dang, ba lang dang rta dang glang po che dang spre'u dang, klu la sogs pa dang yi dvags rdzu 'phrul chen po la sogs par skyes pa la, longs spyod phun sum tshogs pa sna tshogs pa 'byung ba ni, skye bo tshul khrims kyi rkang pa nyams pa ste bral ba las 'byung ngo
rows.english: But when this same practitioner must enjoy their excellent wealth within one of the lower rebirths—falling into the realms of misery; taking their birth for example within a hell on earth; or as a cow, or a horse, or an elephant; or as a water dragon or the like; or as a craving spirit possessed of miracle powers—then this is because “the legs of an ethical life have failed them”: meaning that they failed to follow this way of life.

rows.english: The Letter to a Friend describes the great importance of leading an ethical way of life as follows: Needless to say, You should keep an ethical Way of life, and never lose it; But neither should it ever slip, Or be compromised, or polluted. For they have stated that this way of life Provides the foundation For all good qualities you could ever have— Just as the surface of this great Earth itself Holds up all the things that be, Moving or standing still.

rows.acip: DES NA 'DI LA DBU MA SNYING PO'I 'GREL PAR, MI DGE BA STOBS BZHIS SBYANGS PA DANG, LOG LTA DANG GNOD SEMS KYIS DGE RTZA BCOM PA GNYIS KA ,SA BON NYAMS PA RKYEN DANG PHRAD KYANG MYU GU MI 'BYUNG BA LTAR, DA GDOD RKYEN DANG PHRAD KYANG 'BRAS BU 'BYIN MI NUS PAR GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: des na 'di la dbu ma snying po'i 'grel par, mi dge ba stobs bzhis sbyangs pa dang, log lta dang gnod sems kyis dge rtsa bcom pa gnyis ka ,sa bon nyams pa rkyen dang phrad kyang myu gu mi 'byung ba ltar, da gdod rkyen dang phrad kyang 'bras bu 'byin mi nus par gsungs so
rows.english: Thus it is that the commentary to The Heart of the Middle Way states that in both cases—that is, where we clean ourselves of a negative deed by using the four powers; and also where we destroy our store of good deeds by entertaining mistaken views, or malice towards another—what happens is similar to the case in nature, where even if a seed which is damaged meets with the necessary conditions, it will fail to give a sprout. That is, the deeds in both the cases lack the power to produce a result—even if they subsequently encounter the conditions normally necessary to do so.

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU, LAM GYI SKABS 'DIR YANG BLO STE SHER PHYIN GYIS KYANG, DE NYID LTA BA'I MIG NYAMS PA'I SBYIN SOGS KYI YON TAN RNAMS BLANGS PA STE YONGS SU BZUNG STE,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du, lam gyi skabs 'dir yang blo ste sher phyin gyis kyang, de nyid lta ba'i mig nyams pa'i sbyin sogs kyi yon tan rnams blangs pa ste yongs su bzung ste

rows.english: If we do give our explanations with these two negative motivations—or even with either one of them alone—then it will, as has been stated, act as an obstacle to a large amount of good karma. rows.acip: DE LAS GZHAN PA'I STONG TSUL RNAMS RANG GI NGO BOS STONG PA MIN PA'I RGYU MTSAN NI, STONG TSUL SNGA MA TSAD MAS GRUB ZIN BYED PA MA NYAMS PA'I RING LA, GRUB MTHAS GZHI DE BDEN PA'AM DE'I DON DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA'I SGRO 'DOGS SKYE MI SRID LA, PHYI MA RNAMS KYI DON TSAD MAS GRUB CING BYED PA MA NYAMS KYANG, GRUB MTHA' BDEN PA'AM BDEN PA'I DON DU SGRO 'DOGS PA MI 'GAL BA'O,,
rows.wylie: de las gzhan pa'i stong tshul rnams rang gi ngo bos stong pa min pa'i rgyu mtshan ni, stong tshul snga ma tshad mas grub zin byed pa ma nyams pa'i ring la, grub mthas gzhi de bden pa'am de'i don du yod par 'dzin pa'i sgro 'dogs skye mi srid la, phyi ma rnams kyi don tshad mas grub cing byed pa ma nyams kyang, grub mtha' bden pa'am bden pa'i don du sgro 'dogs pa mi 'gal ba'o
rows.english: And what then is the reason why we say that ways in which things could be empty that are different than these particular ways do not represent an emptiness of some kind of self-essence? Suppose that those previous ways in which we described things as being empty had already been confirmed by accurate perception; and we were all still sitting in a place where none of those confirmations had in any way declined. It would in that state be impossible for us to hold a school of thought which took those same examples of things to exist in truth; neither would it be possible for there to grow, within our minds, that form of overestimation where we held that things could exist in this same kind of truth. The idea in the latter cases here would be that a certain point had been confirmed by an accurate perception, and that the working of this perception had in no way declined; and yet this would not preclude overestimation through a learned philosophical school which said that a certain object was real; or even described what it was to be real. Normal reality cannot stand up under true analysis

rows.english: And it was similar when the high & holy Loving One, Maitreya, commented upon these matters. In Distinguishing between the Middle and the Extremes, and in the Jewel of the Sutras, and Distinguishing Things from the Very Nature of Things, he set forth the idea of a foundation consciousness, and described the position that there are no outer objects. In the Jewel of Realizations and The Higher Line though, he did not set forth any foundation consciousness; and described a position which did not deny outer objects.

rows.english: And making this kind of argument is, further, incorrect, for the following reason. Suppose that—when we have woken from a dream—we remember what we experienced in the dream. And then suppose further that our mind in the dream existed through some nature of its own. In that case, from our remembering then, things like the elephant in the dream would also become just as that state of mind dictated: they would exist as objects appearing in the outside world.

rows.acip: 'DIR 'GREL PAR RMI LAM GYI MYONG BA DRAN PA DANG, RMI LAM GYI YUL NYAMS SU MYONG BA DRAN PA GNYIS BSHAD PAS, RMI LAM GYI SKABS SU GLANG PO CHE LA SOGS PA SNANG BA NA, DPER NA BYAD BZHIN GYI GZUGS BRNYAN MTHONG BA NA DE SNANG BA'I MIG SHES KYIS BYAD BZHIN MYONG BA MIN KYANG, GZUGS BRNYAN LA LTOS PA'I YUL MYONG YOD PA BZHIN DU, RMI LAM GYI TSE YANG GLANG PO CHE MYONG BA'I YUL MYONG MED KYANG, DER SNANG BA'I YUL MYONG YOD PAS YUL DRAN ZER YANG YUL DE MYONG BA DRAN PA'O,,
rows.wylie: 'dir 'grel par rmi lam gyi myong ba dran pa dang, rmi lam gyi yul nyams su myong ba dran pa gnyis bshad pas, rmi lam gyi skabs su glang po che la sogs pa snang ba na, dper na byad bzhin gyi gzugs brnyan mthong ba na de snang ba'i mig shes kyis byad bzhin myong ba min kyang, gzugs brnyan la ltos pa'i yul myong yod pa bzhin du, rmi lam gyi tshe yang glang po che myong ba'i yul myong med kyang, der snang ba'i yul myong yod pas yul dran zer yang yul de myong ba dran pa'o
rows.english: On this point, the autocommentary describes two different types of remembering: one, a memory of the experience of the dream; and two, a memory of experiencing objects within the dream. And so suppose that an elephant or the like appears during a dream. It's like for example when we see a reflection of an object in a mirror. It's not that the visual consciousness which assumes that form is experiencing the object standing in front of the mirror; rather, it is having an experience of an object due to the reflection. The case with a dream is similar; even though at this point there is no experience of a elephant as the object, there has been an experience of an object appearing as an elephant. As such, when we say “I remember a certain object,” we are actually remembering the experience of that object.

rows.english: And if someone were to say that they could not accept the concept of apperception, we would reply that they most certainly should. rows.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, sngar nyams su ma myong ba la dran pa skye mi srid pas dran pa ni sngar gyi nyams su myong ba'i yul can yin na, khyod rang rig mi 'dod pa ltar na sngar gyi sngo 'dzin lta bu'i shes pa yang rang dus su nyams su ma myong bas, phyis kyi dran pa yod par mi 'grub bo
rows.english: And why is that? It is impossible for us to have a memory of something that we have not experienced earlier on. As such, memory is a subject state of mind which holds as its object a previous experience. According to you all though—those of you who do not accept the concept of apperception—a previous perception such as having perceived a patch of blue could not have experienced this object within its own time, which means that you cannot say that there was a later memory.

rows.english: Our own position says first of all that we do accept this description of how recollection occurs to us, as it is described in the everyday world. Nonetheless, what we say is that for a recollection to occur in the way it's described here, it is not something that could have occurred through the power of some kind of apperception, where the previous experience of the object somehow knew itself by itself. Rather, what happens is that there has been the discernment of an object by a previous experience, and then we recollect that; and so it is due to the single object discerned that there can arise in John a recollection where he says to himself, “I saw this previously as well.”

rows.wylie: gal te bdag med mthong ba'i dus su rtag pa'i bdag nang gi byed pa'i skyes bu spong ba ste med par mthong ba yin na ni, de ltar 'dod pa de'i tshe skabs gzhan du bdag gi sgra'i don gzhan la drang du mi rung ba de'i phyir, khyod kyi phung po dang sems bdag tu mi 'gyur la, de lta na ni rang phyogs nyams par 'gyur ro
rows.english: Suppose then that it is the case that—when we perceive that there is no self—we eliminate the idea of an inner being which was some kind of unchanging self. As such, then, your parts to the person, and your mind, could never be the self; and in such manner, your own position would be undermined.

rows.wylie: pa tshab kyi 'gyur gyi dpe mang po las, byung yang rung ma byung yang rung ste, gang gi don du zhes 'byung yang, nag tsho'i 'gyur las, ma byung yang rung don dam pa ni nyams pa med pa yin pas zhes 'byung ba ni, sngar 'grel par mdo drangs pa las, ma byung yang rung chos rnams kyi chos nyid 'di ni gnas pa nyid do, zhes 'byung ba dang mthun pas legs pa yin no
rows.english: Many of the manuscripts of Patsab's translation read: “For whatever the reason, whether it is the case that it has occurred, or has not occurred.” Naktso's translation reads, “For the reason that the ultimate never declines, even if it were something that never came about.” This latter version accords with what we see in the autocommentary, where it quotes the sutra: “Even if it were something that never came about, the real nature of things is quite certainly something that stays.” As such, we can say that this version is preferred.

rows.acip: DE LTAR SLOB DPON 'PHAGS PAS RANG BZHIN ZHAL GYIS BZHES PAR BSTAN PA 'DIS, CHOS DBYINGS BSTOD PA LAS, ,STONG PA NYID NI STON PA'I MDO, ,RGYAL BAS JI SNYED GSUNGS PA KUN, ,DE DAG KUN GYIS NYON MONGS LDOG ,KHAMS 'DI NYAMS PAR BYED MA YIN,

rows.english: Once we understand through this presentation that the master, The Arya, accepts the idea of a nature to things, we can also go on to understand the following lines from A Praise of the Realm of Reality— All of the various sutras Ever spoken by the Victors That presented the idea Of emptiness Were meant to stop The negative emotions; But they do nothing to diminish This basic nature to things.

rows.acip: ZHES STONG NYID STON PA'I MDO SDES BDEN 'DZIN GYI NYON MONGS PA'I DMIGS GTAD 'JIG PA YIN GYI, DE'I DMIGS GTAD BKAG PA'I STONG PA DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA'I KHAMS NYAMS PA STE MED PAR STON PA MIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PA YANG SHES PAR BYA'O,,

rows.english: What this is saying is that the group of sutras that presents the idea of emptiness functions to destroy the point of view of our tendency to see things as real, a view involved with the negative emotions. rows.acip: 'GRO BA RNAMS LA PHAN PA DANG BDE BA NYE BAR SGRUB PA NI, BYAMS PA CHEN PO ZHES BYA BA'I MTSAN NYID DANG, SDUG BSNGAL CAN GYI SEMS CAN RNAMS YONGS SU SKYOB PA NI, THUGS RJE CHEN PO'I MTSAN NYID DO,,

rows.english: Just so, may every one of the uncountably many—the unimaginably many—living beings in the universe, when they have heard my name, then by my mystical power, take upon themselves the three different types of vows. May they never fail in keeping to their code of ethics, and may they never degenerate to a lower ethical code. May no one, anywhere, ever drop to the three lower realms. Medicine Buddha's sixth prayer, for perfect health in the universe Shashtham

We have lived this way for time with no beginning, and yet we have never gotten any meaning out of it; the time has slipped away from us useless, senseless, empty. rows.acip: DE LTAR BSHES GNYEN BSTEN TSUL 'DI BZANG PO BYUNG NA TSE RABS THAMS CAD DU BLA, MAS RJES SU 'DZIN PA DANG DA RES KYI LUS RTEN 'DI ANG KI DANG POR BRTZIS TE 'DI NAS BZUNG DAL BRGYAD 'BYOR BCU TSANG BA'I MI'I RTEN BZANG BAR MA CHAD PAR THOB NAS DAL 'BYOR GYI ANG KI MA 'KHRUGS PAR CHOS NYAMS SU BLANGS TE SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG SGRUB THUB PA 'ONG
rows.wylie: de ltar bshes gnyen bsten tshul 'di bzang po byung na tshe rabs thams cad du bla, mas rjes su 'dzin pa dang da res kyi lus rten 'di ang ki dang por brtsis te 'di nas bzung dal brgyad 'byor bcu tshang ba'i mi'i rten bzang bar ma chad par thob nas dal 'byor gyi ang ki ma 'khrugs par chos nyams su blangs te sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang sgrub thub pa 'ong
rows.english: If our service of our Lama is good, then in all our future lives we will find ourselves taken under the care of Lamas. Then too we can count the life we have found now as the first in a long and unbroken series of lives in which we enjoy each of the eight spiritual leisures, and the ten fortunes. And there will never again be any mistake in this particular arithmetic: we will always enjoy the exact number of circumstances needed to follow our practice of the Dharma, and so finally reach the state of perfect enlightenment.

rows.acip: DES KYANG MI CHOG PA RGYAL MCHOG BSKAL BZANG RGYA MTSOS, KHAMS GSUM 'KHOR BA ZHES GRAGS LCAGS SREG GI KHANG PA PHYOGS BCU GANG DU PHYIN KYANG SDUG BSNGAL GYIS BSREG PA'I SNYING LA GZAN KYANG RANG GI SNANG TSUL DU 'DUG PA GNAS NGAN 'DI 'DRAR 'KHYAMS PA'I SNANG TSUL 'DI SKYO BA
rows.wylie: des kyang mi chog pa rgyal mchog bskal bzang rgya mtshos, khams gsum 'khor ba zhes grags lcags sreg gi khang pa phyogs bcu gang du phyin kyang sdug bsngal gyis bsreg pa'i snying la gzan kyang rang gi snang tshul du 'dug pa gnas ngan 'di 'drar 'khyams pa'i snang tshul 'di skyo ba
rows.english: This in itself though is not enough, as expressed in the following words of Kelsang Gyatso, the highest of all the Victors: This thing they call The three realms of cyclic life Is a house of red-hot steel; Wherever you go In any of the ten directions, The suffering will burn you. You wish so badly That it weren't happening, But this is its very nature. How pitiful our life, To wander aimlessly In such a house of horrors.

rows.english: This is what you are requesting, said our Lama, from your Lama in this verse. You are asking that he or she help you gain the strength to keep your vows perfectly; that you learn to think of the vows contained within your being as the true representative of the Buddha himself, inside you; that you love and cherish your vows, and always hope to defend them. You are asking, he said, to be granted the ability to follow the way of this and the other extraordinary trainings, exactly as they were meant to be. OPEN STEPS FOR THOSE OF GREATER CAPACITY VII. Developing the Wish for Enlightenment

rows.english: In short, if it comes down to choosing between giving up your life, and letting this morality degenerate, you had surely better choose the first. The one thing here in this birth that you cherish above all else is your own life. What you are requesting fromyour Lama is that he or she grant you the power to always keep your vows and pledges properly; that you reach a point where you cherish these commitments infinitely more than your own precious life. rows.english: In the stage of creation we transformall these seemingly ordinary things and events; we turn theminto the three bodies of a victorious Buddha. We take whatever presents itself to us: all that appears to our eyes, all that reaches our ears, and all that comes in our thoughts, and we make it show itself as total and absolute purity, as a galaxy of perfection, as great celestial mansions, as holy angels, as a magical dance put on by our Lamas.

rows.acip: DE YANG LAM LA PHYIN CI MA LOG PA DANG LAM GOL BA DANG LAM NOR BAR SHOR BA, SOGS BZANG NGAN SNA TSOGS YOD CING RANG CAG GIS NYAMS SU BLANG BYA'I LAM DE LAM BZANG PO MA NOR MA 'KHRUL BA ZHIG LA MA ZHUGS NA 'KHRUL BA'I LAM PHYIN CI LOG CIG LA LO STONG DU SGRUB PA BYAS KYANG 'BRAS BU BZANG PO MA 'KHRUL BA 'BYUNG BA GTAN NAS MI SRID LA
rows.wylie: de yang lam la phyin ci ma log pa dang lam gol ba dang lam nor bar shor ba, sogs bzang ngan sna tshogs yod cing rang cag gis nyams su blang bya'i lam de lam bzang po ma nor ma 'khrul ba zhig la ma zhugs na 'khrul ba'i lam phyin ci log cig la lo stong du sgrub pa byas kyang 'bras bu bzang po ma 'khrul ba 'byung ba gtan nas mi srid la
rows.english: So there are these different sorts of spiritual paths, of widely varying quality: some are totally correct, some are totally wrong, some slide off from right to wrong, and on and on. You and I have access to a path which is pure, and unmistaken, and free of any error. We can either enter it now or go off on some wrong road that goes astray. If this second is our choice then we can try to follow such a way for a thousand years, but it is an absolute impossibility that we will derive fromit any good or certain result.

rows.english: Contemplation Two The first point, [how to undertake the actualpractice,] has two sections: meditating on love, and meditating on compassion. The first is described in the lines that talk about "practicing giving and taking alternately"—which is to say, we should meditate upon love by giving away our bodies, our possessions, and our stores of good karma to other people. Our joy in doing so will be much more powerful if first of all we think carefully upon the benefits of love, and so here is a description of these benefits. rows.wylie: zhes gsungs nges na rang nyid kyi, lus dang longs spyod dge rtsa rnams sems can kun la legs btang bas de dag phan bde ma lus dang ldan par gyur cig snyam pa yi byams pa chen po bsgom par bya
rows.english: Once you've come to see the truth of all these words, then go And give away for every living being your very body, All of your possessions, and what virtue you may have; Go and meditate upon the state of greatest love, On thoughts wherein you wish that all of them may always have Every kind of happiness and help that there could be. Contemplation Four: The original text on the practice of giving and taking, from the Offering to Lamas (Lama Chupa) of the First Panchen Lama Perhaps the most famous source for the practice of giving and taking as it is currently followed is the Offering to Lamas (Lama Chupa) of the First Panchen Lama. There are two important verses for the practice; we present them here in bold with some of the other verses near them, in order to show the context. The first of the two verses is considered so vital that in modern Tibetan monasteries it is repeated three times whenever the Offering is recited in the assembly of monks.

rows.english: Here is the fifth point, which is using this practice [that is, exchanging oneself and others] as a basis for the meditation on giving and taking. We practice taking by concentrating on the object of our compassion, and we practice giving by concentrating on the object of our love. Remember the root text [of the Mental Training in Seven Points], where it says, "Alternate the two, of giving and taking." The point is that this practice of giving and taking brings the attitude of exchanging self and others to new heights.

rows.english: Contemplation Six If you plan to make the meditation on giving and taking the central point of your practice, you can follow the custom of the venerable Ngawang Dorje. First go through the process of going for refuge and bringing up the Wish for enlightenment. After that, do the meditation on giving and taking. Next make the prayer that your meditation actually come true, by the power of truth, with the lines that include, "By the pureness of the power of my intentions..." [The full prayer here reads: By the pureness of the power of my intentions, By the power of the blessings of Those Gone Thus, By the powers of the realm of emptiness, May all the goals that I may have, And all my wishes, whatever they be, Come true, with perfect ease.] After this, bring up in your mind the clear conviction that no object in the universe has any nature of its own: not the object being meditated upon, nor the person meditating upon it, nor anything else at all. And then [continue with certain special practices, followed by a final dedication and prayer]. rows.acip: RLUNG LA BSKYON TSUL NI GZHAN SNGAR DANG 'DRA BA LA RANG GI SNA G.YSA NAS RLUNG PHYIR 'BUD, PA DANG MNYAM DU RANG GI BDE DGE RNAMS 'OD DKAR PO'I RNAM PAR SONG BA SEMS CAN RNAMS KYI SNA G.YON NAS ZHUGS TE BDE BA DANG LDAN PAR BSAM LA BYAMS PA DANG YANG SEMS CAN THAMS CAD 'KHOR BA DANG NGAN SONG GI SDUG BSNGAL GYIS MNAR TSUL BSAM LA DE LTA BU'I SDUG BSNGAL DANG SDIG PA RNAMS 'OD NAG PO'I RNAM PAR SEMS CAN RNAMS KYI SNA G.YSA NAS THON RLUNG NANG DU RNGUB PA DANG MNYAM DU RANG GI SNA G.YON NAS ZHUGS TE SNYING GA'I BDAG 'DZIN BCOM PAR BSAM LA SNYING RJE BSGOM
rows.wylie: rlung la bskyon tshul ni gzhan sngar dang 'dra ba la rang gi sna g.ysa nas rlung phyir 'bud, pa dang mnyam du rang gi bde dge rnams 'od dkar po'i rnam par song ba sems can rnams kyi sna g.yon nas zhugs te bde ba dang ldan par bsam la byams pa dang yang sems can thams cad 'khor ba dang ngan song gi sdug bsngal gyis mnar tshul bsam la de lta bu'i sdug bsngal dang sdig pa rnams 'od nag po'i rnam par sems can rnams kyi sna g.ysa nas thon rlung nang du rngub pa dang mnyam du rang gi sna g.yon nas zhugs te snying ga'i bdag 'dzin bcom par bsam la snying rje bsgom
rows.english: As for how to let this meditation "ride on the wind," follow first the steps we mentioned earlier [in the explanation of the first reference, found above]. Then picture all your own happiness and good deeds in the form of white light. Send it out together with your breath when you exhale, from your right nostril, to every living being. See it entering their left nostrils, and think to yourself that they are now filled with happiness. Meditate thus upon love. Contemplate next upon how all these living beings are tormented by the sufferings of cyclic life, and the three lower realms. Picture their suffering, and all their bad deeds, as black light, and see it issuing out of their right nostrils. When you inhale then, see this blackness entering into you together with the air, through your left nostril—and imagine that it has destroyed, within your heart, the tendency to grasp to things as having some self-nature. Meditate thus on compassion.

rows.english: Now I'll put it all together for you; See Your breath as it passes out, Give With it Dharma: happiness, good, To Every mother in six realms. Then When you breathe in take from every Being All their bad deeds and their pain. Go Thus deep, give and also take, Lose Your heart to this supreme Wish. When And wherever you may be Run To your Lama and Three Jewels. Live In this way, both give and take; Luck Amazing that I found this Dharma. Contemplation Eight Grant Me your blessing holy Jewels, Let Every Dharma wish come true. The first Changkya Rinpoche describes the role of breath in the meditation of giving and taking as well in a work entitled, "Entertainment for those of the Higher Way," being an Explanation of the Letter of Instruction known as the "Eight Verses," a Work of Advice on Practicing the Wish for Enlightenment composed by the Great Bodhisattva, Dorje Senge of Langri Tang:

rows.english: When you reach the four lines with the part about "giving and taking that ride upon the wind," try first to bring up in your heart a motivation which includes thoughts of love, compassion, and personal responsibility. Then breath out from your right nostril; while the breath goes out, imagine all your happiness and goodness going with it—that is, give these things to all living beings, your mothers, and see them grow within their minds.

rows.english: Think about the part that mentions, "I will ignore instead myself, and cherish all others; I will take upon myself all the sufferings and negative actions of others." At this point you should meditate on compassion, thinking about how others are tormented by suffering. Now think about the part where the text mentions, "By my act of giving away all my happiness and good deeds." Here you should contemplate how deprived others are of any happiness, and thus meditate on love. If at the beginning you find these attitudes difficult to bring up in your heart, then Contemplation Nine begin by taking on first the suffering that you yourself will be experiencing by this same afternoon. Then take on the suffering you will have tomorrow, and then next month, and next year, and so on. So in stages you can practice giving and taking.

rows.english: Here is how to do the practice of giving, by focusing upon the category of love. Remember the text that says, In order to accomplish the goals of every living being, Turn your body into the form of a wish-fulfilling jewel. Sutras such as Stalks in Array and the Victory Banner of Diamond also state that we should learn to give away our body and our possessions. Here you turn your body into anything and everything that someone might want to have, and then send it out to the world, and to the people living in the world.

rows.english: Do the same with two different kinds of materialpossessions: you can only give away those of your current life and your future lives; the ones from your past lives cannot now be given away. When you do the giving practice, think of all living beings as we talked about before. Think of how they live, bereft of any happiness, and concentrate mainly on developing feelings of love. You must try to make this single section of the mental training tradition the very heart of your practice. rows.english: Even if you do undertake the contemplation this way, the fact is that you will find yourself unable to take away anything directly. You will though finish amassing a great amount of virtuous karma, in a very effective way; and if you really get used to the practice then you will find yourself later actually able to take something. This is similar, said our Lama, to the story of the dedicated practitioner of the meditation of Loving One.

rows.english: The Compendium of All the Trainings [by Master Shantideva] states the following: There are certain lines in the Holy Sutra of Golden Light that teach us how to meditate upon love and compassion. We should contemplate upon them with our every thought, and in the end we should even recite them in our words, on a constant basis. The lines go like this: May the sound of the great drum of the Holy Golden Light Fly to all three realms of a thousand thousands of a thousand worlds And put to an end there all pain: the pain of the lower realms, The pain of the Lord of Death, and the pain of poverty. rows.english: The Holy Ones have stated that—if you are able to follow these practices and work on problems while they are still in their lesser stages—then you will be able to remove the karma that would have brought you more serious problems. I therefore ask that you live your lives this way. This brief explanation has been put down on paper by the glorious Lobsang Drakpa [Je Tsongkapa] in response to a request received, through other parties, from the embodiment of all scripture and reasoning: Rinchen Samdrup, the Teacher from Nyel. The eminent Pabongka Rinpoche, in his Gift of Liberation, further links the concept of giving and taking with that of transforming problems into siritual opportunities:

The line goes: You are able to stay in a state of happiness alone, in a constant stream. rows.english: Here is the meaning of the line "Training yourself in practice is easy." You might think to yourself something like "Taking on all the pain that others have, and giving them all my happiness and goodness, seems like something that would be very hard to do." But start doing it now, if only in your imagination. rows.english: Now there are a great many ways of teaching those advices for training oneself in the greater way—the lojong, or instructions for developing the good heart. In the tradition of the spiritual friend, the geshe, Chekawa, these instructions are organized into a seven-part practice. These seven are: 1) Instructions on the foundation Dharma, the preliminary practices; 2) The actual practice for developing the Wish for Enlightenment; 3) Learning to use problems as a path to Enlightenment; 4) A summary of an entire lifetime's practice; 5) The point at which one can say that he or she has successfully developed the good heart; 6) Pledges to keep for developing the good heart; and 7) Certain advices on developing the good heart. rows.english: Keep to the three laws. Change your mind and stay the same. Speak not of what was broken. Never worry about what they're doing. Rid yourself of the biggest affliction first. Never hope for any reward. Stop eating poison food. Don't let the stream flow smooth. Forget repaying criticism. Give up laying ambushes. No going for the jugular. Load your own truck, no passing the buck. Don't get fixed on speed. Don't feed the wrong face. Don't turn the sweet angel to a devil. Don't look for crap to make yourself happy. rows.english: This beingthe case, you should never let yourself think, “This is one of those practices meant for people who have nothing more profound to meditate upon.” And you should never let yourself think that, “It is admittedly something we should meditate upon, but only at the beginning of our practice, and only for a bit at that; it's not somethingthat warrants a continual effort to put into practice.” Rather you should try to develop a true understanding, from the depths of your heart, where you realize that this is a meditation which you need at the start, at the end, and all throughout the path. rows.english: The subjects of how to serve a spiritual guide, of the spiritual fortune and leisure of this life, and of our impermanence are found throughout the supreme form of speech, the word of the Buddha, and the commentaries upon it. rows.english: Here is the first point, which describes one of the feature of livingin isolation: that the place and so on are so perfectly excellent. "If I go into isolation," you may ask, "where should it be?" Think of a wheel-empowered emperor, who has no one at all to compete with him, and who revels in the objects of the senses at his own complete leisure. Just like this emperor do we live, deep within the woods of peacefulness, at rest from all the various distractions, in a place completely emptied of both any outer conflict and any kind of mental affliction—completely free of any of the objects that could trigger within us emotions such as likingor dislikinganother person. We live doing as we please under some very wide, flat rock as a roof, which is just like a mansion for us. The place is cool, made cool by the touch of sweet sandalwood scent smeared all over—the soft moonlight of the presence of the holy beings who have stayed there in the past. Here the forest is silent, with no kinds of sound to clash with our thoughts, and peaceful with the soft velvet breezes that flow past to grace the ground of our meditation. rows.wylie: bdag gzhan gyi bde sdug la dmigs nas 'dor len mtshungs par byed rigs par thal, gang gi tshe bdag dang gzhan gnyis ka bde ba 'dod du mtshungs pa la bdag dang gang zag gzhan khyad par ci yod na ci yang med pa'i phyir rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na bdag gcig bu, bde bar brtson par byed cing gzhan gyi bde ba la mi brtson pa mi rigs so gang gi tshe, bdag dang gzhan gnyis ka sdug bsngal mi 'dod par mtshungs pa la bdag dang gzhan khyad par ci yod na ste ci yang med pa'i phyir ro rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir gzhan gyi bde ba bsrung ba min par bdag gi bde ba ched du bsgrub cing mi nyams par srung bar byed gnyis ka mtshungs par bsgrub rigs so
rows.english: It is right that I should act exactly the same towards the happiness and sufferings of others as I do towards those of my own, for the following reasons. Given the fact that both myself and others are exactly the same in how we want happiness, what difference then could there ever be between us—between myself and others? There is no difference at all. And for what reason then do I work only for happiness for myself—what is my justification? Why do I not work the same for the happiness of others? What I'm doingnow is not right. Given the fact that both myself and others are exactly the same in how we do not want any pain, what difference could there ever be between us, between myself and others? There is no difference at all. And for what reason then do I fail to protect the happiness of all others, and concentrate instead on reaching my own happiness, and protectingit from ever beinglost? The two happiness are exactly the same, and it is right for me to work to achieve them both. The last section is from the Overview of the Middle Way, composed by Master Kedrup Tenpa Dargye (1493-1568).

rows.english: Instances in which you have committed some transgression of your vows, at whichever level of vows you may have, should be repaired according to the methods prescribed for those particular vows. For repairing the damage caused by other kinds of bad deeds you should utilize the four powers. As the Sutra on the Four Practices states, O Loving One, if a great bodhisattva keeps four practices, then he or she can never be overwhelmed by bad deeds that they have both committed and collected. And what are these four practices? They are the activity of destruction, and the activity of an antidote, and the power of restoring, and the power of the The expression "committed and collected" refers to actions whose karmic results are "certain to be experienced." If even these types of karmic results can be overcome by the four practices, then there is no need to mention those which are not certain to be experienced. An Original Source for the Principle that Old Karma Can be Removed The general principle that old karma can be removed from our mind streams is clearly stated in a number of important works by Lord Buddha himself. One of the most famous of these is a part from the famous Diamond-Cutter Sutra, which appears in the following selection in bold lettering. The commentary that follows the sutra is the only known native Tibetan explanation of the work, and was composed by Chone Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) of the incomparable Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery. Chone Lama skillfully weaves the root text into his explanation, and these words have also been printed in bold. He moreover quotes several other important original sources to demonstrate that old karma can be removed.

rows.english: In this same vein, The Biography of Loving One says: It's like this, o child of noble family. Think of a single butter lamp; you can carry it into any cottage or house at all and it will clear away the dark and light up the place, the minute you step in, even if the dark has been accumulating there for the last thousand years. Now think of the Wish to reach total omniscience, just a single lamp of the Wish. Suppose you stick it for a moment into the mind of any particular living being smothered in the darkness of ignorance. In the very next moment, all the darkness of the spiritual obstacles created by karma and the mental afflictions—darkness that has been collecting there for so many millions of eons that words could not express their number—is cleared away; and the light of wisdom is born in its fullness.

rows.english: On this subject, let me give you a description of the environmental results of the ten non-virtuous deeds. If you have killed other beings, then you live in a world where food and medicine have very little potency. If you have stolen other people's things, then the crops in your land are deficient, and fail to ripen fully. If you have committed sexual misconduct, then the place where you live has areas like cesspools, places filled with filth and putrid smells.

rows.english: Suppose though there comes a point that a particular virtuous karma has been ruined because one has developed wrong views, or thoughts of malice; or else that the power of a particular non-virtuous karma has been ruined by applying an antidote, such as repudiating the act; or deciding to restrain oneself; or by confessing what's been done. rows.english: This way of teaching things is a sharp knife to the minds of the twiceborn whose eyes Of ascertainment were ruined when the venom of jealousy splashed into them. It is though ultimate instruction that pours the honey of fine explanation into The mouths of the mass of sixlegs who have clear and unbiased minds. ["Twiceborn" refers to (among other things) birds, who have been born once when their egg came out of their mother and once when they emerged from the egg. "Sixlegs" means "bees." The point of this classical poetry seems to be that intelligent people, like bees, are able to thread around the thorns on a flower and get the nectar that clumsy birds (jealous, competitive scholars) are unable to extract. Or perhaps the "sharp knife" is the sting of a snake, as snakes traditionally fight the kings of all birds—the garudas. rows.english: There is furthermore some additional text at this point which differentiates it from the preceding, similar passage. Lord Buddha says, “Think further, o Subhuti, of any son or daughter of noble family who holds or carries or does any of the other actions mentioned with this sutra; who puts it into practice. Living beings like this may well suffer from a whole variety of illnesses; they may come to live in conflict, they may be criticized, they may be imprisoned or beaten and others of the like. It is possible that they might experience, in fact, intense suffering—but this will be no great problem for them.

rows.acip: 'DI LTA BU ZHIG SNGAR YANG BYUNG MOD, DE NI MOS SPYOD KYI SA NAS NYAMS SU LEN PA'I DBANG DU MDZAD CING, 'DIR NI LHAG BSAM DAG PA 'PHAGS PA'I SA NAS NYAMS SU LEN PA'I DBANG DU MDZAD CES KA MA LA SH'I LAS GSUNG NGO,,
rows.wylie: 'di lta bu zhig sngar yang byung mod, de ni mos spyod kyi sa nas nyams su len pa'i dbang du mdzad cing, 'dir ni lhag bsam dag pa 'phags pa'i sa nas nyams su len pa'i dbang du mdzad ces ka ma la shI las gsung ngo
rows.english: Master Kamalashila explains that—although a section like this has admittedly already occurred earlier on in the sutra—that earlier section was spoken with reference to our practice at the point where we are still practicing at the levels where our grasp of emptiness is largely based on belief. The present section then is meant to refer to the point where we are practicing at the levels where our sense of personal responsibility is “pure”—at levels where we are already a realized being. How to deny the Buddha

rows.english: And what the sutra is saying next is that this body of reality is beyond the things they know if one is holding things in the way we described it above—since people who do hold things this way will never be able to know these things. rows.wylie: gang la na, phyogs re tsam ma yin par rab 'byams gsung rab kun la lta ba'i mig tu gyur cing, skal ba bzang por gyur pa'i gdul bya thar par bgrod pa'i 'jug ngogs te lam mchog tu gyur pa'i skyes bu gsum gyi lam gyi rim pa 'di nyid, brtse ba'i thugs kyis bskyod pa ste drangs pa'i thabs mkhas kyi mdzad pa yis gdul bya la gsal bar mdzad pa'i bshes gnyen rnams la'o
rows.english: And who is it that we bow down to in this verse? It is to all of those spiritual friends who utilize a variety of skillful means to clarify these teachings to their disciples, "moved by"-compelled by-their heart's love. And what are those teachings? They are these very steps on the path, which themselves constitute the very highest of all paths for individuals of three different capacities. These steps serve as eyes to view the content of all-and not just individual pieces-of the myriad forms of high teachings. And they serve as well as an entry point for disciples of sufficient goodness to make the journey to freedom.

rows.english: The second kind of greatness here is that the steps make it possible for each & every one of the classic teachings of the Buddha to strike us as advice meant for each of us, personally. rows.wylie: gsung rab dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa'i brjod bya mtha' dag nyams su len gyi go rim dang mthun par bshes gnyen bsten tshul nas zhi lhag gi bar bsdus nas dpyad sgom dang 'dzeg sgom ci rigs kyi sgo nas nyams su len tshul shes par 'gyur bas na, gsung rab thams cad gdams par 'char ba'i che ba dang
rows.english: Which is to say, we come to see how the entire content of the high speech of the Enlightened Ones, along with the commentaries which clarify its intent, are completely consistent with the order of the steps that we will need to take in our own personal practice. And we see how this practice will involve either analytical meditation or fixed meditation-whichever the case may be-upon the steps in this grand summary, which stretches from how to study with a spiritual friend, on up to the final topics of meditative quietude combined with special insight.

rows.english: The third sort of greatness then is that the steps permit us to realize, with perfect ease, the true intent of the Victors. rows.english: As such-that is, for the reason that these steps do indeed possess the types of greatness that we have just described-where could we ever find a person with intelligence whose heart wasn't completely stolen away by them? rows.english: That state of mind where we aspire to higher rebirths by means of giving up bad deeds, and accomplishing good deeds, constitutes the path which is shared with people of lesser capacity. And that state of mind where we aspire to freedom because we want to be liberated from the cycle of pain constitutes the path which is shared with people of medium capacity. Both of these states of mind are present in the mind stream of a bodhisattva; and both of them must be practiced by a bodhisattva.

rows.acip: LTA BA RGYA'I MKHAN PO LTAR 'THAD NA NYAMS LEN YANG DE KHO NA LTAR 'GYUR DGOS TE, MTSAN 'DZIN RNAM PA KUN TU DGAG PA RIGS KYI SO SO SKYE BOS KYANG MTSAN 'DZIN PA NYAMS LEN GYI MTHIL DU BYED PA NI RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MI RIGS SO,,
rows.wylie: lta ba rgya'i mkhan po ltar 'thad na nyams len yang de kho na ltar 'gyur dgos te, mtshan 'dzin rnam pa kun tu dgag pa rigs kyi so so skye bos kyang mtshan 'dzin pa nyams len gyi mthil du byed pa ni rnam pa thams cad du mi rigs so
rows.english: If the views of this master were correct, then a practice associated with the views would have to follow, accordingly. In this case, it would be the right thing to do to attempt to put a stop to any & all perceptions where we hold that the characteristics of things belong to those things. And in that case it would be completely wrong for normal people to utilize such perceptions at the very core of their practice.

rows.wylie: tshig gsal gyi stong thun du 'dir skye ba bkag pa bsgrub bya'i chos su 'dod pa'i tshe de kho nar rten chos can phyin ci log tsam gyi bdag gi dngos po rnyed pa nyams par 'gyur bar rtog ge pa 'dis rang nyid kyis khas blangs pa yin no zhes gsungs so
rows.english: He expresses this point in his interlude on emptiness known as A Clarification of the Verses: When we take the position here that denying the growth of things is the quality we seek to prove, then this logician has-on his own accord-accepted precisely, with nothing more than this, that the idea that the basis of the quality (the subject under consideration) can be perceived to be a self-existing entity, and thus simply mistaken, has been compromised.

rows.acip: THEG CHEN MTHONG SPANGS KYIS BSDUS PA'I SHES SGRIB DE DAG CHOS KYI GNAS LUGS MNGON SUM GYIS GSAR DU RTOGS TZAM GYIS SPONG NGAM, 'ON TE GOMS PAR BYED DGOS PHYI MA MI RIGS TE, SGOM SPANGS SU 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR, DANG PO LTAR NA, NYAN THOS 'PHAGS PAS MA SPANGS PA NYAMS SO,,
rows.wylie: theg chen mthong spangs kyis bsdus pa'i shes sgrib de dag chos kyi gnas lugs mngon sum gyis gsar du rtogs tsam gyis spong ngam, 'on te goms par byed dgos phyi ma mi rigs te, sgom spangs su 'gyur ba'i phyir, dang po ltar na, nyan thos 'phags pas ma spangs pa nyams so
rows.english: That is, a question arises of whether obstacles to knowledge taken in by problems eliminated, on the greater way, by the path of seeing are eliminated simply through the direct perception of the way that things exist; or, rather, is a process required here where we habituate ourselves to the realization. The latter position would though have to be mistaken, since these obstacles would then have to be problems eliminated by the path of habituation. And the former position would call into question the position that realized beings on the listener track had not eliminated the obstacles. A summary on impossible nirvana

rows.acip: BYAMS CHOS RJES 'BRANGS DANG BCAS PA'I GZHUNG GANG DU YANG GROL BA TZAM DANG THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA'I LAM GNYIS SU BYAS PA'I GROL LAM DU MI RTAG SOGS RNAM PA BCU DRUG 'BA' ZHIG BSTAN GYI, RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS DGOS PA GANG YANG MA BSTAN PA'I PHYIR DANG,
rows.wylie: byams chos rjes 'brangs dang bcas pa'i gzhung gang du yang grol ba tsam dang thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam gnyis su byas pa'i grol lam du mi rtag sogs rnam pa bcu drug 'ba' zhig bstan gyi, rang bzhin med par rtogs dgos pa gang yang ma bstan pa'i phyir dang
rows.english: And that's because-in the major classics of the Five Books of Maitreya, and in the works that follow them-the sixteen aspects of impermanence and so on are taught only with the path of liberation, where a division is made between the two paths of simple liberation and omniscience. There is no indication there at all that one must realize how nothing has any nature of its own.

rows.english: Let's consider all these things that are impermanent, and things which deceive us. Those beings who are wise ones, who have come to the end of everything they ever needed to accomplish-which is to say, those realized beings-see, directly, that these things are devoid of each & every kind of self-nature. And that's because they see, directly, that these things are hollow, similar to a piece of straw, feeble: empty of any nature where things or the person are themselves. How Nagarjuna sees things

rows.english: Well then I disagree to the second part of your reason. I disagree that-relative to the person to whom the argument is being presented-there is no need to add the expression "in an ultimate sense." And yet even in this second context there is no need for it; Because in a case where the opponent is a follower of a non-Buddhist school and has failed even to grasp the concept of two realities-deceptive & ultimate-it is appropriate to make our refutation from the point of view of both of those realities at once.

rows.english: But that's not the way it is; and here's why. Suppose we have a case where we've accepted-as the quality we are trying to prove about a particular subject that we have under consideration-the absence of the starting of a thing. We entirely accept that, with nothing more than that, the tendency of a state of mind which is nothing but mistaken to see some self-nature in the subject under consideration-that which acts as the basis of this quality-is undermined.

rows.english: person to feel a Wish for enlightenment which is complete in every necessary characteristic, it is not sufficient simply to intend to lead all other living beings to the state of Buddhahood. Rather, you must have the desire that you yourself reach this state as well. This is exactly why Maitreya stated that "The Wish for enlightenment consists of the intention to reach total enlightenment for the sake of others."[46] The part about "the sake of others" is meant to indicate that you must intend to lead other beings to nirvana, whereas the part about the "intention to reach total enlightenment" means that you must intend to reach perfect Buddhahood yourself.

rows.acip: DE LTAR SANGS RGYAS PA DANG CHOS BSTAN PA SOGS CHOS THAMS CAD DON DAM PAR MED KYANG THA SNYAD DU YOD PAS SBYIN PA BYIN PA LAS BSOD NAMS CHEN PO 'BYUNG MOD, DE LAS KYANG CHOS 'DI LA THOS BSAM SGOM PA'I NYAMS LEN BYAS PA'I BSOD NAMS LHAG PAR CHE'O ZHES STON PA NI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA KHYOD 'DI JI SNYAM DU SEMS, RIGS KYI BU DANG BU MO GANG LA LA ZHIG GIS,

rows.english: With this next section of the sutra, Lord Buddha wishes to demonstrate a certain fact. In the sections above we have spoken about the act of becoming enlightened, and of teaching the Dharma, and so on. Neither these, nor any other object in the universe, exists ultimately. Nonetheless, they do exist nominally. As such, one would have to admit that anyone who performs an act of giving does acquire great merit thereby. Yet anyone who carries out the process of learning, or contemplating, or meditating upon this teaching acquires infinitely greater merit. To convey this point, the Conqueror asks Subhuti the question beginning with "What do you think? Suppose some son or daughter of noble family were to take this great world system, a system with a thousand of a thousand of a thousand planets..."

rows.english: reason for this is as follows. The act of giving someone the Dharma is of much more benefit that the act of giving material things. Not only that, but the enlightenment of the totally enlightened Buddhas comes from—is achieved through—the perfection of wisdom: the realization of emptiness which forms the subject matter of this text. It is from putting this into practice as well that the Buddhas, the Conquerors, are born.

rows.english: And so let's consider further, the Buddha is saying, anyone who "takes up" or commits this sutra to memory, or even just holds the book in their hands, or goes on to read it, or further comprehends its meaning—that is, who knows it; and finally thinks to put it into practice properly in their personal life. rows.english: There is furthermore some additional text at this point which differentiates it from the preceding, similar passage. Lord Buddha says, "Think further, o Subhuti, of any son or daughter of noble family who holds or carries or does any of the other actions mentioned with this sutra; who puts it into practice. Living beings like this may well suffer from a whole variety of illnesses; they may come to live in conflict, they may be criticized, they may be imprisoned or beaten and others of the like. It is possible that they might experience, in fact, intense suffering—but this will be no great problem for them.

rows.english: We see for example the single object of a horse referred to in a variety of words from different languages—languages like Sanskrit or Chinese, or Tibetan or Mongolian. rows.english: Some people say that, as a preliminary to the practice of the stage of completion, the disciple have gained the three kinds of belief.  This though is not only a prerequisite for the stage of completion, but rather is a necessary step prior to any practice of the path of the secret word in general.  The three are the following: 1] Once the Lama has instructed the disciple in the secret teachings, the disciple must have recognized the beauty of these teachings, and come to believe in them. 2] The disciple must have come to believe in the Lama, since he or she is the one who has granted the disciple advices. 3] The disciple must have come to believe in themself, for they have gained extraordinary realizations by putting into actual practice the teachings they have received.]

The three are the following: 1] Once the Lama has instructed the disciple in the secret teachings, the disciple must have recognized the beauty of these teachings, and come to believe in them. 2] The disciple must have come to believe in the Lama, since he or she is the one who has granted the disciple advices. 3] The disciple must have come to believe in themself, for they have gained extraordinary realizations by putting into actual practice the teachings they have received.]"}

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU RDUL PHRA RAB TSOGS PA'I YAN LAG CAN GYI RDZAS NI MED DO, ,RDUL PHRA RAB MED PA'I SO SOR SNANG BA DMIGS SU MED DE, DPER NA RMI LAM NYAMS SU MYONG BA DANG MTSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du rdul phra rab tshogs pa'i yan lag can gyi rdzas ni med do, ,rdul phra rab med pa'i so sor snang ba dmigs su med de, dper na rmi lam nyams su myong ba dang mtshungs so
rows.english: Just so, introduce this disciple to the beliefs of the Yogi's Way [the Mind-Only School]: "There exist no substantial entities with parts that are made up of atoms.  The various appearances of things without physical atoms are insubstantial: they are, for example, the same as something that we experience in a dream.

The various appearances of things without physical atoms are insubstantial: they are, for example, the same as something that we experience in a dream."}

rows.acip: ,SNYING LA KHYOD SKU'I SNANG BA DRAN TZAM GYIS, ,RAB 'BYAMS SHES BYA'I TSOGS RNAMS MA LUS PA, ,JI BZHIN RTOGS PA'I RNAM DPYOD 'OD STONG GIS, ,'GRO BA'I RMONGS MUN MA LUS SEL BAR SHOG
rows.wylie: snying la khyod sku'i snang ba dran tsam gyis, ,rab 'byams shes bya'i tshogs rnams ma lus pa, ,ji bzhin rtogs pa'i rnam dpyod 'od stong gis, ,'gro ba'i rmongs mun ma lus sel bar shog
rows.english: I will think of you sometimes, that shining light of your sacred form, and I pray that by this simple thought, a thousand rays of crystal light-- knowledge that sees the entire galaxy of things that can be known, exactly as they are-- flies to every living being, and rips from them the darkness of ignorance.

rows.acip: DE NYID KYI STENG GI RGYAB LA PHYOGS PAR SNA TSOGS PAD ZLA NYI MA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI GDAN LA, RGYAL BA RDO RJE 'CHANG LA NYAMS LEN BYIN RLABS BRGYUD PA'I BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA,
rows.wylie: de nyid kyi steng gi rgyab la phyogs par sna tshogs pad zla nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi gdan la, rgyal ba rdo rje 'chang la nyams len byin rlabs brgyud pa'i bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa
rows.english: Upon this same massive throne, towards the back, is another cushion of a multicolored lotus, and the disks of the moon and the sun.  Upon it is seated the Victorious One, the Keeper of the Diamond, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of the blessings of practice.

Upon it is seated the Victorious One, the Keeper of the Diamond, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of the blessings of practice."}

rows.acip: G-YAS PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN BYAMS PA LA RGYA CHEN SPYOD BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA, G-YON PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN 'JAM DBYANGS LA ZAB MO LTA BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA,
rows.wylie: g-yas phyogs su rje btsun byams pa la rgya chen spyod brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa, g-yon phyogs su rje btsun 'jam dbyangs la zab mo lta brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa
rows.english: On this same massive throne, to the right of the Buddha, sits the holy Loving One, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of far-reaching deeds.  To the Buddha's left sits the holy Gentle Voice, with the Lamas of the lineage of the profound view circling him.
rows.raw: {"course": "TCS01", "acip": "G-YAS PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN BYAMS PA LA RGYA CHEN SPYOD BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA, G-YON PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN 'JAM DBYANGS LA ZAB MO LTA BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA,", "wylie": "g-yas phyogs su rje btsun byams pa la rgya chen spyod brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa, g-yon phyogs su rje btsun 'jam dbyangs la zab mo lta brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa", "english": "On this same massive throne, to the right of the Buddha, sits the holy Loving One, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of far-reaching deeds.  To the Buddha's left sits the holy Gentle Voice, with the Lamas of the lineage of the profound view circling him."}

rows.acip: DE NAS BLA MA THUB PA'I DBANG PO'I THUGS KA'I H'Um LAS 'OD ZER 'PHROS PA, MTHA' SKOR NA BZHUGS PA'I ZHI KHRO RAB 'BYAMS THAMS CAD LA 'PHOG PAS,
rows.wylie: de nas bla ma thub pa'i dbang po'i thugs ka'i hUM las 'od zer 'phros pa, mtha' skor na bzhugs pa'i zhi khro rab 'byams thams cad la 'phog pas
rows.english: Once more, light emerges from the sacred sound of huung at the heart of my Lama, the Lord of the Able Ones.  It flies forth and strikes the billions of sacred beings--both peaceful beings and wrathful ones--seated all round.

It flies forth and strikes the billions of sacred beings--both peaceful beings and wrathful ones--seated all round."}

rows.acip: THOGS MED KYIS RJE BTZUN BYAMS PA KHYI MOR MTHONG BA DANG, MEE TRI PAS RNAL 'BYOR GYI DBANG PHYUG SHA WA RI PA PHAG GSOD PA SOGS MI 'TSAM PA BYED PAR MTHONG BA BZHIN DU,
rows.wylie: thogs med kyis rje btsun byams pa khyi mor mthong ba dang, mee tri pas rnal 'byor gyi dbang phyug sha wa ri pa phag gsod pa sogs mi 'tsham pa byed par mthong ba bzhin du
rows.english: Asanga too saw the holy Loving One as a female dog.  And there was Maitripa, who saw Shawaripa, a veritable lord among yogis, committing highly inappropriate acts such as killing pigs.

rows.acip: MA ZAD, MKHAS GRUB SANGS RGYAS YE SHES KYI ZHABS DRUNG DU MDO SNGAGS KYI LAM GYI DKA' GNAS THAMS CAD GSAN TE THUGS NYAMS SU BZHES PAR MDZAD PAS,
rows.wylie: ma zad, mkhas grub sangs rgyas ye shes kyi zhabs drung du mdo sngags kyi lam gyi dka' gnas thams cad gsan te thugs nyams su bzhes par mdzad pas
rows.english: Not only that--he had also already sat at the feet of the wise and accomplished Sangye Yeshe, and listened to every difficult point in both the open and secret teachings, and grasped them thoroughly.

rows.acip: SNYING PO LEN PA'I TSUL YANG BLA MA SANGS RGYAS 'BRAL MED DU BSTEN NAS, DES BSTAN PA'I THEG PA MCHOG GI GDAMS PA'I SNYING PO NYAMS SU BLANGS TE, TSE GCIG NYID LA SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG BDE BLAG TU THOB PAR BYA'O, ,DE LTAR BYED NUS PAR BLA MA LHAS BYIN GYIS BRLAB TU GSOL, ZHES GSOL BA BTAB PAS,
rows.wylie: snying po len pa'i tshul yang bla ma sangs rgyas 'bral med du bsten nas, des bstan pa'i theg pa mchog gi gdams pa'i snying po nyams su blangs te, tshe gcig nyid la sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang bde blag tu thob par bya'o, ,de ltar byed nus par bla ma lhas byin gyis brlab tu gsol, zhes gsol ba btab pas
rows.english: How will I get this essence?  I will rely upon my Lama, and rely upon him or her as being indivisible from a Buddha; and then I will put into practice the very essence of the advices of the highest way.  In this way I will easily attain the high state of an enlightened Being, in this one life itself.  And so I make this supplication: "I beg you, my Lama, my Angel, to bless me, that I may be able to do so."

rows.acip: DE'I SANG NYIN DKA' BCU RAB 'BYAMS PA BZHI LNGA TZAM GYIS 'DUS PA'I RTZA RGYUD GYI 'GREL BSHAD RGYAS PA GCIG KHYER NAS 'DI'I STENG NAS CHOS THUN RE CIS KYANG ZHU ZHES GSOL BA BTAB PA DANG,
rows.wylie: de'i sang nyin dka' bcu rab 'byams pa bzhi lnga tsam gyis 'dus pa'i rtsa rgyud gyi 'grel bshad rgyas pa gcig khyer nas 'di'i steng nas chos thun re cis kyang zhu zhes gsol ba btab pa dang
rows.english: The very next day, a group of four or five high monk-scholars, including both Kachupas (Masters of the Ten Texts) and Rabjampas (Masters of Myriad Texts) came bearing a copy of the traditional commentary upon the root tantra for the Secret Collection.  They beseeched him, saying, "Is there any way at all that we could devote some sessions to working on this particular teaching?"

rows.acip: 'CHI BAR MA ZAD NAM 'CHI LA'ANG NGES PA MED DE, RANG CAG 'DZAM BU GLING PA'I TSE LA NGES PA MED PA DANG, 'CHI RKYEN SHIN TU MANG ZHING GSON PA'I RKYEN NYUNG BA DANG, LUS CHU'I SBU BA LTA BUR NYAMS CHUNG BAS NAM 'CHI LA NGES PA MED,
rows.wylie: 'chi bar ma zad nam 'chi la'ang nges pa med de, rang cag 'dzam bu gling pa'i tshe la nges pa med pa dang, 'chi rkyen shin tu mang zhing gson pa'i rkyen nyung ba dang, lus chu'i sbu ba lta bur nyams chung bas nam 'chi la nges pa med
rows.english: "Not only do I have to die, but there is absolutely no certainty when I will have to die.  We live on the continent of Dzambu, where the lifespan is not something which is fixed in length.  There are millions of things that can kill us, and only a very few which help to keep us alive.  And our bodies are like water bubbles; fragile and weak.  And so we can't be certain when it is we will die.

rows.acip: MANG PO NI MA BRTAGS NYAMS DGA' BAS GZHAD GAD DANG BCAS TE 'DUG PA DANG, PHAL CHES SER SNAS BSAGS PA'I DNGOS PO RJE NYID LA RE BA'I SEMS KYIS 'BUL BA
rows.wylie: mang po ni ma brtags nyams dga' bas gzhad gad dang bcas te 'dug pa dang, phal ches ser snas bsags pa'i dngos po rje nyid la re ba'i sems kyis 'bul ba
rows.english: Many were living without a care in the world; laughing, thinking of nothing.  The great majority of them were making offerings to the Lord himself, giving things that they had accumulated out of their unwillingness to share with others, hoping they would get something out of it.
rows.raw: {"course": "TCS01", "acip": "MANG PO NI MA BRTAGS NYAMS DGA' BAS GZHAD GAD DANG BCAS TE 'DUG PA DANG, PHAL CHES SER SNAS BSAGS PA'I DNGOS PO RJE NYID LA RE BA'I SEMS KYIS 'BUL BA", "wylie": "mang po ni ma brtags nyams dga' bas gzhad gad dang bcas te 'dug pa dang, phal ches ser snas bsags pa'i dngos po rje nyid la re ba'i sems kyis 'bul ba", "english": "Many were living without a care in the world; laughing, thinking of nothing.  The great majority of them were making offerings to the Lord himself, giving things that they had accumulated out of their unwillingness to share with others, hoping they would get something out of it."}

rows.acip: SER SNAS BSAGS PA'I NOR RDZAS SBRANG MA'I SBRANG RTZI DANG 'DRA BA 'DI LTAR MNGON SUM DU GSAL BAR STON PA'I SLOB DPON NO SNYAM DU THUGS SHIN TU 'BYUNG BAR GYUR NAS NYAMS MGUR 'DI LTAR MDZAD DO,
rows.wylie: ser snas bsags pa'i nor rdzas sbrang ma'i sbrang rtsi dang 'dra ba 'di ltar mngon sum du gsal bar ston pa'i slob dpon no snyam du thugs shin tu 'byung bar gyur nas nyams mgur 'di ltar mdzad do
rows.english: And these things they bring to offer me--all these things they've accumulated by refusing to share with others--they're all just a trap, like sticky honey inside a bee hive.  Oh everything around me is my Teacher, showing me very clearly, right to my face, how life really is. And so out of sadness in his holy heart, he wrote the following song of his own experience.

rows.acip: ,MDOG STOBS GZI NYAMS MI SDUG RNYINGS PA'I LUS, ,YID 'ONG YUL BRGYA 'TSOGS KYANG SPYOD MI NUS, ,DRAN DBANG BLO NYAMS 'GUM PAR MNGON PHYOGS PA, ,'JIGS RUNG RGAS PA'I TSUL 'DI GROGS DAG LTOS,
rows.wylie: mdog stobs gzi nyams mi sdug rnyings pa'i lus, ,yid 'ong yul brgya 'tshogs kyang spyod mi nus, ,dran dbang blo nyams 'gum par mngon phyogs pa, ,'jigs rung rgas pa'i tshul 'di grogs dag ltos
rows.english: Look at me, my companions in life-- look upon the terror of getting old: ugly, decrepit body, the ruddy complexion--gone the power of muscle--gone the dignity I carried--gone. rows.acip: NYON MONGS MANG BA LTUNG BA 'BYUNG BA'I SGO YIN PAS, 'DOD CHAGS KYI GNYEN POR MI SDUG PA DANG , ZHE SDANG GI GNYEN POR BYAMS PA DANG , GTI MUG GI GNYEN POR RTEN CING 'BREL BAR 'BYUNG BA SOGS BSGOMS NAS, NYES PA RNAMS KYIS MA GOS PA'I TSUL KHRIMS RNAM PAR DAG PA LA TSUL BZHIN DU BSLAB PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: nyon mongs mang ba ltung ba 'byung ba'i sgo yin pas, 'dod chags kyi gnyen por mi sdug pa dang , zhe sdang gi gnyen por byams pa dang , gti mug gi gnyen por rten cing 'brel bar 'byung ba sogs bsgoms nas, nyes pa rnams kyis ma gos pa'i tshul khrims rnam par dag pa la tshul bzhin du bslab par bya'o
rows.english: Allowing the mind to entertain different negative emotions at any given time is yet another open door to transgressing ones ethical commitments.  To prevent then the emotion of liking things in an ignorant way I will cultivate an awareness of how truly repulsive things are.  To prevent the emotion of disliking things in an ignorant way, I will cultivate love for others.  And to prevent the dark ignorance which underlies both of these, I will cultivate an understanding of principles such as dependent origination.  In these ways then I will see to it that I am able to follow a practice of the ethical life which is completely pure, unsullied by any kind of imperfection.

rows.acip: BDAG DANG MA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI RGYUD LA, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD LA NYE RING CHAGS SDANG DANG BRAL BA'I SEMS SNYOMS PA DANG MAR SHES DRIN DRAN DRIN GZO BYAMS SNYING RJE BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS KYI RTOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN SKYE BAR BLA MA LHAS BYIN GYIS BRLAB TU GSOL,
rows.wylie: bdag dang ma sems can thams cad kyi rgyud la, sems can thams cad la nye ring chags sdang dang bral ba'i sems snyoms pa dang mar shes drin dran drin gzo byams snying rje byang chub kyi sems kyi rtogs pa khyad par can skye bar bla ma lhas byin gyis brlab tu gsol
rows.english: Then make the following supplication: I ask you, my Lama, my Angel, to bless me and every other living being--each one of them by own mother--so that we may be able to develop within ourselves extraordinary realizations into a sense of equanimity towards every other living creature, completely free of the emotions of liking those who are close to us and disliking those who are not close to us.  And may we develop such realizations too into the practices of recognizing that all living beings are our mother; and learning to recall the kindness they have paid us; and working to repay that kindness; developing love for them; compassion for them; and finally the Wish for enlightenment, for them.

rows.acip: GNYIS PA THOB PA MI NYAMS PA BSRUNG TSUL NI, BYANG SEMS KYI SDE SNOD DGONGS 'GREL DANG BCAS PA LA MKHAS PA'I BSHES GNYEN DAM PA TSUL BZHIN DU BSTEN NAS BYANG SEMS KYI BSLAB BYA'I GNAS RNAMS SHES PAR BYA ZHING , KHYAD PAR RTZA LTUNG BCO BRGYAD DANG , NYES BYAS ZHE DRUG SOGS SHES PAR BYA DGOS SHING ,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa thob pa mi nyams pa bsrung tshul ni, byang sems kyi sde snod dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa la mkhas pa'i bshes gnyen dam pa tshul bzhin du bsten nas byang sems kyi bslab bya'i gnas rnams shes par bya zhing , khyad par rtsa ltung bco brgyad dang , nyes byas zhe drug sogs shes par bya dgos shing
rows.english: Next we describe ways for those who have received the bodhisattva vows to keep them, and prevent their decline.  You must first submit yourself, in the proper way, to a holy spiritual guide, one who is learned in the scriptures of the bodhisattva way, and in the commentaries which explain the true intent of these scriptures.  Then you must educate yourself in all the various bodhisattva precepts.  You should especially learn the eighteen root downfalls, the forty-six secondary offenses, and so on. The Eighteen Root Downfalls

rows.english: Come, offer your forehead To your Lord, your Lama, Highest Guide and King; Let it be a jewel That they wear upon their feet, and never remove. Throw your entire life Into practicing that profound path Which combines Both method and wisdom; The very cream Churned from the infinite ocean Of the Word of the Buddhas, Both open and secret. Wouldn't it be better if in this very life You and I could attain the unending bliss Of the three glorious bodies of an Angel? What think you? * * * Never to Leave the Highest Path We continue now with our review of the foundation commitments, in preparation for taking the vows of the secret way.  We have reached the second part of the more serious transgressions of the bodhisattva vows:

rows.acip: DE NAS BKRA SHIS LHUN POR PHEBS NAS SNGAGS GRVAR BZHUGS PA'I RAB 'BYAMS PA RNAMS LA 'DUS PA'I BSHAD NYAN GYI STENG DU DPAL DUS KYI 'KHOR LO'I RGYUD 'GREL GYI 'CHAD NYAN GSAR 'DZUGS MDZAD,
rows.wylie: de nas bkra shis lhun por phebs nas sngags grvar bzhugs pa'i rab 'byams pa rnams la 'dus pa'i bshad nyan gyi steng du dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i rgyud 'grel gyi 'chad nyan gsar 'dzugs mdzad
rows.english: He traveled on then to Trashi Hlunpo, where the rabjampas or master scholars of the monastery's tantric college were devoting themselves to teaching and learning the high practices of the Secret Collection.  At this point, he also introduced into the curriculum the teaching and study of both the root tantras and commentaries upon the glorious Kalachakra, or Wheel of Time.

rows.acip: DE NAS RE SHIG SKU MTSAMS MDZAD DE DPAL GSANG BA 'DUS PA'I ZAB LAM RIM PA LNGA LA NYAMS BZHES RTZE GCIG TU MDZAD PAS RIM LNGA'I RTOGS PA MNGON DU GYUR TE PHYI RABS KYI GDUL BYA RNAMS LA 'JAM MGON BLA MA'I RJES SU SLOB PAR 'DOD PA RNAMS KYIS RANG NGOS NAS NYAMS LEN BYUNG PHYIN RJE'I BSTAN PA 'DI LA TSE GCIG NYID LA ZUNG 'JUG BSGRUB PA'I NYE LAM 'DI LTA BU YOD DO ZHES RDO RJE'I SGRA DBYANGS SGROGS PAR MDZAD PA NI,
rows.wylie: de nas re shig sku mtshams mdzad de dpal gsang ba 'dus pa'i zab lam rim pa lnga la nyams bzhes rtse gcig tu mdzad pas rim lnga'i rtogs pa mngon du gyur te phyi rabs kyi gdul bya rnams la 'jam mgon bla ma'i rjes su slob par 'dod pa rnams kyis rang ngos nas nyams len byung phyin rje'i bstan pa 'di la tshe gcig nyid la zung 'jug bsgrub pa'i nye lam 'di lta bu yod do zhes rdo rje'i sgra dbyangs sgrogs par mdzad pa ni
rows.english: Following this he went into a personal retreat for some time, devoting himself single-mindedly to the practice of the Five Stages, a profound path within the teachings of the glorious Secret Collection.  As a result, he gained high realizations into these stages. He then burst forth with the following Song of the Diamond.  It is meant to declare the fact that there really does exist, here in the teachings of Lord Tsongkapa, a shortcut for achieving the Combination of the Two--tantric Buddhahood--in but this one brief life. The song tells the story of how he himself succeeded in actually using this shortcut; and he writes it specifically for future generations of disciples who hope to practice in the footsteps of our Lama, the Gentle Protector, Je Tsongkapa.

As a result, he gained high realizations into these stages. He then burst forth with the following Song of the Diamond.  It is meant to declare the fact that there really does exist, here in the teachings of Lord Tsongkapa, a shortcut for achieving the Combination of the Two--tantric Buddhahood--in but this one brief life. The song tells the story of how he himself succeeded in actually using this shortcut; and he writes it specifically for future generations of disciples who hope to practice in the footsteps of our Lama, the Gentle Protector, Je Tsongkapa."}

rows.english: I've been able To explore the meaning Of the Word, Both open and secret; I know How the cycle works, This realm Of causes and effects; I have trained In love, and in compassion, And in the One Wish For Buddhahood; I grasp The view of the world Which grasps That place beyond-- The way In which all things are; And I understand The profound practice Of the path Of two secret stages. When I think of this, I think of my Lama's kindness-- And oh how kind you have been to me, My Lama and my Lord.

rows.english: Next comes the meditation on love, which you do as follows.  First visualize a person sitting in front of you who is as appealing to you as your very own mother. rows.english: Let me school myself In love, and compassion, And in the two Different forms of the Wish; Let me perceive, Directly, that empty realm-- Free of all elaboration, Free of anything being itself. And let me travel To the very end of the path: The high secret practice Of both secret stages. Bless my mind to do so, Dromtun you my Lord. * * * The Five Immediate Misdeeds Our review of the root bodhisattva vows has taken us now to the five which correspond to the five "immediate" misdeeds, so called because a person who commits any of them takes their very next birth--immediately, with no other birth in between--in the lowest of the realms of hell.

rows.english: Others made commitments to recite, on a daily basis, some special prayers or the like--be it just once or 21 times, or whatever.  These would include prayers like Excellent Deeds; or The Prayer of Loving One; or The Confession of Transgressions; Verses in Praise of Tara; The Heart Sutra; The Verse for Taking Refuge; the lines of supplication for whichever Lama they happened to follow; or even just the mani mantra.  Others promised to give up taking any kind of life, or else to perform a certain number of prostrations--either the regular kind, or the type where you go all the way on the ground and stretch out your entire body.

rows.english: There were great difficulties then in the ensuing task of recognizing the next incarnation of the Dalai Lama.  Again, the revered one, Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen, gave his own personal material resources without the least hesitation.  He took all the crude people here in our Land of Snows and bought their cooperation with gifts of money and things. He showed perfect impartiality to one and to all.  Whenever it looked like some disturbance or military action might break out, he went to work using his compelling powers of love and compassion.  He brought people to make their peace, free of any hostility for each other, and saved the lives of a great many evil people.

rows.english: If in that hour you leave behind Even the name you used to be called, Then what need mention everything else? Oh here we are, me and the others of you Who perhaps are the same as me myself, Ignoring this one great terror to come, Completely engrossed in this life's affairs, Which having nothing to do with anything. Come please look after us, I pray, My Lama, look on us with love; We are every suffering person there is, And we have no one else to help us. * * * To Give Up Every Hope With this class we reach the final section in our review of the root bodhisattva vows.  This includes the last transgression of all, which is that unthinkable act of deciding that your will not one day become and enlightened Angel who can travel to all worlds and help all living beings.

rows.acip: MDOR NA THUB PA'I DBANG POS RANG YAL BAR DOR NAS GZHAN GCES PAR BZUNG STE, GZHAN GYI DON 'BA' ZHIG MDZAD PAS MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS PA YIN, BDAG GIS KYANG DE LTAR BYAS NA CHES SNGA BAR 'TSANG RGYA BA LA, DE LTAR MA BYAS PAS DA LTA'I BAR DU 'KHOR BAR 'KHYAMS,
rows.wylie: mdor na thub pa'i dbang pos rang yal bar dor nas gzhan gces par bzung ste, gzhan gyi don 'ba' zhig mdzad pas mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas pa yin, bdag gis kyang de ltar byas na ches snga bar 'tshang rgya ba la, de ltar ma byas pas da lta'i bar du 'khor bar 'khyams
rows.english: To put it briefly, the Lords of the Able Ones ignored themselves, and cherished others.  They worked only for others, and this is what brought them to the state of total enlightenment.  If I had managed to do the same thing, then I would have reached my own enlightenment too--long, long ago.  But I couldn't cherish others, and so I have wandered, to this day, in the cycle of pain.

But I couldn't cherish others, and so I have wandered, to this day, in the cycle of pain."}

rows.acip: THUGS DAM ZAB MO LAS G-YO BA MED PAR BZHUGS SHING THUN MTSAMS RNAMS SU BYAMS PAS DAM BCAS PA'I GSUNG GLENG MANG PO DANG ,
rows.wylie: thugs dam zab mo las g-yo ba med par bzhugs shing thun mtshams rnams su byams pas dam bcas pa'i gsung gleng mang po dang
rows.english: He remained unshakeable in the deepest state of mind.  Between his meditation sessions, he would suddenly blurt out all kinds of things, driven by the power of his love.  Over and over he would say things like the following--words about how we should be inspired by the infinite power of the Wish for enlightenment, never feeling discouraged as we work for the good of every living being, until the day that the universe itself draws to an end:
