rows.acip: GNYIS PA SEMS BSKYED CHO GAS BZUNG TSUL LA GNYIS, SDOM PA MA THOB PA THOB PAR BYA BA DANG , THOB PA MI NYAMS PAR BSRUNG TSUL LO,,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa sems bskyed cho gas bzung tshul la gnyis, sdom pa ma thob pa thob par bya ba dang , thob pa mi nyams par bsrung tshul lo
rows.english: Here second is our description of committing oneself to the Wish for enlightenment through a formal ceremony.  We proceed in two parts: going from not having bodhisattva vows to having them; and then keeping oneself from breaking the vows.
rows.raw: {"course": "TCS03", "acip": "GNYIS PA SEMS BSKYED CHO GAS BZUNG TSUL LA GNYIS, SDOM PA MA THOB PA THOB PAR BYA BA DANG , THOB PA MI NYAMS PAR BSRUNG TSUL LO,,", "wylie": "gnyis pa sems bskyed cho gas bzung tshul la gnyis, sdom pa ma thob pa thob par bya ba dang , thob pa mi nyams par bsrung tshul lo", "english": "Here second is our description of committing oneself to the Wish for enlightenment through a formal ceremony.  We proceed in two parts: going from not having bodhisattva vows to having them; and then keeping oneself from breaking the vows."}

rows.acip: GNYIS PA THOB PA MI NYAMS PAR BSRUNG TSUL NI, SPYI BOR BLA MA LHA BSGOM BZHIN PA'I NGANG x, MA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON DU MYUR DU YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG THOB PAR BYA,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa thob pa mi nyams par bsrung tshul ni, spyi bor bla ma lha bsgom bzhin pa'i ngang x, ma sems can thams cad kyi don du myur du yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par bya
rows.english: Here is the second part from above, which is keeping oneself from breaking the vows.  Go through the same part as before: Your Angel Lama is seated atop your head.  Think to yourself, "Now, for the sake of every living being--each one my own mother--I will quickly attain the state of a perfectly enlightened Buddha.

Go through the same part as before: Your Angel Lama is seated atop your head.  Think to yourself, \"Now, for the sake of every living being--each one my own mother--I will quickly attain the state of a perfectly enlightened Buddha."}

rows.acip: GZHAN YANG BLA MA SOGS LA KU RE DANG BZHAD GAD KYI PHYIR DU YANG BRDZUN GYIS DBU BSKOR BA DANG , GZHAN DGE BA BYED PA LA 'GYOD PA BSKYED PA DANG , THEG CHEN LA ZHUGS PA'I BYANG SEMS LA ZHE SDANG GIS MI SNYAN PAR SMRA BA DANG , LHAG BSAM MA YIN PAS G-YO SGYU BYED PA STE, NAG PO'I CHOS BZHI LA SOGS PA SEMS BSKYED NYAMS PA'I RGYU RNAMS SPONG BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: gzhan yang bla ma sogs la ku re dang bzhad gad kyi phyir du yang brdzun gyis dbu bskor ba dang , gzhan dge ba byed pa la 'gyod pa bskyed pa dang , theg chen la zhugs pa'i byang sems la zhe sdang gis mi snyan par smra ba dang , lhag bsam ma yin pas g-yo sgyu byed pa ste, nag po'i chos bzhi la sogs pa sems bskyed nyams pa'i rgyu rnams spong ba dang
rows.english: "I will moreover give up any behavior which might cause this Wish to diminish.  This includes the Four Black Deeds and other such acts: deceiving my Lama or any other such being with a lie, even if it is meant as a jest, or for fun; causing others to regret any good deed they have done; getting angry and then saying something unpleasant to a bodhisattva--meaning anyone who has entered the greater way; and acting in a devious way, unless it be through some high motivation such as taking personal responsibility for the liberation of all beings.

rows.acip: DE NYID KYI STENG GI RGYAB LA PHYOGS PAR SNA TSOGS PAD ZLA NYI MA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI GDAN LA, RGYAL BA RDO RJE 'CHANG LA NYAMS LEN BYIN RLABS BRGYUD PA'I BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA,
rows.wylie: de nyid kyi steng gi rgyab la phyogs par sna tshogs pad zla nyi ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi gdan la, rgyal ba rdo rje 'chang la nyams len byin rlabs brgyud pa'i bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa
rows.english: Upon this same massive throne, towards the back, is another cushion of a multicolored lotus, and the disks of the moon and the sun.  Upon it is seated the Victorious One, the Keeper of the Diamond, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of the blessings of practice.

Upon it is seated the Victorious One, the Keeper of the Diamond, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of the blessings of practice."}

rows.acip: G-YAS PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN BYAMS PA LA RGYA CHEN SPYOD BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA, G-YON PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN 'JAM DBYANGS LA ZAB MO LTA BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA,
rows.wylie: g-yas phyogs su rje btsun byams pa la rgya chen spyod brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa, g-yon phyogs su rje btsun 'jam dbyangs la zab mo lta brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa
rows.english: On this same massive throne, to the right of the Buddha, sits the holy Loving One, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of far-reaching deeds.  To the Buddha's left sits the holy Gentle Voice, with the Lamas of the lineage of the profound view circling him.
rows.raw: {"course": "TCS03", "acip": "G-YAS PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN BYAMS PA LA RGYA CHEN SPYOD BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA, G-YON PHYOGS SU RJE BTZUN 'JAM DBYANGS LA ZAB MO LTA BRGYUD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS BSKOR NAS BZHUGS PA,", "wylie": "g-yas phyogs su rje btsun byams pa la rgya chen spyod brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa, g-yon phyogs su rje btsun 'jam dbyangs la zab mo lta brgyud kyi bla ma rnams kyis bskor nas bzhugs pa", "english": "On this same massive throne, to the right of the Buddha, sits the holy Loving One, surrounded by the Lamas of the lineage of far-reaching deeds.  To the Buddha's left sits the holy Gentle Voice, with the Lamas of the lineage of the profound view circling him."}

rows.acip: DE NAS BLA MA THUB PA'I DBANG PO'I THUGS KA'I H'Um LAS 'OD ZER 'PHROS PA, MTHA' SKOR NA BZHUGS PA'I ZHI KHRO RAB 'BYAMS THAMS CAD LA 'PHOG PAS,
rows.wylie: de nas bla ma thub pa'i dbang po'i thugs ka'i hUM las 'od zer 'phros pa, mtha' skor na bzhugs pa'i zhi khro rab 'byams thams cad la 'phog pas
rows.english: Once more, light emerges from the sacred sound of huung at the heart of my Lama, the Lord of the Able Ones.  It flies forth and strikes the billions of sacred beings--both peaceful beings and wrathful ones--seated all round.

It flies forth and strikes the billions of sacred beings--both peaceful beings and wrathful ones--seated all round."}

rows.acip: GNYIS PA DNGOS GZHI LA RANG RGYUD SMIN BYED PHAR PHYIN DRUG DANG , GZHAN RGYUD SMIN BYED BSDU BZHI'I NYAMS LEN GNYIS LAS,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa dngos gzhi la rang rgyud smin byed phar phyin drug dang , gzhan rgyud smin byed bsdu bzhi'i nyams len gnyis las
rows.english: Here secondly is the actual practice.  Here we cover practice relating to those actions which serve to ripen ones own mental continuum--the six perfections; and then practice relating to the actions which ripen the minds of others--that is, the four methods of gathering disciples.

Here we cover practice relating to those actions which serve to ripen ones own mental continuum--the six perfections; and then practice relating to the actions which ripen the minds of others--that is, the four methods of gathering disciples."}

rows.acip: DBUL ZHING 'PHONGS PA'I SEMS CAN RNAMS LA LAN DANG RNAM PAR SMIN PA LA RE BA MED PAR SER SNA SPANGS TE, JI LTAR 'OS PA'I YO BYAD GTONG BAR BYED PA ZANG ZING GI SBYIN PA STE, SBYIN PA RNAM PA GSUM GYI NYAMS LEN LA TSUL BZHIN DU BSLAB PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: dbul zhing 'phongs pa'i sems can rnams la lan dang rnam par smin pa la re ba med par ser sna spangs te, ji ltar 'os pa'i yo byad gtong bar byed pa zang zing gi sbyin pa ste, sbyin pa rnam pa gsum gyi nyams len la tshul bzhin du bslab par bya'o
rows.english: And I will give the gift of material assistance to living beings who are poor and in need, by giving away any object which might fit their needs, without any trace of stinginess--giving up all hope of getting anything from them in return, or any karmic reward.

rows.english: I had hoped to accomplish Some practice of that deepest truth; But I got lost in gain and fame: To make people think I knew something I collected all these little bits of knowledge-- There is danger That I will miss the forest For the trees.

rows.english: Most of my hair Has fallen out, and what's left has turned to gray; My eyes Are blurry, they've sounded retreat, and sunken back in my head. rows.english: Use the deep practice, The path that combines method and wisdom, To rip out the hearts Of your enemies: that birth, that aging, the sickness and death. In every moment of your life Pray for a body and things and friends that no longer come and go.

rows.acip: DES NA RANG NYAMS LA DPAGS TE RIG PA 'PHANG 'DI TZAM ZHIG BSTOD NA RGOD PA SKYE BAR 'DUG SNYAM PA LAS CUNG ZAD GLOD, 'DI TZAM DU BZHAG NA BYING BA SKYE BAR 'DUG SNYAM PA LAS CUNG ZAD 'PHAR BSTOD NA RAN PAR 'GYUR BAS,
rows.wylie: des na rang nyams la dpags te rig pa 'phang 'di tsam zhig bstod na rgod pa skye bar 'dug snyam pa las cung zad glod, 'di tsam du bzhag na bying ba skye bar 'dug snyam pa las cung zad 'phar bstod na ran par 'gyur bas
rows.english: And so you have to develop the ability to judge where you are: "If I stimulate my frame of mind to this point, I tend to get agitation "--and then you loosen up a touch.  "But if I just let my mind slack to this extent, I tend to get dullness "--and then you stimulate the mind, raise it a bit, just far enough.

rows.acip: ,KHA PHYI LTA'I THA SNYAD RTOG GE PAS, ,'DI THOS NA 'GAL 'DU'I PHUNG POR SEMS, ,DON NYAMS MYONG CAN GYI RNAL 'BYOR BAS, ,GLU 'DI 'DRA GSAN NA 'DZUM PA 'CHOR, ,ZHES DANG ,
rows.wylie: kha phyi lta'i tha snyad rtog ge pas, ,'di thos na 'gal 'du'i phung por sems, ,don nyams myong can gyi rnal 'byor bas, ,glu 'di 'dra gsan na 'dzum pa 'chor, ,zhes dang
rows.english: O you logicians Men of words, with eyes that only point to the outside, You will read these words, And find here a mountain of disallowable paradox-- But if there's some yogi Who has any actual experience of the thing itself, I know This song of mine will bring a little smile to her lips. * * * Focusing on the Outer Form We continue now with our survey of the secondary offenses against the vows of the bodhisattva, from the masterful explanation of Geshe Tsewang Samdrup.  Here we complete the offenses which relate to the perfection of wisdom.

rows.acip: ,GDON DNGOS 'DZIN 'KHRUL PAS YID BSKYOD NAS, ,SGRO PHYIN CI LOG TU BTAGS SHING ZHEN, ,DE'I MTHU LAS BDAG GZHAN RIS SU BCAD, ,LAS NYON MONGS DBANG GIS 'KHOR BAR 'KHYAMS,
rows.wylie: gdon dngos 'dzin 'khrul pas yid bskyod nas, ,sgro phyin ci log tu btags shing zhen, ,de'i mthu las bdag gzhan ris su bcad, ,las nyon mongs dbang gis 'khor bar 'khyams
rows.english: Driven By that demon, the great mistake Of grasping onto things, My mind Makes up different objects Where none exist, and craves them. The force Of that then makes me divide What I see as "me, " and see as "you. " The power Of my bad thoughts and the deeds I do Then send me wandering through the cycle.

rows.acip: YANG DE DUS NGES DON ZAB MO'I NYAMS BZHES LA BRTZON PAR MDZAD PAS GZHUNG CHEN RNAMS DANG MTHUN PA'I MNYAM GZHAG DANG RJES THOB KYI RNAL 'BYOR GNYIS KA LA THUGS BKOL DU BTUB PA BYUNG NAS 'DI KHA'I RGYUD BSKYANG RGYU BYUNG NA STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA LA DKA' BA MI YONG BA 'DUG SNYAM PA THUGS LA SHAR ZHING
rows.wylie: yang de dus nges don zab mo'i nyams bzhes la brtson par mdzad pas gzhung chen rnams dang mthun pa'i mnyam gzhag dang rjes thob kyi rnal 'byor gnyis ka la thugs bkol du btub pa byung nas 'di kha'i rgyud bskyang rgyu byung na stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa la dka' ba mi yong ba 'dug snyam pa thugs la shar zhing
rows.english: In those days he threw himself into the practice of that most profound of all things: the one thing that the Buddha really had in mind with everything he ever taught.  And the following thought came up within his holy mind: Suppose I were able to devote my heart entirely to that pair: to the emptiness yogas of balanced meditation and subsequent wisdom.  And suppose I were able to maintain these yogas over some period of time.  I don't see how it would be any difficult thing then to perceive emptiness directly.

rows.acip: ,DUS DE RING NYAMS KYI SNANG BA LA, ,SPYIR 'GAL MED 'GAL BA LTAR SNANG BA'I, ,YID NGO MTSAR RI MO SNA TSOGS SHAR, ,CHA TZAM ZHIG 'PHAGS PA'I DBYANGS SU BSDEBS,

rows.english: It was today That a great many different And amazing Sketches appeared within my mind About the dance Of the things that appear around me-- Things That seem to contradict each other When in actuality They are in no contradiction at all. I'll set down In writing just a tiny fraction Of what I saw, In this  song of a realized being.

rows.acip: ,MNYAM MED BU RAM SHING PA'I DGONGS PA'I DON, ,DPAL LDAN MAR ME MDZAD DPAL YAB SRAS DANG , ,BLO BZANG RGYAL BA GNYIS PAS GSAL MDZAD PA, ,MDOR BSDUS NYAMS LEN RIM PAR BSGRIGS PA 'DI,
rows.wylie: mnyam med bu ram shing pa'i dgongs pa'i don, ,dpal ldan mar me mdzad dpal yab sras dang , ,blo bzang rgyal ba gnyis pas gsal mdzad pa, ,mdor bsdus nyams len rim par bsgrigs pa 'di
rows.english: The shining one, The Maker of Light, The glorious Father and Son-- And Lobsang too, The Buddha Come Again-- Have illuminated for us the true intent Of the matchless One of the Sugar Cane. I have undertaken then To set these teachings down in steps That are brief and easily practiced. [Translator's note: The "Maker of Light, Father and Son " here are Lord Atisha and his spiritual son, Dromton Je.  The "One of the Sugar Cane " is an epithet of Lord Buddha, whose people were known as the "Clan of the Sugar Cane. "]

rows.acip: BCOM LDAN 'DAS RDO RJE SEMS DPA', BDAG DANG SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI SDIG SGRIB DANG , DAM TSIG NYAMS CHAGS THAMS CAD BYANG ZHING DAG PAR MDZAD DU GSOL, ZHES GSOL BA BTAB PAS,

rows.english: And then I beg The Diamond Two, In the following words: O Conquering Ones, Warriors of the Diamond, I make this request of You: Take now all the negative things That I and every living creature Have ever committed. Take all our obstacles Take all the commitments We've overstepped or broken. Take them, Clean us of them, And make us pure again.

rows.acip: DENG KHYOD DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA THAMS CAD KYI RIGS SU ZHUGS KYI, DES NA NGAS KHYOD LA RDO RJE YE SHES BSKYED PAR BYA STE, YE SHES GANG GIS KHYOD DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA THAMS CAD KYI DNGOS GRUB RNAMS KYANG THOB PAR 'GYUR NA, DNGOS GRUB GZHAN RNAMS LTA SMOS KYANG CI DGOS, KHYOD KYIS KYANG 'DI DKYIL 'KHOR MA MTHONG BA RNAMS KYI MDUN DU SMRA BAR MI BYA STE, KHYOD DAM TSIG NYAMS PAR GYUR TA RE,
rows.wylie: deng khyod de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi rigs su zhugs kyi, des na ngas khyod la rdo rje ye shes bskyed par bya ste, ye shes gang gis khyod de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dngos grub rnams kyang thob par 'gyur na, dngos grub gzhan rnams lta smos kyang ci dgos, khyod kyis kyang 'di dkyil 'khor ma mthong ba rnams kyi mdun du smra bar mi bya ste, khyod dam tshig nyams par gyur ta re
rows.english: Today you have entered the high family of all those who have Gone That Way.  As such, I will now trigger within you the wisdom of the diamond.  This is the wisdom with which you will be able to reach all the high attainments of those who have Gone That Way; and so needless to say it will bring you all other goals you desire.  On your part, you must agree now never to speak of the things of this secret world to those who have yet to lay their eyes upon it.  Know that, if you do, then your commitments will be broken.

rows.acip: (ZHES BCOM LDAN 'DAS DPAL RDO RJE 'JIGS BYED BDUD LAS RNAM RGYAL GYI CHO GA CHA LAG TSANG BA NAG 'GROS SU BKOD BA ZHIG DGOS ZHES DAR HAN WANG GI PHYOGS KYI GRVA RIGS MANG THOS SDE SNOD 'DZIN PA SMON LAM RAB 'BYAMS PA BSTAN PA'I 'KHOR LO NAS RIN CHEN GNYIS PA'I RTEN 'BREL DANG LHA DAR BCAS RNA BA YANG YANG 'DZAR BA'I SOS DAL DU GNAS MA BCUG PAR BRTEN,)
rows.wylie: (zhes bcom ldan 'das dpal rdo rje 'jigs byed bdud las rnam rgyal gyi cho ga cha lag tshang ba nag 'gros su bkod ba zhig dgos zhes dar han wang gi phyogs kyi grva rigs mang thos sde snod 'dzin pa smon lam rab 'byams pa bstan pa'i 'khor lo nas rin chen gnyis pa'i rten 'brel dang lha dar bcas rna ba yang yang 'dzar ba'i sos dal du gnas ma bcug par brten,)
rows.english: (With this then I have ended the text.  It was composed in response to a request from a certain monk who lives in the area of Darhan Wang, who said to me, "We really need a ceremony which is complete, one which includes all the parts and the various ritual objects we need, and written in running prose, for granting initiation into the Conqueror, the shining Diamond Lord of Terror, Victor over the Demons."  The monk's name is Munlam Rabjampa Tenpay Korlo, and he is a highly learned man who holds all three of the collections of scripture.  He came to me with an auspicious offering of the second of the precious substances [silver coin], along with the raiment of the gods [a silk scarf], hanging his request on my ears again and again, stirring me from my customary state of indolence.

rows.acip: DE LTAR BZLAS PA BYAS PA LA DGOS PA YOD DE, RANG LA LHAG PA'I LHA NYE BA'I SGO NAS LAS RAB 'BYAMS MYUR DU 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR BA DANG, RDZOGS RIM GYI SKABS SU RDOR BZLAS KYI RTOGS PA SKYE BA'I DGE RTZA SMIN BYED PA 'GYUR BA DANG,

rows.english: Now there is a specific purpose for doing the visualization this way. rows.acip: ,PHYAG 'TSAL 'JAM DPAL DPAL GYUR RDZOGS PA KHYOD, ,CHOS KYI SKU LA BYAMS SDANG MI MNGA' YANG, ,SRID GSUM GDUG PA MA LUS 'DUL BA'I PHYIR, ,THUGS RJE THABS KYIS KHRO RGYAL SKUR BSTAN PA, ,'JIGS BYED GSHIN RJE GSHED LA PHYAG 'TSAL LO,
rows.wylie: phyag 'tshal 'jam dpal dpal gyur rdzogs pa khyod, ,chos kyi sku la byams sdang mi mnga' yang, ,srid gsum gdug pa ma lus 'dul ba'i phyir, ,thugs rje thabs kyis khro rgyal skur bstan pa, ,'jigs byed gshin rje gshed la phyag 'tshal lo
rows.english: Bow down! I bow to You, the glorious Gentle Voice, complete in all Your glory. You who in Your skilful means, In the highest love there is, Show yourself in the precious form Of the King of Wrath-- But only because You want to bring The evil beings of the universe To a state of peace: For the Body of the Dharma Knows no love or hate. I bow to You, Lord of Terror, Slayer of the Lord of Death.

rows.wylie: de nyid thugs rje chen pos rab khros pas, ,sgyu ma'i srin po srid gsum za ba bzhin, ,dam nyams phyi nang 'chi bdag gshin rje'i dgra, ,bla ma yi dam dbyer med skyabs bzung nas
rows.english: The boundless compassion of Your heart Now rages in fury; You're a warlock of illusion Prepared to swallow All three realms of the universe: Now You are The foe of the Slayer, The enemy of the Lord of Death, The death outside and in as well, The death of pledges broken. Protect us, keep us, Lama and Close Angel, Indivisible.

rows.acip: ,H'Um ZAG MED YE SHES BDUD RTZIR BYIN BRLABS PA'I, ,BDE BA CHEN PO'I TSOGS KYI MCHOD PA 'DI, ,DPAL LDAN RDO RJE 'JIGS BYED GSHID RJE'I GSHED, ,DUS 'KHOR GSANG BDE DGYES PA RDO RJE SOGS, ,YI DAM ZHI KHRO RAB 'BYAMS RNAMS LA 'BUL, ,DGYES SHING BZHES NAS SGRUB MCHOG BDAG CAG LA, ,'PHRIN LAS RNAM BZHI GRUB PA CHEN PO BRGYAD, ,BLA MED MCHOG GI DNGOS GRUB STZAL DU GSOL,
rows.wylie: hUM zag med ye shes bdud rtsir byin brlabs pa'i, ,bde ba chen po'i tshogs kyi mchod pa 'di, ,dpal ldan rdo rje 'jigs byed gshid rje'i gshed, ,dus 'khor gsang bde dgyes pa rdo rje sogs, ,yi dam zhi khro rab 'byams rnams la 'bul, ,dgyes shing bzhes nas sgrub mchog bdag cag la, ,'phrin las rnam bzhi grub pa chen po brgyad, ,bla med mchog gi dngos grub stsal du gsol
rows.english: Hung! Here is the Offering of the Gathering, Ecstasy itself, Blessed and become the nectar of deathlessness, Immaculate understanding. And we offer it To the glorious Diamond Lord of Terror, To the Slayer of the Lord of Death; And to all the millions of Close Angels, Peaceful ones and wrathful too: To those who count among Their number The Wheel of Time; the Secret Collection; Highest Bliss and the Diamond of Pleasure. Be pleased, we beg You, With our gift, and accept it from us. For we are high practitioners, And we ask that You grant us The power of the four mighty deeds, The eight great attainments, And the highest spiritual goal of all-- The unsurpassable.

rows.english: Be happy, come, Agree to come; Let all your painful thoughts And suffering be ended. Come find love, come find mercy; Find the highest Wish of all. Come and fill Your hearts with wealth: Worldview pure, no more mistakes. Come and quickly reach the state Where Your eyes will see all things.

rows.acip: 'DIR GSANG SNGAGS KYI SDOM PA MA THOB PA THOB PAR BYED PA'I THABS, THOB PA MI NYAMS PA BSRUNG TSUL, NYAMS NA PHYIR BCOS TSUL, SDOM PA BSRUNG BA'I PHAN YON DANG BZHI,
rows.wylie: 'dir gsang sngags kyi sdom pa ma thob pa thob par byed pa'i thabs, thob pa mi nyams pa bsrung tshul, nyams na phyir bcos tshul, sdom pa bsrung ba'i phan yon dang bzhi
rows.english: Our explanation of the commitments of the Diamond Way will proceed in four sections: how to go from not having secret vows to having them; how to keep from breaking your vows, once you have them; how to restore the vows if you do break them; and the benefits we derive from keeping these vows. How the Vows are Taken

How the Vows are Taken"}

rows.acip: GNYIS PA THOB PA MI NYAMS PAR BSRUNG TSUL NI, RDO RJE SLOB DPON MTSAN NYID DANG LDAN PA TSUL BZHIN DU BSTEN NAS, DAM TSIG DANG SDOM PA'I BSLAB BYA RNAMS SHES PAR BYA ZHING ,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa thob pa mi nyams par bsrung tshul ni, rdo rje slob dpon mtshan nyid dang ldan pa tshul bzhin du bsten nas, dam tshig dang sdom pa'i bslab bya rnams shes par bya zhing
rows.english: Here secondly is how we keep ourselves from breaking our vows, once we have received them.  For this we must first take ourselves in the proper way to a Diamond Master who is fully qualified, and learn from them all the necessary instructions concerning the various pledges and vows. *** Our Diamond or Tantric Master is the Warrior of Diamond; before we go on, here are some comments on this Diamond Being, from Je Tsongkapa's commentary to the Fifty Verses on Lamas:

rows.acip: BLA MA DANG NI SLOB MA DAG ,MTSUNGS PAR DAM TSIG NYAMS 'GYUR BAS, ,DPA' BOS DANG POR SLOB DPON DANG , ,SLOB MA'I 'BREL PA BRTAG PAR BYA,
rows.wylie: bla ma dang ni slob ma dag ,mtshungs par dam tshig nyams 'gyur bas, ,dpa' bos dang por slob dpon dang , ,slob ma'i 'brel pa brtag par bya
rows.english: From the Fifty Verses on Lamas: Warriors must first examine Any potential relationship Between Master and disciple, Since otherwise both of them-- Both Lama and disciple-- Will equally fail in their pledge. ***

rows.acip: 'DI LTAR MA BRTAGS PAR GANG RUNG RUNG DANG 'BREL PA BYAS NA, SNOD MIN LA GSANG BA BSTAN PAS BLA MA DAM TSIG NYAMS PAR 'GYUR LA SLOB MAS KYANG DAM TSIG BLANGS PA RNAMS BSRUNG BAR ME NUS PAS NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO, ,DES NA GNYIS KA MTSUNGS PAR DAM TSIG NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BAS BRTAG DGOS,
rows.wylie: 'di ltar ma brtags par gang rung rung dang 'brel pa byas na, snod min la gsang ba bstan pas bla ma dam tshig nyams par 'gyur la slob mas kyang dam tshig blangs pa rnams bsrung bar me nus pas nyams par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro, ,des na gnyis ka mtshungs par dam tshig nyams par 'gyur bas brtag dgos
rows.english: Now suppose a Teacher and a disciple make this relationship lightly, without first examining each other properly.  In so doing, the Lama has failed in their secret pledges, for they have revealed secrets to a person who is not yet a proper vessel for them.  The disciple as well will then be unable to keep their pledges, even if they should take them on.  Since both Teacher and disciple would then have failed, equally, in their pledges, such people must absolutely examine each other before creating any such relationship. ***

rows.english: The Fifty Verses says, Those who disparage their Master Will contract an illness that tortures them-- Some infectious disease, or a demon of sickness, The plague, or some kind of poisoning, And then these supremely ignorant ones Will go to their deaths. They are killed by the King, Or by fire, or poison of a snake, Or in water, or by spirits, Or by thieves or those Who guide them wrong; And they pass then to The realms of hell. ***

rows.english: The first chapter of the root tantra of Highest Bliss also states: Those who hope to practice, Those who live in meditation, Must always maintain their pledges. rows.english: The wording of this particular vow says that we have committed it when we have lost our love "for living beings," using the plural.  You should understand though that we break it whenever we have lost our love for any one living being. Now exactly what is it that we have to do to commit this particular downfall?  Krishnapada explains it as follows: Those who follow the greater way must feel towards every living being the same way they would towards their only child.  They must never, for even a single instant, give up on any one of these beings.  A follower of the greater way who has divorced themselves from this powerful karmic object of a single living being no longer even deserves the name of a "follower of the greater way."  It would be like calling  a firefly "the sun." Shantipa puts it this way: The state of "love" is where we have a true desire to assure that each and every living being reaches a state of unsurpassed help and happiness: where we never, ever, give up on one of them. These two explanations of the vow amount to the same thing, and so we can say that acting in a way opposite to what is described in them as "love" would constitute the act of giving up our love. ***

rows.english: A person then might come up with the following question: "Well which of the two is it that we have to do to commit this downfall of losing our love for a being: is it when we become angry at someone, and then fail to feel love towards that one particular person, or rather feel a wish that they fail to attain some happiness? The Red Tantra says, We must never give up Our thoughts of love For every living being. Jewel of Heart of Diamond also says, Never lose the Wish; Never give up a living being. These are talking about giving up our love; and so we can say that what the vow refers to is ever having the thought, "May they not find happiness they want." ***

rows.english: The empowerment includes the following wording: Today the Warrior of Diamond himself Has taken His seat within your heart. If you ever speak of these things, Then your heart will rip apart, And He will take His leave. The point here is that the pledges of the person who reveals the secrets deteriorate; and whereas the Warrior of the Diamond up to that point had resided within their heart, he is now no longer there.  In these and other descriptions, a great many major texts exhort us insistently never to reveal these secrets. Moreover, as we noted earlier in the quotation from The Book of Union, a person who has not yet been granted entrance into the secret world may engage in secret practices as much as they want, but they won't be able to reach any attainments at all by doing so.  As such, there is simply no purpose served by revealing secrets to such people: even if they try to put them into practice, there is absolutely no chance that they will reach any meaningful attainments this way.

rows.english: Suppose there is a person who is disparaging the Three Jewels, or our Lama; or who is engaged in destroying the teachings, a person who should properly be sent on.  If we befriend such a person either in our actions or our words, then we have committed the root downfall known as [10] "Acting kindly towards those who are truly evil." This is not to say that we commit a root downfall if we do not go further and actually send them on.  Nor do we ever give up our loving kindness for them in our hearts. ***

rows.english: Exactly what kind of action must we do in order to commit this particular root downfall?  We must "befriend" this person, acting kindly towards them in our actions and our words.  It is stated in the scriptures though that even if it reaches the point where we must send this person on, we must still in our hearts feel the greatest compassion for them.  As such, this downfall is not referring to having feelings of love for them. The two commentaries are in agreement upon this point.  This by the way is what constitutes the downfall of befriending them; it is not that anyone is saying that the root downfall here consists of failing to send such a person on. ***

rows.acip: DE LTAR MA BLTAS NA SDOM PA NYID NYAMS PA ZHES MA BZHAG LA, DE NYID KYIS DE SHIN TU G-YEL BAS BRGYA LAM NA NYES PA DE 'BYUNG BA DANG 'BRAL BA YIN LA, LAM 'DIR NI SKU GSUNG THUGS KYI DAM TSIG LAS 'GAL TE, SHES PA DE DANG BRAL BA NA THUGS KYI DAM TSIG NYAMS PAR BZHAG PAS NA DES 'JIGS PAS BSKUL TE RTAG TU TING NGE 'DZIN DE DANG 'BRAL BAR MI BYED CING BRAL BAR SPYAD NA YANG BAG YOD PAS SDOM ZHING 'CHAGS LA YANG SBYOR BAS NA RTAG TU MA BRAL BA STE,
rows.wylie: de ltar ma bltas na sdom pa nyid nyams pa zhes ma bzhag la, de nyid kyis de shin tu g-yel bas brgya lam na nyes pa de 'byung ba dang 'bral ba yin la, lam 'dir ni sku gsung thugs kyi dam tshig las 'gal te, shes pa de dang bral ba na thugs kyi dam tshig nyams par bzhag pas na des 'jigs pas bskul te rtag tu ting nge 'dzin de dang 'bral bar mi byed cing bral bar spyad na yang bag yod pas sdom zhing 'chags la yang sbyor bas na rtag tu ma bral ba ste
rows.english: Not being able to see things in this way--as an illusion--is not what we're talking about as the vow here.  Rather, it's during those infrequent occasions when we are distracted to an extreme degree away from this precise view that we are "separated" from it.  In this path we are at that point acting against the pledges of holy actions, words, and thoughts. The scripture here is urging us on, inciting fear in us, knowing that whenever we are separated from this particular state of mind then we have failed in our pledge to the holy mind.  We must never allow ourselves to be separated from this level of concentration; and if we do find that we have lost it, then we must use our awareness to restrain ourselves; to join us back to what we lost.  This then is "never being separated."

rows.english: The "jewel" in the name of the Angel called "Source of Jewels" is the wisdom referred to as "equivalent wisdom."  Because the family here is produced by this wisdom, the Angel is named "Source of Jewels."  The yoga of this Angel is where we unite ourselves, over and over, with this Angel, single-pointedly.  And this is what makes someone a practitioner of this particular family. The pledge that we take upon ourselves here--the action which we cannot transgress--is to delight in the various forms of giving. And when we "join" or apply ourselves to this act of giving, it brings us delight: thus it is that giving is described as "wonderful." ***

rows.wylie: sbyin pa bzhi'i chos dang zang zing sbyin pa sla la phyi ma gnyis ni, rtse mo las, ,dgra dang grogs dang bar ma la, ,sems snyoms mi 'jigs rab tu sbyin, ,snyan cing bden par smra ba yis, ,zhe sdang 'joms byed byams pa bsgom, zhes gsungs pa ltar shes par bya'o
rows.english: Two of the four types of giving--giving the Dharma and giving material things--are easily understood. What though exactly do the two latter forms of giving refer to? We can understand them as expressed in the following lines from the Tip of Diamond: Constantly give the gift of protection, By maintaining thoughts of equanimity For enemy, friend, and those between. Practice the gift of love By destroying your thoughts of anger, By speaking sweetly and with truth. ***

rows.acip: NYIN RE LA SBYIN PA BYED LUGS NI ZANG ZING DANG CHOS LA DNGOS SU BYED PA MA BYUNG BA'I TSE, RANG GI LUS DANG LONGS SPYOD GZHAN LA GTONG BA'I BSAM PA DANG RANG GI DGE BA'I CHOS GZHAN LA BSNGO BA'I BSAM PA SBYANGS TE, GTONG SEMS SPEL BA NYID SBYIN PA LA SLOB PA'I GTZO BO YIN PA'I PHYIR RO, ,BTANG SNYOMS DANG BYAMS PA BSGOMS NAS KYANG MI 'JIGS PA DANG BYAMS PA'I SBYIN PA BYA'O, ,DE BZHIN DU DAM CHOS 'DZIN PA DANG MCHOD PA LA YANG DNGOS DE CHOS DANG YID KYI SGO NAS BSGRUB PAR BYA STE RIGS GZHAN GNYIS KYI NI GO SLA'O,
rows.wylie: nyin re la sbyin pa byed lugs ni zang zing dang chos la dngos su byed pa ma byung ba'i tshe, rang gi lus dang longs spyod gzhan la gtong ba'i bsam pa dang rang gi dge ba'i chos gzhan la bsngo ba'i bsam pa sbyangs te, gtong sems spel ba nyid sbyin pa la slob pa'i gtso bo yin pa'i phyir ro, ,btang snyoms dang byams pa bsgoms nas kyang mi 'jigs pa dang byams pa'i sbyin pa bya'o, ,de bzhin du dam chos 'dzin pa dang mchod pa la yang dngos de chos dang yid kyi sgo nas bsgrub par bya ste rigs gzhan gnyis kyi ni go sla'o
rows.english: Now as for how we perform these acts of giving, there may be days when we're not actually able to present someone else with a material object, or with the Dharma.  In cases like this we should do the practice mentally, reflecting on how we can give our body or our things away to others, and dedicating to others the good deeds we have already done. This makes sense because the main point of the practice of giving is to increase our inner capacity for generosity.  And the very emotions of equanimity and love are giving protection from fear, and giving love.  It's easily grasped then how we can practice in the other two families the actions of both keeping the Dharma and making offerings, both actually and mentally. *** Returning now to Geshe Tsewang Samdrup, for the pledges of the next family:

rows.english: Saraha puts it this way, in his Ritual for the Secret World of the Skull of the Enlightened Ones: Warriors must rise in the morning And begin the day of observing The entire group of vows they possess: Commitments for eating, protecting, and such. Honor your pledges and vows Even at the cost of body or life; Lose yourself in the practice Of reviewing them thrice each day and night. If a yogi fails in doing so, They commit a serious misdeed. ***

rows.english: We must constantly live in fear that we may, in one of the ways described above, fail in one of these pledges. rows.english: The fifth pledge states that we should never set aside our actual, or our imagined, consort without having attained a firm state of simultaneous bliss. rows.english: Practitioners of this path should stay in deep concentration--which means that they should keep from ever being distracted, in their actions, words, or thoughts--and always (meaning continually) keep their pledges, refusing to let them be broken.  The pledges that they should keep are the primary and secondary pledges spoken in other secret teachings, as well as those spoken in this one.

rows.acip: DAM TSIG DE DAG MA BSRUNG NA RTZA RGYUD KYI LE'U DANG PO LAS, ,DAM TSIG NYAMS PAS DKYIL 'KHOR DU, ,DBANG BSKUR DNGOS GRUB THOB MI 'GYUR,

rows.english: The first chapter of the root secret teaching describes what will happen if you fail to keep your pledges: Those who break their pledges Will never reach the attainments Of empowerment in the secret world.

rows.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR, RTZA BA'I DAM TSIG LA SOGS PA NYAMS PAS NI SNGAR DKYIL 'KHOR DU DBANG BSKUR BA THOB PAR MI 'GYUR BA STE NUS PA NYAMS PAR 'GYUR LA, SNGAGS BZLAS PA SOGS KYIS KYANG DNGOS GRUB THOB PAR MI 'GYUR BA DANG , DER MA ZAD TSE 'DIR NAD GDON DU MAS GTZE BA DANG , PHYI MAR NGAN 'GROR 'GRO BA SOGS KYI NYES DMIGS SHIN TU CHE BA DANG ,

rows.english: The point of these lines is that those who break their primary pledges or the like will "never reach" their previous empowerment into the secret world--meaning that the energy of the empowerment will be lost.  And then even if they undertake practices such as reciting the secret words they will never reach any spiritual attainments.  Not only that; they will further be harmed by a great many spirits of sickness, and also have obstacles in their future lives, such as having to take birth in the lower realms.  The problems then of breaking your pledges are extremely serious.

rows.acip: SHES PAR BYAS NAS KYANG RDO RJE 'CHANG GI BCAS MTSAMS RNAMS LA DRAN SHES BSTEN NAS BSRUNG BA LA 'BAD DGOS SO, DE LTAR BYAS NA NYES PA DE RNAMS JE CHUNG NGU 'GRO ZHING BCAS MTSAMS LAS 'DAS PA RNAMS LA YANG 'GYOD PA SKYES NAS PHYIR 'CHOS PAR 'DOD PA 'BYUNG BAS TSE 'DI'AM SKYE BA GZHAN DU RING POR MI THOGS PAR BSHES GNYEN BSTEN PA LA MKHAS SHIN MKHAS PA LTAR DU NYAMS SU LAN NUS PA,
rows.wylie: shes par byas nas kyang rdo rje 'chang gi bcas mtshams rnams la dran shes bsten nas bsrung ba la 'bad dgos so, de ltar byas na nyes pa de rnams je chung ngu 'gro zhing bcas mtshams las 'das pa rnams la yang 'gyod pa skyes nas phyir 'chos par 'dod pa 'byung bas tshe 'di'am skye ba gzhan du ring por mi thogs par bshes gnyen bsten pa la mkhas shin mkhas pa ltar du nyams su lan nus pa
rows.english: And even after we have learned the rules of how to behave around our Lama we must go further: we need to devote ourselves to maintaining a high degree of awareness and watchfulness as we strive to keep ourselves from stepping over the lines of the rules set down by the Keeper of the Diamond. If we keep this up, we will find that we incur these faults less and less frequently; and that, whenever we do happen to transgress these rules, we feel intense regret, and naturally desire to restore our commitments. Once we have reached this point, we will find that before long--whether it be in this lifetime, or in those that follow--we will gain a very high level of ability to serve our Lama properly: to become a master among masters in the art of taking ourselves to our Lama. ***

rows.english: Now those who really hope, from the bottom of their heart, to train themselves in the unsurpassed way must first attain their empowerment.  And the very first thing they should do after that is to learn all the fine distinctions involved with the fourteen root vows and other commitments, so that they can keep from ever going over these lines. A person who is not honoring their commitments in this way can talk all they want about practicing the path, or a teaching or learning the secret teachings, but they are surely doing no more than gradually wandering further and further off the path of the diamond way. Those who wish themselves well then must first go and obtain an authentic empowerment, and then as the very foundation of their practice honor their pledges and vows.  With this basis then they must take themselves through the three-step process of learning, and contemplating, and then meditation upon the way of the secret word. *** B. The Mother Vows, Part Two We conclude now our study of the Mother Vows, with the second half of The Shining Glory of Great Bliss, by the great Kalka Damtsik Dorje:

rows.wylie: gsum pa nyams na phyir bcos tshul ni, bla ma la brnyas smod byed pa'i rtsa ltung lta bu la, bla ma de mnyes pa'i phyir 'byor ba ci yod kyis mchod pa dang , skyabs 'gro sems bskyed nan tan byas nas, dbang bskur ba tshul bzhin du blangs nas sdom pa gsor gzhug par bya zhing
rows.english: This brings us to the fourth section of our entire presentation: how to restore our commitments if we happen to break them.  suppose we have committed an act such as the root downfall of criticizing or disparaging our Lama. In this case we must first seek to please our Lama, by making Them an offering of whatever we can afford.  We must then seek shelter, and bring up within us the Wish for enlightenment, in a truly heartfelt way. With these then we must again seek to be granted empowerment, and take it in the proper way.  Within the empowerment then we restore our commitment.

rows.english: The various downfalls that we've described in this text are rules that were set down for the purpose of keeping us from committing the most serious of negative deeds.  It's good to remember that the principle objects towards which we commit these mistakes are three: the One who teaches us the Dharma; the friends who help us practice this Dharma; and the Dharma which we seek to practice, itself. ***

rows.wylie: 'dir 'bad pa chen pos ma bsgoms kyang skye ba bdun na dngos grub 'grub pa dang de yang rnal 'byor cung zad sgom pa dang dam tshig dang sdom pa dag pas 'grub kyi dam tshig nyams na dngos grub 'grub pa lta zhog ngan 'gror 'gro bas bde 'gro yang rnyed dka'o zhes gsungs so
rows.english: With these vows, one will achieve the final goal within seven lifetimes--even if you make no great efforts in the other practices.  When the scriptures say this though what they mean is that a person will reach the final goal if they keep up a minimum level of deep practice, and if they keep their pledges and vows pure.  But if we fail in this pledges, the scriptures are also saying, then not only is there no question of achieving the final goal; we will instead pass to the realms of misery, and just staying in a higher birth then would be highly unlikely.

rows.english: On the meaning of these lines, "beseeching the gods for help" and the rest, Jnyana Bodhi has given the following quotation: You may make to Them Offerings of fragrant Incense or flowers, But They will refuse To accept them. What this is saying is that--once a person has transgressed their pledges--then they may make offerings to Buddhas and bodhisattvas, but these beings will refuse to accept the offerings.  It is stated as well that angels and other such beings actually do harm to those who have failed in their pledges; and that Buddhas will refuse to protect them. ***

rows.wylie: rtsa ltung spong ba'i dam tshig ni sngags pa rnams kyi gnad dam pa yin pas 'bad nas bsrungs te dang po nas ma gos par bya ba dang gal te nyams na'ang ji mi snyam par mi 'jog par phyir bcos tshul bzhin du byas nas gso dgos te de ltar ma byas na de'i lhag ma rnal 'byor bzhi sgom pa sogs kyis 'bras bu 'byin mi nus pa ta la ya thog bskams pa'i dpes gsungs so
rows.english: The pledge to give up ever committing one of the root downfalls is a high spiritual key for those who follow the way of the secret way.  As such, we must devote ourselves to honoring our commitments: working never to be sullied by the downfalls in the first place, and--in the event that we do fail on occasion--never just letting it go, but rather restoring our commitments in the proper way.  If we fail in this one mission, then we can throw ourselves into the rest as much as we want--all four of the high yogic practices, or anything of the like--but it will never produce in us the fruits we desire.  We will be like, the scriptures say, the example of the dried-out top of a palm tree. ***

rows.english: Thus it is that the Tip of Diamond says, If you fail in these very pledges You will never reach the goal. Drink-- This is the water That will send you to hell, The water that will burn you If you break your commitments. And this water too Is the diamond nectar of deathlessness That will bring you every attainment If you keep your commitments. Commit yourself now To this core of the pledge Of the diamond bodhisattvas. ***

rows.english: For the first, we turn ourselves into the Angel through the practice of the six Angels. We then undertake the recitation of the mantras, being sure to maintain the four steps, in conjunction with restricting the exchange of the life-wind.

rows.wylie: 'di la kha cig na re, rgyud sde 'og ma'i tshogs lam pa'i rgyud kyi byams snying rje byang chub kyi sems sogs phar phyin theg pa nas bshad pa'i lam rnams chos can, rgyud sde 'og ma'i lam yin par thal, khyod kyis de dag gi lam lnga dang sa bcu 'jog tshul 'thad pa'i phyir
rows.english: Regarding this presentation, someone may come and raise the following objection: Consider the love, compassion, Wish for enlightenment, and other such qualities found in the heart of a person who has attained the path of accumulation that relates to one of the lower classes of the secret teachings--qualities which are described in the open teachings of the greater way.   Are you claiming then that these qualities constitute paths that belong to the lower classes of the secret teachings?  Because isn't the way you've defined the five paths and ten levels for these classes something which is accurate?

rows.english: This brings us to the second major part within our presentation of the levels and paths within the four classes of the secret teachings: a somewhat more expanded presentation of how we travel the path of the highest class of secret way--the teachings on the deep practice of the unsurpassed.  We proceed in four steps covering (1) how we are made into a worthy vessel for practicing this path; (2) keeping our pledges and commitments purely; (3) how we put the path into practice; and (4) how we then manifest the results of this practice.

rows.wylie: de yang lam rdzogs par nyams su len pa'i dbang du byas na dbang bzhi pa thob dgos shing , bum dbang gang du thob pa'i dkyil 'khor la ras bris dang rdul tshon dang lus dkyil gsum dang , gdul bya'i khyad par 'ga' zhig la bsam gtan gyi dkyil 'khor yang gsungs pas spyir na bzhi'o
rows.english: If we are talking about practicing this path in its entirety, then one must receive the fourth empowerment [see note below].  And generally speaking there are four different secret worlds in which one may receive the empowerment of the vase: in a secret world which is depicted in a painting; one drawn with colored sand; and the secret world of the body--along with the secret world of meditation described in scripture as appropriate for certain very special disciples. [Note: There is a serious error here in all editions of the text we have available to us.  The above sentence should read "one must receive all four empowerments" {DBANG BZHI KA THOB DGOS,} as confirmed by Je Tsongkapa's Great Book on the Way of the Secret Word, folio 251b.]

rows.wylie: rnam shes don gzhan chags pa yis, ,nus med don gzhan mi 'dzin phyir, ,zhes pa ltar, yid kyi shes pa don gzhan la zhugs drags pas mig la sogs pa'i shes pa skye ba'i de ma thag rkyen gyi nus pa nyams pas de dag re zhig ma skyes pa yin gyi dbang shes kyi snang ba bskyed rim gyis bkag pa min no
rows.english: The reason is the same as described in the text [of the Commentary on Valid Perception] that says, The reason is that, Because the consciousness is glued To a certain object, The power is gone-- And so it cannot grasp To another object. The point here is that--when the consciousness of our thoughts is fiercely focused upon a certain object--then the power to act as an immediately-preceding factor in producing a visual or similar type of consciousness is lost.  This then means that, for the time being, these types of consciousness cannot arise; it is not the case though the scenes in the mind that would occur through these sense consciousnesses is blocked by the stage of creation.

rows.english: You will notice that, among the 32 different Angels, we have not mentioned here the Ten Angels of Ferocity; or Loving One; or Excellence.  This only reflects the fact that they are not mentioned directly, in any clear way, in the root tantra.  Generally speaking though there are 32 different Angels of the transcendent body, because the entire 32 are mentioned in the section on the transcendent body found in the Hidden Explanation of How It Began.  Here you can refer to the commentary with the notes.

rows.english: There is a part in Kedrup Je's Treatise on the Secret Teaching in Two Sections which presents this is a way which conflicts with the explanation above.  It says, Suppose now that the third of the empowerments is given in its actual form to a bodhisattva who is in his or her final rebirth.  This bodhisattva, through practice with their partner, is able to give birth to a form of ecstasy which is complete in every aspect.  They are though still maintaining--they have still not lost--their direct perception of emptiness from before.

rows.english: There are a great many practices of the stage of completion which have been taught by authentic and accomplished masters which are not included in this list.  Among them is the practice of the stage of completion in the secret teachings of Lo Diamond, as explained by the accomplished master Virupa--where there is a way that we practice this stage all contained in the path of the three empowerments.  Another example would be the practices--described by the accomplished masters Dombipada and Durjaya Chandra--of the drop of spring, and the stages in the dissolution of the colors.

rows.acip: DUS 'KHOR NAS BSHAD PA'I RTZA LTUNG DANG PO NI, RDO RJE SLOB DPON GYI THUGS DKRUG PA DANG , GNYIS PA NI, BLA MA'I BKA' BSKO BA BCAG PA DANG , LNGA PA NI, KUN DA LTA BU'I BYANG SEMS 'DOR BA DANG , DRUG PA NI, SNGAGS DANG PHAR PHYIN PA'I THEG PA'I DE KHO NA NYID GNYIS LA MCHOG DMAN DU BZUNG NAS SMOD PA DANG , BCU PA NI, SGYU YI BYAMS PA ZHES PA ZHE LA GDUG PA 'DZIN ZHING KHA LA BYAMS PA BYED PA STE KHA ZHE MI MTHUN PA'I BYAMS PA BSTEN PA DANG , D'A RI KA PAS 'DI DANG MI 'DRA BAR BSHAD DO,,
rows.wylie: dus 'khor nas bshad pa'i rtsa ltung dang po ni, rdo rje slob dpon gyi thugs dkrug pa dang , gnyis pa ni, bla ma'i bka' bsko ba bcag pa dang , lnga pa ni, kun da lta bu'i byang sems 'dor ba dang , drug pa ni, sngags dang phar phyin pa'i theg pa'i de kho na nyid gnyis la mchog dman du bzung nas smod pa dang , bcu pa ni, sgyu yi byams pa zhes pa zhe la gdug pa 'dzin zhing kha la byams pa byed pa ste kha zhe mi mthun pa'i byams pa bsten pa dang , dA ri ka pas 'di dang mi 'dra bar bshad do
rows.english: The first root downfall described in the Wheel of Time is to disturb the precious heart of our Diamond Master.  The second is to break a command of our Lama.  The fifth is to give up the Wish for enlightenment, in the sense of the kunda--the element of enlightenment.  The sixth is to disparage the teachings, in the form of holding the opinion that there is a difference in the quality of emptiness between the secret teachings and the open teachings of the greater way.  The tenth is called "the illusion of love," which refers to holding malice in your heart but expressing love with your tongue: maintaining a form of love where the heart and the tongue are at odds with each other.  The explanation given by Darikapa at this point differs from this one.

rows.acip: DES NA SKU DE 'GRUB PA LA RDUL PHRA RAB TSOGS PA'I LUS NYAMS PAR BYA DGOS PAS, DE NI GSER 'GYUR GYI RTZIS LCAGS GSER DU BSGYUR BA BZHIN DU LUS LA BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS 'DZAG MED DU BCINGS PAS BEMS PO'I KHAMS RNAMS ZAD PAR BYED DE,
rows.wylie: des na sku de 'grub pa la rdul phra rab tshogs pa'i lus nyams par bya dgos pas, de ni gser 'gyur gyi rtsis lcags gser du bsgyur ba bzhin du lus la byang chub kyi sems 'dzag med du bcings pas bems po'i khams rnams zad par byed de
rows.english: It is though true that--in order to reach this holy body--the body which is composed of aggregates of atoms must be made to disappear.  As such, we must lock the element of enlightenment within the body, preventing it from oozing out.  This then can act like the alchemical elixir which turns iron into gold.  It brings all the various material parts of us to an end.

rows.acip: BDAG GIS RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS KYI GO 'PHANG THOB PAR BYAS LA, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD 'KHOR BA'I SDUG BSNGAL GYI RGYA MTSO LAS BSGRAL NAS RDZOGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI BDE BA LA DGOD PAR BYA, DE'I CHED DU RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA'I LAM GYI RIM PA NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BGYI'O, ZHES LAN GSUM GYIS TSAD MED BZHI TSANG BA'I SEMS BSKYED,
rows.wylie: bdag gis rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par byas la, sems can thams cad 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal gyi rgya mtsho las bsgral nas rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi bde ba la dgod par bya, de'i ched du rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i lam gyi rim pa nyams su blang bar bgyi'o, zhes lan gsum gyis tshad med bzhi tshang ba'i sems bskyed
rows.english: (Make then the Wishcomplete with the Four Immeasurablesby repeating this three times:) I swear I will reach the state Of a fully enlightened Buddha, And then I will free Every single living being From the ocean of pain Of this suffering life, And lead them finally To the bliss Of total enlightenment. To accomplish all this I will now carry out Each step to the path Of the Angel of Diamond.

rows.wylie: lnga pa bla ma'i rnal 'byor ni, mdun gyi nam mkhar seng khri pad+ma nyi zla brtsegs pa'i steng du drin can rtsa ba'i bla ma rdo rje chos kyi rnam pa can sku mdog dmar po lang tsho dar la babs pa, mdzes shing 'dzum pa'i nyams can
rows.english: In mid-air before me Stands a lion throne, And atop it cushions Of a lotus, the sun, and moon Stacked one atop the other. Upon the cushions Sits my Root Lama, The One of Total Kindness, In the form of the Angel, Dharma of Diamond. His body is made Of crimson light; His age is that Of an adult. He is lovely, And smiles at me With love.

My holy hair is black, It flows free, And covers me to my waist. I am a strong young woman, My nipples are erect in desire, And I have the look of pleasure. In my hair I wear An ornament made Of five dried human heads, And as a garland Another fifty more. I am naked, Adorned by the five accoutrements.

rows.acip: CES RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA N'A RO MKHA' SPYOD KYI SIN+D+HU RA'I DKYIL 'KHOR SGRUB MCHOD DANG DBANG GI CHO GA BDE CHEN GSAL SGRON ZHES BYA BA 'DI NI, RANG NYID LA RTZOM 'DUN NAR MAR YOD PA'I THOG ,NYE CHAR DGE TSUL MA SKAL BZANG CHOS SKYID NAS TSES BCU RNAM GNYIS LA NYAMS SU BLANGS CHOG PA'I SGRUB DKYIL TSIG NYUNG ZHING DON 'DUS PA ZHIG DGOS ZHES YANG DANG YANG DU BSKUL BA LTAR,

rows.english: (This ends the Light for Finding Ecstasy, a ritual for reaching, making offerings to, and then taking empowerment into the secret world of sindhura: the practice of the Heaven of the Angel, granted to Naropa for reaching the holy Angel of Diamond.  I had for quite some time been thinking constantly of composing such a work, and then recently I was approached by the novice nun Kelsang Chukyi, who urged me repeatedly to undertake this work, saying that people were in great need of a concise, abbreviated ceremony which could be used during the two tenth-day rituals of the month, as a practice for reaching Her, and entering into Her secret world.)

rows.english: Here, over a period of three years, Kyungpo Neljor was able to found 108 different monasteries, among them Shongshong.  He also gave a great many teachings of the Dharma. At some points, the monks would become complacent about their studies, and distracted form their practices.  Then Kyungpo Neljor would push them back in, by showing them different divine beings.  Some needed to see the exquisite forms of many different goddesses, while others required a whole variety of terrifying Angels: forms of the Slayer of Death.

rows.wylie: de'i nub yum mtshan nag gnal du song ba'i ngang nas, yul 'khor phra sa le gzigs pa'i bde stong gyis nyams cig shar, snga dro yab la zhus pas, yab shin tu mnyes par gyur te, khyod kyis lus la srid cig chags pa yin, de nyid dkon mchog gi thugs rjes phun gsum tshogs pa cig 'byung bar 'gyur ro gsung nas, slar yang dkon mchog la mchod pa phun gsum tshogs pa nam 'khrungs 'khrungs kyi bar du phul lags so
rows.english: On that very evening, as night fell, His holy Mother went to sleep and had a dream in which she saw the entire land bathed in light.  She then went into an experience of bliss and voidness, combined. In the morning, she related the dream to Naropa's holy Father, who was exceedingly pleased.  "A baby has been conceived in your womb," he said, "and the child is sure to be a most excellent one, having come to us through the compassion of the Three Jewels."  And with this they continued to present the finest of offerings to the Jewels, constantly, up to the time of the birth. His Wondrous Birth

rows.english: I bow down to my Angel, and to the Jewels. In kindness the Triple Gem Have taken me into Their care; And so listen I beg you, Father and Mother, To what I have to say. What use is devotion If it isn't devoted To the holy Dharma? What kind of love for a son Refuses that son What would make him happy? How can a person practice the Dharma But fail to think of impermanence— The day that we will die? If it doesn't displease you, Father and Mother, Then I ask you to allow me To return to the land of Kashmir In the company of these sages.

rows.english: The Prince decided that, for the time being, He would do as His holy parents had asked Him to.  He respectfully requested the sages to return to Kashmir without Him, and then devoted himself to His personal spiritual practice there in the palace. But then His holy parents approached Master Naropa again, with the following request: It's a wonderful thing, son, that you are teaching the holy Dharma to all of us here.  If however we actually put into practice what these teachings preach, then this fine ancestral lineage of Gautama himself will be broken forever.  As such, you yourself must find a maiden to be your queen, and bring her here to the palace, and make her your bride.

rows.english: "He did though say that, if he had no choice but to do so, then it would only be under one condition: we would have to find for him a maiden who belongs to a Hindu line; who doesn't grasp reality in any mistaken manner at all; who observes absolute cleanliness; who possesses love, compassion, and the Wish for enlightenment; who is sixteen years of age; and whose name happens to be Immaculate.  How on earth will we ever be able to find a maiden like this? "And that," he added, "is the reason why I'm so miserable."

rows.english: Crowds of people begin to gather there outside the door, in sympathy for the ministers.  The mob starts to shout out, demanding that the Brahmin allow Immaculate to take Her place as Queen.  Unable to bear it any longer, the Brahmin finally agrees to release his daughter. Overcome with joy, the two ministers return to their homeland.  They come to the king, Armor of Peace, and relate all these events to him.  The king is infinitely pleased, and sends forth a great many ministers, and members of the court, and palace servants to the Brahmin to greet his arrival, and bearing an infinite number of riches as gifts for him.

rows.acip: DE THAMS CAD LA YON TAN GYI SKYES LUGS KYI SNA RE RE MA BYUNG BA MED DE, DER DGA' ZHIG LA NYAMS DANG RTOGS PA SHAR, LA LAS MNGON SHES DANG RDZU 'PHRUL THOB, LA LAS RIG PA'I GNAS LNGA LA SBYANGS PA'I PHUL DU PHYIN PA MKHYEN, DUS DER PHYOGS THAMS CAD SNYAN PA DANG GRAGS PAS KHYAB STE, SANGS RGYAS KYI BSTAN PA 'DZIN NGOS SHES PA'I SKYES BU DAM PA CIG YOD PAR 'DUG ZER CING , MTSAN YANG GNAS BSTAS BSTAN PA 'DZIN PA ZHES YONGS SU GRAGS NAS LO DRUG BZHUGS TE,
rows.wylie: de thams cad la yon tan gyi skyes lugs kyi sna re re ma byung ba med de, der dga' zhig la nyams dang rtogs pa shar, la las mngon shes dang rdzu 'phrul thob, la las rig pa'i gnas lnga la sbyangs pa'i phul du phyin pa mkhyen, dus der phyogs thams cad snyan pa dang grags pas khyab ste, sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa 'dzin ngos shes pa'i skyes bu dam pa cig yod par 'dug zer cing , mtshan yang gnas bstas bstan pa 'dzin pa zhes yongs su grags nas lo drug bzhugs te
rows.english: These themselves were extraordinary people, and there was not a single amazing spiritual quality that you could not find mastered among them.  Some were undergoing profound spiritual experiences, giving birth to high realizations.  Others gained clairvoyance, and the ability to perform miracles.  Still others devoted themselves to the study of the five great divisions of classical knowledge, mastering them perfectly. It was during this period too that Naropa's own reputation and fame started to spread in every direction.  People began to say, "Now here is a truly holy being--someone who really knows how to uphold the teachings of the Buddha in this world."  And so Master Naropa himself came to be known by a new name:  The Elder who Upholds the Teachings.  He lived in this place for six years.

rows.english: With this we arrive at the third major division of Master Naropa's biography: a description of how He entered the door of the teachings of the secret way.  Here we proceed in six broad sections: (1) the way in which Master Naropa defeated His misperceptions of the Wish-Giving Jewel, His Tantric Teacher; (2) how His eyes were opened by this Jewel, when Tilopa revealed the meaning of silent messages and thus imparted to Naropa the path which ripens a person for higher practice; (3) how He experienced great hardships and suffering in order to undertake His practice of the path which liberates a person; (4) how He set his own disciples--disciples with the ten signs and the eight high spiritual qualities--upon the paths of ripening and liberation; (5) how He attained, in this very life, the holy form of the diamond--the rainbow body--and reached the knowledge of how all things are; and (6) how He imparted the oral lineage then to that holy being, Marpa, and thus brought these teachings to flourish here in the Land of Snows.

rows.acip: SGRA TSAD MDO RGYUD LA SOGS PA, GANG 'DOD KYI BSHAD PA MDZAD PA'I TSE 'KHRUL GYI BSHAD PA THAMS CAD SPANGS NAS DON NAM DAG GSAL BAR STON, SEMS SKYED DANG DBANG BSKUR, RAB GNAS MDZAD PA'I TSE, BYIN BRLABS KYIS LHAG TSAN, BSAM GTAN PA RNAMS LA MAN NGAG 'BOGS BA'I TSE, NYAMS RTOGS SHAN BYED PA'I MKHAS KHYAD, 'DI LTA BU'I MKHAN PO PHYOGS GZHAN DU PHEBS NAS CHU DANG BRAL BA'I NYA DANG KHYAD MI 'DUG
rows.wylie: sgra tshad mdo rgyud la sogs pa, gang 'dod kyi bshad pa mdzad pa'i tshe 'khrul gyi bshad pa thams cad spangs nas don nam dag gsal bar ston, sems skyed dang dbang bskur, rab gnas mdzad pa'i tshe, byin brlabs kyis lhag tshan, bsam gtan pa rnams la man ngag 'bogs ba'i tshe, nyams rtogs shan byed pa'i mkhas khyad, 'di lta bu'i mkhan po phyogs gzhan du phebs nas chu dang bral ba'i nya dang khyad mi 'dug
rows.english: "Then He teaches us whatever we need to learn, whether it be classical languages or the art of reasoning, the open or secret teachings—everything.  And when he does, he clears away all the mistaken explanations that might have been given before, elucidating then the proper meaning. "Whenever he performs a ceremony, whether it be granting the vows of the Wish for Enlightenment; or bestowing a secret empowerment; or carrying out the consecration of a sacred place, the blessings he imparts are incredibly powerful.  And when he gives personal advices to the monks in their meditation practice, he is extraordinarily skilled at describing all the different variations of meditative experience. "If we let this abbot of ours leave for some other place, we're all going to be left like fish out of the water." [Translator's note: Part of a sentence which appears to be missing in the original has been reconstructed in this section.]

rows.wylie: kho na re, ,sgyu lus zhen pa med gyi mda', ,'od gsal nyams kyis gzhu bkang nas, ,ngar 'dzin lus kyi ri bo la, ,bzung 'dzin ri dvags rgyug pa de, ,bsod las mos pa'i rngon pa bdag ,sang ni nya pa rgya mtsho snyog zer, mi snang bar gyur to, yang sang gsol ba 'debs bzhin tshol du phyin pas
rows.english: And the Dark Man says to Him, The wild deer Of holding that what we see And the one that sees it Both come from themselves Is racing up the mountain Of our bodies: our tendency To think they must be "me". I am the Hunter Who wants nothing more Than the kill: I take the arrow Of the rainbow body, The belief that nothing Is as it seems, And I use the bow Of the state of being In clear and simple light. Seek me then tomorrow, The fisherman At the ocean's shore. And with this He disappears.  And so the next day Naropa is walking still, praying still, seeking still.

rows.english: Tilopa replies to Naropa's request by saying, "O Naropa, to receive the instructions, one must first be granted empowerment--and so I shall do that now.  Bring me some embers from the fire, and a length of cloth." Naropa fetches the coals and cloth and offers them to His Master.  Tilopa takes the cloth, stretches it out evenly on the ground, and pins it down with four stakes.  He takes one edge of the cloth and has Naropa hold it in His hands; then Tilopa himself takes another edge, and starts that edge on fire with the embers. The cloth burns down to ashes, but you can still make out the pattern of its threads distinctly.  The form of the cloth is thus still there, unaffected; but its essence has changed to ashes, and it can no longer work as a piece of cloth.

rows.english: The essence of the empowerment, Which is like the embers, Burns away the cloth: The disciple's perception that Things come of themselves. rows.acip: DPAL N'A RO PAS, MA RIG MUN PA'I LJONGS 'GYUR PA'I, DMU LONG BDAG GIS JI LTAR LTA, ZHUS PAS, RJE GTZUN T'I LO YI ZHAL NAS, LTA RU MED PA'I TSUL GYIS LTOS, MTHONG DU MED PA'I NGANG NYID LAS, DO GZUNG MED PA'I DON THONG STE, MTHONG MED RNAL 'BYOR RANG GROL 'GYUR, GSUNGS PAS, DE N'A RO PAS DBANG GYIS NYAMS LEN LA LTAR MED DU BLTAS PAS, MTHONG MED DU MTHONG STE, GROL MED DU SKAD GCIG LAS GROL NAS,
rows.wylie: dpal nA ro pas, ma rig mun pa'i ljongs 'gyur pa'i, dmu long bdag gis ji ltar lta, zhus pas, rje gtsun tI lo yi zhal nas, lta ru med pa'i tshul gyis ltos, mthong du med pa'i ngang nyid las, do gzung med pa'i don thong ste, mthong med rnal 'byor rang grol 'gyur, gsungs pas, de nA ro pas dbang gyis nyams len la ltar med du bltas pas, mthong med du mthong ste, grol med du skad gcig las grol nas
rows.english: And the glorious Naropa replied, I am a blind man; My eyes were gouged out By my own ignorance. How can I See? That holiest of beings, Tilopa, utters then these words from His precious lips: See without seeing. See that thing Beyond all grasping By seeing Without seeing. Be the yogi Who unravels himself By simply not Seeing. Naropa remembers the empowerments. He tries to use them. He looks without looking. He sees without seeing. In a single instant, He is free in freeless.

rows.english: On top of all this, he must have entered the Sindura world of this very practice, and there been granted fully a deep blessing such that he will surely meet the inner, outer, and secret Queen of the Diamond. rows.english: dak gi dzokpay sanggye kyi gopang toppar je la,  semche tamche korway dukngel gyi  gyatso le drel ne dzokpay janchub kyi dewa la gupar ja,  dey chir du dorje nelnjormay lam gyi rimpa nyam su langwar gyio (Then recite:) I swear I will reach the state Of a fully enlightened Buddha, And then I will free Every single living being From the ocean of pain Of this suffering life, And lead them finally To the bliss Of total enlightenment. rows.acip: (CES BYAMS PA CHOS LEGS KYIS MDZAD PA 'DI BTON NA LONGS SPYOD 'PHEL BA'I RTEN 'BRAL KYANG YOD PAR GSUNGS PA 'DI NYID SOGS SHIS BRJOD KYIS MTHA' BRGYAN PAR BYA'O,)

rows.acip: (DE LTAR RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA N'A RO MKHA' SPYOD KYI SGRUB THABS THUN MONG MA YIN PA BDE CHEN NYE LAM ZHES BYA BA 'DI NI LAM 'DI NYAMS SU LEN PA'I RNAL 'BYOR BA DAG GI RGYUN GYI RNAL 'BYOR DANG, MTSAMS BSNYEN SOGS KYI SKABS NYAMS SU LEN BDE BA'I RIM PA KHO NAR SGRIGS KYI, DKYIL 'KHOR SGRUB MCHOD DANG 'BREL BA'I SKABS DKYIL CHOG DANG SBRAGS NAS NYAMS SU LEN TSUL GYI KHYAD PAR PHYED PAR BYA'O, ,)
rows.wylie: (de ltar rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma nA ro mkha' spyod kyi sgrub thabs thun mong ma yin pa bde chen nye lam zhes bya ba 'di ni lam 'di nyams su len pa'i rnal 'byor ba dag gi rgyun gyi rnal 'byor dang, mtshams bsnyen sogs kyi skabs nyams su len bde ba'i rim pa kho nar sgrigs kyi, dkyil 'khor sgrub mchod dang 'brel ba'i skabs dkyil chog dang sbrags nas nyams su len tshul gyi khyad par phyed par bya'o, ,)
rows.english: (This then is the Short Path to Great Bliss, a Unique Method for Becoming the Holy Angel of the Diamond, and Reaching the Heaven of Naropa.  I have written it only to provide some steps that are easy to carry out during those occasions when persons who usually follow this path perform their regular practice, or when they do a retreat or similar activity.  You should however draw a distinction between this and the method of practice connected to the Ritual for the Secret World, which is to be carried out on occasions that relate to the Offering to Reach the Secret World.)

rows.english: We have now reached the point, said our Lama, where I can begin delivering to you my brief teaching on the two stages of this path. rows.acip: 'BRING GIS DE LTAR NYAMS SU BLANGS KYANG RTAGS SOGS MA BYUNG NA GZHI BSNYEN 'BUM BRGYA KHA SKONG BSNYEN SGRUB SBRAGS MA, LANGGA LI YA'I SHING LA BRTEN NAS SGRUB PA LAS SBYOR BCAS BYAS PAS MKHA' SPYOD DU BGROD,
rows.wylie: 'bring gis de ltar nyams su blangs kyang rtags sogs ma byung na gzhi bsnyen 'bum brgya kha skong bsnyen sgrub sbrags ma, langga li ya'i shing la brten nas sgrub pa las sbyor bcas byas pas mkha' spyod du bgrod
rows.english: Those of medium abilities will travel to the Heaven of the Angel if they do the same; but it they fail to see a sign of the success of their practice, or something else like a sign, then they must do what we call the "foundation" retreat for getting close to the Angel, completing 100 sets of 100,000 recitations; and then in fulfillment they must combine the retreat with special practice for reaching the Angel.  This is the practice of the Tree of Langaliya; which combined with practices of the four modes enables them to travel to this Heaven.

rows.english: There is also the account of a Nepalese who lived in the days of Panchen Pelden Yeshe.  He came from the town of Shigatse, and kept this path as his practice.  One day sindhura powder fell from the sky onto his head; he went to Panchen Rinpoche and said, "This morning a rain of sindhura powder fell down on my head; it must be time for me to go to the Heaven of the Angel."  Then he showed the Rinpoche the sindhura, still stuck in his hair.   One day it came to pass that the man from Nepal had simply vanished; for he had actually gone to Her Heaven.

rows.wylie: 'di nyid kyi smon lam las, mar gyur 'gro la brtse ba'i gzhan dbang gis, sogs ltar lam thun mong bas rgyud legs par sbyangs te rab lam gtso gsum la rtsol med kyi myong ba thon pa, 'bring rtsol bcas kyi myong ba thon pa, dma' mtha'ang de gsum la go ba chags nas nyams 'og tu tshud pa zhig nges par dgos shing
rows.english: The concluding prayer for this very practice includes lines such as "May I learn to lose myself in love for every living being, my Mother."  This indicates the kind of person required: they must be well trained in the path which is shared by both the open and the secret teachings.  This means that, at the best, they must have an experiential knowledge of the three principal paths that can be called up without any effort at all.  Only fairly good is if the person can call up this kind of knowledge, but only with some effort.  And at the very least, they must definitely have a good intellectual understanding of the three and have gotten a good start at actually practicing them.

rows.acip: BLA MED KYI DKYIL 'KHOR CHEN PO ZHIG GI DBANG CHEN THOB PA NAS SNGAGS SPYI'I LAM NYAMS SU LEN PA LA ZHUGS CHOG KYANG, MKHA' SPYOD MA 'DI NYID KYI BSKYED RDZOGS LA NYAN BSHAD BSGOM BZLAS SOGS BYED DU MI RUNG BAS BLA MED KYI DBANG CHEN THOB PA'I RJES SU NGES PAR RJE BTZUN MA 'DI NYID KYI SINDH'U RA'I DKYIL 'KHOR DU ZHUGS TE, NANG GI RNAL 'BYOR MA BSKYED, PHYI'I RNAL 'BYOR MA DBAB, GSANG BA'I RNAL 'BYOR MA NGO SPRAD PA STE PHYI NANG GSANG BA'I RDO RJE BTZUN MO NGO 'PHROD NGES KYI DBANG BZHI BYIN RLABS LEGS PAR THOB PA,
rows.wylie: bla med kyi dkyil 'khor chen po zhig gi dbang chen thob pa nas sngags spyi'i lam nyams su len pa la zhugs chog kyang, mkha' spyod ma 'di nyid kyi bskyed rdzogs la nyan bshad bsgom bzlas sogs byed du mi rung bas bla med kyi dbang chen thob pa'i rjes su nges par rje btsun ma 'di nyid kyi sindhU ra'i dkyil 'khor du zhugs te, nang gi rnal 'byor ma bskyed, phyi'i rnal 'byor ma dbab, gsang ba'i rnal 'byor ma ngo sprad pa ste phyi nang gsang ba'i rdo rje btsun mo ngo 'phrod nges kyi dbang bzhi byin rlabs legs par thob pa
rows.english: Once one has received a great empowerment in one of the great secret worlds of the Unsurpassed group, they are allowed to engage in the practice of the general path of the secret word; but it is not appropriate for them to study or teach the creation or completion stages of this Angel in particular; to perform Her meditation and recitation; or so on. What the person must definitely do is--after receiving one of the great empowerments of the Unsurpassed group--enter this Angel's sindhura secret world.  There they must create the inner Angel; have the outer Angel descend; and be introduced to the secret Angel; that is, they must receive well a blessing of the four powers, such that it is certain that they will be introduced to the outer, inner, and secret Angels of the Diamond.

rows.english: Of all the teachings on the Angel, the Dharma that we intend to carry out should be one with four qualities of the oral tradition and four qualities of authenticity.  The first of the four qualities of the oral tradition is that the stream of empowerment should not have dried up.

rows.acip: BLA MED KYI RGYUD SDE CHEN PO'I DKYIL 'KHOR DU DBANG BZHI RNAM PAR DAG PA THOB CING, LHAG PAR 'DI NYID KYI DBANG BZHI BYIN RLABS MTSAN NYID TSANG BA THOB PA NAS BZUNG, DBANG BZHI BYIN RLABS KYI ZHAL SHES THUN MONG MA YIN PA'AM, THUN MONG BA GANG RUNG 'CHAG MED DU NYAMS SU BLANGS PA'O,
rows.wylie: bla med kyi rgyud sde chen po'i dkyil 'khor du dbang bzhi rnam par dag pa thob cing, lhag par 'di nyid kyi dbang bzhi byin rlabs mtshan nyid tshang ba thob pa nas bzung, dbang bzhi byin rlabs kyi zhal shes thun mong ma yin pa'am, thun mong ba gang rung 'chag med du nyams su blangs pa'o
rows.english: This means that everything must have been practiced in a continual stream over the years, without any break.  The pure four empowerments must have been received in a secret world belonging to the great Unsurpassed group of secret teachings.  Most especially, the four empowerments of this particular practice, complete in every requirement, must have been received.  And everything from here on up must be unbroken too, all the way to the private advices on the blessing of the four powers (which can be the unique advices, those that are shared, or both).

rows.acip: GNYIS PA BYIN RLABS KYI BRGYUD PA MA NYAMS PA NI, NYAMS SU BLANG BYA'I CHOS LA THE TSOM GYI SGRO 'DOGS BCAD DE, BAR DU TSUL 'CHAL DANG, DAM NYAMS DANG, 'DRES KHYER GYI SLAD PA MA ZHUGS PAR CHU BO'I RGYUN LTAR NYAMS SU LEN PA YIN,

rows.english: The second quality is that the stream of blessing must not have deteriorated.  This means that the Dharma you wish to carry out must have been examined and cleaned of any doubtful aspects: it must have been carried on in a steady flow uninterrupted by any corrupted morality, degenerated pledges, or any impurities introduced into the practice.

rows.english: The four qualities of authenticity refer to an authentic Lama; Word; classical commentary or instruction; and experience.  First, the root of all the paths of both the open and secret teachings depends on a qualified spiritual guide; and so here the "authentic Lama" consists of all the Lamas from the Angel Dharma of Diamond up to your own root Lama.

rows.acip: PAn CHEN N'A RO PAS KYANG DE DAG KHUNGS SU MDZAD DE YI DAM RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA DNGOS KYI MAN NGAG LA BRTEN NAS SROL PHYES, DE DAG KYANG TSIG GI BRGYUD PA TZAM MIN PAR RANG NYID KYIS SA LAM GYI RTOGS PA JI LTAR NYAMS SU MYONG BA BZHIN BSTAN PAS BSTAN PA GZHAN LAS KHYAD PAR DU 'PHAGS SHING, DER MA ZAD RJE BLA MAS, RGYA GAR GRUB CHEN RNAMS KYIS KYANG RGYUD DON DE NYID BCU BZHI'I CHINGS DANG SBYAR BA'I STENG NAS BKRAL BAS RGYUD KYI MAN NGAG RNYED SLA BAR GSUNGS SHING,
rows.wylie: paN chen nA ro pas kyang de dag khungs su mdzad de yi dam rdo rje rnal 'byor ma dngos kyi man ngag la brten nas srol phyes, de dag kyang tshig gi brgyud pa tsam min par rang nyid kyis sa lam gyi rtogs pa ji ltar nyams su myong ba bzhin bstan pas bstan pa gzhan las khyad par du 'phags shing, der ma zad rje bla mas, rgya gar grub chen rnams kyis kyang rgyud don de nyid bcu bzhi'i chings dang sbyar ba'i steng nas bkral bas rgyud kyi man ngag rnyed sla bar gsungs shing
rows.english: These essential practices are what Panchen Naropa used as his authoritative source when he founded his system based on the advices he had received directly from the Angel of Diamond.  They were not just passed on as mere words; rather they relate the actual realizations of the path as Naropa himself experienced them.  This makes them far superior to other teachings; even Je Lama said: "The great realized saints of India also gave their explanations utilizing the root sources of the Fourteen Essential Practices, and this has made the advices of this secret teaching easy to find."

rows.acip: RTEN GZHAL YAS KHANG CHOS 'BYUNG DANG, BRTEN PA LHA ZHAL GCIG PHYAG GNYIS TZAM LAS BSGOM MI DGOS LA, DENG DUS RNAM GA YENG DANG LE LO'I DBANG DU SONG BA DAG GIS KYANG NYAMS SU LON NUS PA'I TSIG TSOGS NYUNG LA DON RGYA CHE BYIN RLABS MYUR BA 'DI LTA BU GZHAN LA MED PAS LAG TU BLANG BDE BA'I KHYAD CHOS,
rows.wylie: rten gzhal yas khang chos 'byung dang, brten pa lha zhal gcig phyag gnyis tsam las bsgom mi dgos la, deng dus rnam ga yeng dang le lo'i dbang du song ba dag gis kyang nyams su lon nus pa'i tshig tshogs nyung la don rgya che byin rlabs myur ba 'di lta bu gzhan la med pas lag tu blang bde ba'i khyad chos
rows.english: Secondly, this practice requires no complicated visualization of a secret world; just a place, consisting of a palace made of a dharma star, and a being in that place, an Angel with no more than one head and two arms.  And the rituals are something that even those of us in modern times, overcome as we are by our distractions and lack of effort, can carry out: they pack a great amount of meaning into a small amount of words, and no other practice has blessings that are so quick.  And so the path we speak of today has a second unique quality, of being very easy to put into actual practice.

rows.acip: GSUM PA JI LTAR NYAMS SU LEN PA'I TSUL LA GNYIS, PHYI'I MKHA' SPYOD GTZO BOR SGRUB PA BSKYED RIM GYI RNAL 'BYOR DANG, NANG GI MKHA' SPYOD GTZO BOR SGRUB PA RDZOGS RIM GYI RNAL 'BYOR RO,

rows.english: This brings us to the part of the teaching on how it is that on should carry out the authentic Dharma he has found. rows.acip: DE YANG SA CHEN GYIS MDZAD PA'I BSKYED RIM RNAL 'BYOR BCU GCIG GI SDOM TSIG LA BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD LE'U NGA GCIG PA LAS GSUNGS PA'I DE NYID BCU BZHI KHA BSKANGS NAS SGRO 'DOGS GCOD PA DANG, RGYAL MCHOG LNGA PA'I MTHONG GROL LDE MIG GI BCAD DON NYAMS LEN SEMS 'DZIN GYI BYA BA SOGS KYIS GZHI MDZAD,
rows.wylie: de yang sa chen gyis mdzad pa'i bskyed rim rnal 'byor bcu gcig gi sdom tshig la bde mchog rtsa rgyud le'u nga gcig pa las gsungs pa'i de nyid bcu bzhi kha bskangs nas sgro 'dogs gcod pa dang, rgyal mchog lnga pa'i mthong grol lde mig gi bcad don nyams len sems 'dzin gyi bya ba sogs kyis gzhi mdzad
rows.english: Now our holy teacher, Master Quicksilver--Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra--once granted us a teaching on the two stages of the Woman of Holiness, the Angel of Diamond, Vajra Yogini. The foundation for His presentation had two parts.  The first is a thorough explanation of the teaching on the stage of creation granted by the great Sachen, Kunga Nyingpo--his verses of summary upon the Eleven Yogas--supplemented by the Fourteen Essential Practices spoken in the 51st chapter of the root tantra of Highest Bliss.  The second consists of the practices of visualization and so forth which are outlined in Freedom on Sight, the Key--composed by His Holiness, the Great Fifth of the Dalai Lamas.

rows.english: We now continue to an in-depth explanation of the two steps of sleeping and waking, and partaking of the nectar.
