rows.acip: DE TZAM BSGOMS PA YANG BSKYED RIM PA'I BDE CHEN 'BAR BA'I THABS SU 'GYUR MOD, 'ON KYANG LCANG SKYA RIN PO CHES RDZOGS RIM GYI BDE CHEN 'DREN PA LA RTZA GSUM 'KHOR LO BZHI SOGS GSAL BTAB NAS 'BAR 'DZAG BSGOM NA SHIN TU LEGS PAR GSUNGS PA'I DGONGS PA LTAR BDAG GI RJE BLA MAS KYANG RGYAS PAR NYAMS SU LEN TSUL DANG, BSRE BA SKOR GSUM SOGS KYANG SKABS 'GAR GSUNG NGO,,
rows.wylie: de tsam bsgoms pa yang bskyed rim pa'i bde chen 'bar ba'i thabs su 'gyur mod, 'on kyang lcang skya rin po ches rdzogs rim gyi bde chen 'dren pa la rtsa gsum 'khor lo bzhi sogs gsal btab nas 'bar 'dzag bsgom na shin tu legs par gsungs pa'i dgongs pa ltar bdag gi rje bla mas kyang rgyas par nyams su len tshul dang, bsre ba skor gsum sogs kyang skabs 'gar gsung ngo
rows.english: Admittedly, even if you only meditate on this, it becomes a means of igniting great bliss for a person on the stage of creation.  However, it has been stated by the Precious Changkya that, in order to elicit the great bliss of the completion stage, it is extremely good if we meditate on the blazing and dripping, while visualizing the three channels, the four chakras, and so on.  And this thought is shared by our own Lord and Lama, who has extensively explained this on several occasions, in his topics such as how to put this into practice, and the three stages of mixing.

rows.wylie: rdo rje phag mo'i bskyed rim ngag bzlas dang bcas pa 'di mkha' spyod sgrub pa'i thabs mchog tu gyur pa yin zhing rdzogs rim la nges par ltos mi dgos pas bskyed rim phag mo mkha' spyod ces gsungs kyang don du 'di nyid bskyed rdzogs zung 'brel gyi nyams len yin pas bskyed rim gzhan las khyad par du 'phags so
rows.english: As Master Tsarchen is saying here, this creation-stage practice of the Diamond Sow, along with the practice of verbal recitation, is actually the highest method for reaching Her heaven; as such it is not completely necessary to delve into the practices of the completion stage.  It is for this reason that this practice of the creation stage has been given the name "Heaven of the Sow."  And since the purpose of this particular practice is to unite the creation and completion stages together, it is considered to be on a completely higher level than other creation-stage practices.

rows.acip: LAM MTHUN MONG BAS RGYUD SBYANGS, DAM SDOM TSUL BZHIN DU BSRUNG BA GZHIR BZHAG NAS MA CHAG PAR NYAMS SU BLANGS, GZHI BSNYEN 'BUM PHRAG BZHI KHA SKONG GI SBYIN SREG DANG BCAS PA SONG ZHING, TSES BCU RNAM GNYIS MA CHAG CING TSOGS 'KHOR LA BRTZON PAR BYAS NA DUS RE ZHIG NA LUS 'DI MA SPANGS PAR RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA'I SPRUL PA'I BUD MED KYIS MKHA' SPYOD DU 'KHRID PAR 'GYUR RO,,

rows.english: Then we must use the practices of the shared path to purify our mind, and we must make keeping our pledges and vows properly the foundation of our practice. And if we practice continuously, completing our four close retreats of 100,000 mantras (along with their fire offerings to purify any mistakes), always keeping the two practices of the 10th, and making heartfelt efforts in the offerings of the circle of the gathering, then in a very short time--without our having to give up this present body--a female emanation of the holy Diamond Angel will come and lead us to heaven.

rows.acip: PHYOGS ZHES PA BCU'I MING DANG, ZLA BA ZHES PA GCIG GI MING STE BCU DANG GCIG GI RNAL 'BYOR TSUL BZHIN DU NYAMS SU BLANG NA, NAM ZHIG GI DUS NA DGA' MA STE BUD MED RJE BTZUN MA'I SPRUL PA YIN PA'I RTAGS SU BYU RU LTAR SHA MDOG SHIN TU DMAR BA, LI KHRI'I KHA DOG LTA BU'I SKRA DMAR SER BSIL BUR GROL BA, SMIN MA DMAR SER CAN GYI MIG G-YO MA DPRAL BAR SHA'I RI MO DGA' PA 'KHYIL BA'I RNAM PA CAN YOD PA DANG MJAL NAS
rows.wylie: phyogs zhes pa bcu'i ming dang, zla ba zhes pa gcig gi ming ste bcu dang gcig gi rnal 'byor tshul bzhin du nyams su blang na, nam zhig gi dus na dga' ma ste bud med rje btsun ma'i sprul pa yin pa'i rtags su byu ru ltar sha mdog shin tu dmar ba, li khri'i kha dog lta bu'i skra dmar ser bsil bur grol ba, smin ma dmar ser can gyi mig g-yo ma dpral bar sha'i ri mo dga' pa 'khyil ba'i rnam pa can yod pa dang mjal nas
rows.english: Directions is a code word for the number ten, and moon is a code word for the number one: thus we are praying here that if we properly carry out the ten and one deep practices, then may it one day soon bring me my lover, the lady of bliss.  And as a sign that she really is emanating as this holy human female may she appear flushed with red, the color of coral, with free and flowing golden hair.  May her eyes move in laughter, beneath golden eyebrows, and may the skin at her forehead suggest a swirl of bliss.  Then after I meet her...

rows.acip: SINDHU RGYA SKAD DANG, BOD SKAD LI KHRI, DE DANG LANGGA LI'I SHING SOGS YO BYAD DANG PHYAG LEN MA 'DZOL BA'I SGO NAS, RO LDAN TE DUR 'KHROD KYI GNAS SU BSGRUBS SHING YUL PHYOGS THAMS CAD DU MYUL BA STE 'KHYAMS PAS
rows.wylie: sindhu rgya skad dang, bod skad li khri, de dang langga li'i shing sogs yo byad dang phyag len ma 'dzol ba'i sgo nas, ro ldan te dur 'khrod kyi gnas su bsgrubs shing yul phyogs thams cad du myul ba ste 'khyams pas
rows.english: Once all this completed, then take all the essentials--such as the Sindhura powder (as it is called in Sanskrit, or Litri in Tibetan); and a Langali trunk; and your own spiritual observances free of any errors--and practice in the home of the dead (meaning in a burial ground, surrounded by corpses).  And then go wandering off--journey at random--in every direction, to places both far away and nearby.

rows.acip: DES KYANG DA DUNG LE LO MI BYA BAR GLO SNYING BRANG GSUM BLA MA RJE BTZUN MAR GTAD NAS NYAMS LEN CHAG MED BYAS NA BAR DOR MKHA' SPYOD KYI DPA' BO MKHA' 'GROS BSU BAR BDE MCHOG RTZA RGYUD LAS GSUNGS LA,

rows.english: Those of us who are too lazy to accomplish even this much are categorized as the very lowest of the low. And it has been stated that once that has transpired, then if they have not broken their pledges and vows; or if they have broken them, but at some point before the time of their death they restore their secret vows--first by confessing and swearing and then by either requesting empowerment or taking self-initiation; then unless this person has been sullied by a new root downfall, they will reach their highest goals either in three lifetimes, or five, or seven, or at the very most within sixteen lifetimes.

rows.acip: DRI YI BZHON PAR GYUR PA'I MGYOGS 'GRO RLUNG GIS, RANG SEMS BAm YIG GI GZUGS SU GSAL BA DE, DH'U T'I RTZA DBU MA'I LAM BRGYUD NAS SPYI BO TSANGS PA'I BU GA'I SGOR BSKYOD PA RGYAL YUM RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA'I BDE STONG GNYIS SU MED PA'I THUGS DANG BSRE BAR BYED PA'I 'DA' GA MA'I NYAMS LEN MYUR LAM 'PHO BA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYIS LUS SEMS BRAL MA THAG PA'I SKAD CIG DE LA MKHA' SPYOD DU BGROD NAS MYUR DU GROL BA THOB PAR SHOG CIG, CES SMON PA'O,
rows.wylie: dri yi bzhon par gyur pa'i mgyogs 'gro rlung gis, rang sems baM yig gi gzugs su gsal ba de, dhU tI rtsa dbu ma'i lam brgyud nas spyi bo tshangs pa'i bu ga'i sgor bskyod pa rgyal yum rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i bde stong gnyis su med pa'i thugs dang bsre bar byed pa'i 'da' ga ma'i nyams len myur lam 'pho ba'i rnal 'byor gyis lus sems bral ma thag pa'i skad cig de la mkha' spyod du bgrod nas myur du grol ba thob par shog cig, ces smon pa'o
rows.english: And we are praying here that we can use this inner wind to take my mind, which is expressing itself in the form of  the letter Vam, up the path or road of the central channel--the channel of dance, to the door or hole of the Pure One at the crown of the head.  And we are then praying that, by doing so, we may be quickly freed, that we may reach the goal, by travelling to Her heaven in that single instant when we sever the connection between mind and body through the deep practice of transferring our consciousness--that quick path practiced at the very hour of death, where we become blended within the holy mind of indivisible bliss and voidness of the Angel of Diamond, Woman of all Victors. Note: The instructions for the unique form of the Yoga of the Inconceivable follow here, and will be granted individually to students of the course when the time is right!

rows.acip: ' ,NUB NYI SHU PAR, MTHONG GROL DU RDZOGS RIM LA SGRO 'DOGS GCOD PA SEMS 'DZIN ZHES NYIS SBRAGS SU GTONG RGYU MED PAR GSUNGS, SPYIR SA LUGS LA SGRO 'DOGS GCOD PA DANG SEMS 'DZIN SO SOR BZHED KYANG RJE RIN PO CHES SGRO 'DOGS GCOD PA DE NYAMS SU LEN TSUL KHO NA LA GCOD PA YIN GYI NYAMS SU LEN TSUL GZHAN DANG SGRO 'DOGS GZHAN LA GCOD PA MA YIN TE,
rows.wylie: ' ,nub nyi shu par, mthong grol du rdzogs rim la sgro 'dogs gcod pa sems 'dzin zhes nyis sbrags su gtong rgyu med par gsungs, spyir sa lugs la sgro 'dogs gcod pa dang sems 'dzin so sor bzhed kyang rje rin po ches sgro 'dogs gcod pa de nyams su len tshul kho na la gcod pa yin gyi nyams su len tshul gzhan dang sgro 'dogs gzhan la gcod pa ma yin te
rows.english: As for the evening of the 20th day, it is said in Freedom on Sight that "On the subject of the stage of completion, we have no reason to undertake a separate analysis and focus of meditation."  Generally speaking, the Sakya tradition holds that the analysis or review of topics, and the daily focus of meditation, are two separate things.  Je Tsongkapa though says that the only thing we analyze or review during the analysis of subjects is in fact what we intend to put into our actual practice: it's not that we're examining one thing first and then focusing our practice on something else after that.

rows.acip: RTA DKYU SA GZHAN DU BYAS NAS RGYUG SA GZHAN DU STON PA BZHAD GAD GYI GNAS LTAR, THOS BSAM GYIS GZHAN ZHIG GTAN LA PHAB NAS NYAMS SU LEN RGYU GZHAN SGOM NA BZHAD GAD KYI GNAS YIN PAS SO SOR MI BZHED LA,
rows.wylie: rta dkyu sa gzhan du byas nas rgyug sa gzhan du ston pa bzhad gad gyi gnas ltar, thos bsam gyis gzhan zhig gtan la phab nas nyams su len rgyu gzhan sgom na bzhad gad kyi gnas yin pas so sor mi bzhed la
rows.english: He says that you'd be a fool to take your horse and train him on one cross-country course when the actual race was going to be run on a different course nearby--one that you could just as well be training him on from the beginning.  That is, you'd be a fool to undertake the first two steps of learning and contemplation to nail down one subject, and then when you get to the third step of meditation to switch to some other subject.  As such, He asserts, the examination and the focus are no two separate things.

rows.acip: LAM RIM CHEN MOR GSUNGS BSHAD RGYAS PAR GNANG NAS BSHAD PA THAMS CAD LAG LEN 'KHYER SHES PA DKA' BAS SKYONG TSUL GUD PA RE YANG BYA'O, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR NA 'DIR RDZOGS RIM GSUM PO LA YANG DANG PO BSHAD PA MANG LA PHYI MA GNYIS NYUNG NGU LAS MED PAS CHA MI SNYOMS PA 'JUG PAS CHA SNYOMS TE SGRO 'DOGS GCOD PA DANG NYAMS LEN SEMS 'DZIN GYI BYA BA GNYIS 'BYUNG YANG, RANG GI GO YUL DANG BSTUN PA 'DI LTAR,
rows.wylie: lam rim chen mor gsungs bshad rgyas par gnang nas bshad pa thams cad lag len 'khyer shes pa dka' bas skyong tshul gud pa re yang bya'o, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar na 'dir rdzogs rim gsum po la yang dang po bshad pa mang la phyi ma gnyis nyung ngu las med pas cha mi snyoms pa 'jug pas cha snyoms te sgro 'dogs gcod pa dang nyams len sems 'dzin gyi bya ba gnyis 'byung yang, rang gi go yul dang bstun pa 'di ltar
rows.english: It is though true that it is said that "When you grant a detailed teaching of the Great Book on the Steps of the Path, it is difficult to undertake--during that same period--actual practical sessions on each and every one of the subjects as they are presented; and so, one should later go through them in sessions apart from the teaching."  In the same way, you will find here that as far as the three practices of the stage of completion we will devote more explanation to the first, but nothing more than a touch on the latter two.  It would seem then that the attention paid is unequal; but you must make it in practice equal: you should do both the examination of the subject and the practical application in the focus of the meditation, in keeping with your current understanding of each practice.

rows.acip: LAM THUN MONG BAS RGYUD SBYANGS PA, DBANG RNAM PAR DAG THOB PA, DBANG DUS SU KHAS BLANGS PA'I DAM TSIG DANG SDOM PA RNAMS SROG BSDOS KYIS BSRUNG LA, BSKYED RDZOGS LAM NYAMS SU LEN TSUL RNAMS GO RIM MA 'KHRUL BAR TSUL BZHIN DU BSTAN PA LTAR NYAMS SU BLANGS PAS
rows.wylie: lam thun mong bas rgyud sbyangs pa, dbang rnam par dag thob pa, dbang dus su khas blangs pa'i dam tshig dang sdom pa rnams srog bsdos kyis bsrung la, bskyed rdzogs lam nyams su len tshul rnams go rim ma 'khrul bar tshul bzhin du bstan pa ltar nyams su blangs pas
rows.english: The case is the same here in this practice.  Suppose a person conducts their personal practice exactly as we've described it here--properly, and without mixing up the proper order of things.  First, they train their hearts in the path which is shared by the open and secret teachings.  Then they take a pure initiation, and honor the pledges and vows which during the initiation they swore to keep--they honor them even at the cost of their life.  And then finally they undertake the paths of the stage of creation and the stage of completion.

rows.acip: ,KHA CIG RDZOGS RIM GYI SNGON 'GRO'I CHOS LA YID CHES GSUM LDAN ZHIG DGOS ZHES PA NI, RDZOGS RIM KHO NAR MA ZAD GSANG SNGAGS KYI LAM SPYI'I SNGON DU 'GRO DGOS LA, DE'ANG BLA MAS RGYUD BSHAD PA NA DE'I LEGS BSHAD MTHONG NAS RGYUD LA YID CHES LA, RGYUD NAS JI LTAR BSHAD PA'I MAN NGAG RNAMS BLA MAS BSTAN PAS BLA MA LA YID CHES SHING, MAN NGAG NYAMS SU BLANGS PAS RGYUD NAS BSHAD PA LTAR GYI RTOGS PA KHYAD PAR CAN RGYUD LA SKYES PAS RANG LA YID CHES PA GSUM MO,,
rows.wylie: kha cig rdzogs rim gyi sngon 'gro'i chos la yid ches gsum ldan zhig dgos zhes pa ni, rdzogs rim kho nar ma zad gsang sngags kyi lam spyi'i sngon du 'gro dgos la, de'ang bla mas rgyud bshad pa na de'i legs bshad mthong nas rgyud la yid ches la, rgyud nas ji ltar bshad pa'i man ngag rnams bla mas bstan pas bla ma la yid ches shing, man ngag nyams su blangs pas rgyud nas bshad pa ltar gyi rtogs pa khyad par can rgyud la skyes pas rang la yid ches pa gsum mo
rows.english: Some people say that, as a preliminary to the practice of the stage of completion, the disciple should have gained the three kinds of belief.  This though is not only a prerequisite for the stage of completion, but rather is a necessary step prior to any practice of the path of the secret word in general.  The three are the following: 1) Once the Lama has instructed the disciple in the secret teachings, the disciple must have recognized the beauty of these teachings, and come to believe in them. 2) The disciple must have come to believe in the Lama, since he or she is the one who has granted the disciple advices. 3) The disciple must have come to believe in themselves, for they have gained extraordinary realizations by putting into actual practice the teachings they have received.]

rows.acip: GRUB PA'I DBANG PHYUG JO BO N'A RO TA PAS RGYUD SDE RGYA MTSO'I SNYING PO'I BCUD PHYUNG BA'I GDAMS PA ZAB MO N'A RO CHOS DRUG TU GRAGS PA'I BSHAD KHRID, LUS SBYONG N'A RO DRUG SKOR 'BEBS KYI SKOR SOGS DANG, LAG KHRID BCAS RJE BDAG NYID CHEN PO'I GSUNG KHRID YIG YID CHES GSUM LDAN GYI STENG NAS NYAMS KHRID BZHI BSHAD KYI TSUL DU LEGS PAR THOB PA'I BRGYUD PA NI,
rows.wylie: grub pa'i dbang phyug jo bo nA ro ta pas rgyud sde rgya mtsho'i snying po'i bcud phyung ba'i gdams pa zab mo nA ro chos drug tu grags pa'i bshad khrid, lus sbyong nA ro drug skor 'bebs kyi skor sogs dang, lag khrid bcas rje bdag nyid chen po'i gsung khrid yig yid ches gsum ldan gyi steng nas nyams khrid bzhi bshad kyi tshul du legs par thob pa'i brgyud pa ni
rows.english: Here is the complete lineage for instructions I have received, in four different ways, upon what are known as the "Six Practices of Naropa"--advices that represent the inner essence drawn from the ocean of the various groups of secret teachings by that absolute lord of all accomplished saints, the Lord, Narotapa.  I have received commentarial teachings; instructions on the various practices of the body among the six, on how substances descend and so forth; teachings through private demonstrations; and experiential teachings based on the presentation by the Lord, the Great Being Tsongkapa, entitled The Book of Three Beliefs.

rows.wylie: 7yang zab lam nA ro chos drug gi khrid yig, dga' ldan nag tshang blo bzang bstan pa dar rgyas kyis mdzad pa'i yig cha'i steng nas nyams khrid zab mo lus sbyong nA ro drug skor gyi lag khrid dang bcas pa legs par nos pa'i brgyud pa ni, nag tshang rdo rje 'chang bstan pa dar rgyas, tre hor khang gsar skyabs mgon blo bzang tshul khrims bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan, nags shod stag phu rdo rje 'chang ngag dbang blo bzang dpal bzang ldan 'jam dpal bstan pa'i dngos grub dpal bzang po'i zhal snga nas, bdag la dgyes bzhin du stsal to
rows.english: There is also the lineage through which the book of instructions on the deep path of the Six Practices of Naropa--along with the profound teachings of personal experience based on the text composed by Lobsang Tenpa Dargye of the Naktsang College of Ganden, and the private instructions on the practices of the body known as the six topics of Naropa--has been imparted so well: 1) The Keeper of the Diamond from Naktsang, Tenpa Dargye 2) Lobsang Tsultrim Tenpay Gyeltsen, our Refuge and Protector, from the New House of Trehor College (aka Drupkangpa, 1848-?) 3) The Good and Glorious Ngawang Lobsang of Takpu, Keeper of the Diamond, from Nakshu College; the Good and Glorious Jampel Tenpay Ngudrup 4) And from his holy lips, granted joyfully to myself.]

rows.acip: DE LA YANG THOG MAR TSE 'DI LA BLO MA LDOG NA THEG PA CHE CHUNG GANG GI YANG LAM GYI GEGS YIN PAS, TSE 'DIR RING DU MI GNAS PA'I 'CHI BA DRAN PA DANG, SHI BA'I 'OG TU NGAN 'GROR 'KHYAMS PA'I TSUL RNAMS BSAMS NAS, TSE 'DI LA BLO LDOG PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: de la yang thog mar tshe 'di la blo ma ldog na theg pa che chung gang gi yang lam gyi gegs yin pas, tshe 'dir ring du mi gnas pa'i 'chi ba dran pa dang, shi ba'i 'og tu ngan 'gror 'khyams pa'i tshul rnams bsams nas, tshe 'di la blo ldog par bya'o
rows.english: On this same point, it's a great obstacle to every kind of path--whether we're talking about the greater way or the lesser way--if you are unable, at the very outset, to prevent the state of mind which is focussing on the goals of this present life.  You should therefore try to stay aware of the fact that you will not be staying here in this life very long--you will die.  Think too of how then, after you die, you may have to wander in the lower realms.  We thus stop any thought of concentrating on this life.

rows.acip: DE'I 'OG TU RANG NYID ZHI BDE'I SEMS BZLOG PA'I PHYIR DU, BYAMS PA DANG SNYING RJE DANG DE'I RTZA BA CAN GYI BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS LA RING DU SBYANGS NAS, BCOS MA MA YIN PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS SBYANG BAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: de'i 'og tu rang nyid zhi bde'i sems bzlog pa'i phyir du, byams pa dang snying rje dang de'i rtsa ba can gyi byang chub kyi sems la ring du sbyangs nas, bcos ma ma yin pa'i byang chub kyi sems sbyang bar bya'o
rows.english: After this, work to prevent any idea of concentrating only on your own happiness.  This is done by devoting much time to training yourself in thoughts of love, and compassion, and the Wish for enlightenment rooted in these two.  Work finally to bring this Wish to the point where it comes to you in a perfectly natural way, not something you have to try to feel artificially.

rows.wylie: rdo rje sems dpa'i zhal nas, rigs kyi bu khyod kyi sdig sgrib dang, dam tshig nyams chags thams cad dag go, zhes gsungs nas rang la thim pas, rang gi sgo gsum dang rdo rje sems dpa'i sku gsung thugs dbyer med du gyur par bsams la, dge rtsa bsngo ba dang smon lam gdab po
rows.english: And the Warrior of Diamond says to you, Child of my family, you are pure, pure of your past bad deeds and obstacles, pure of all the pledges you have ever broken. Next dedicate the good karma you have collected, and make final prayers.

rows.acip: THEG PA 'DI LA GANG SNANG LHA'I 'KHOR LO DANG, NYAMS MYONG BDE BA CHEN PO, RTOG PA SKYE MED KYIS RGYAS 'DEBS PA CIG DGOS PA YANG RIM PA DANG PO NAS 'BYUNG LA, SROG DH'U T'IR TSUD PA LAS BYUNG BA'I RDZOGS RIM PA'I BDE CHEN SKABS 'DIR MED KYANG, YAB YUM DNGOS LTA BU'I GSAL SNANG SHIN TU BRTAN PA RNYED PAS, DE 'DRA BA'I THABS SHES MNYAM PAR SBYAR ZHING, PHAt YIG GIS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS PHYIR 'PHO BA BKAG PA LAS BYUNG BA'I BSKYED RIM PA'I BDE CHEN DU MA ZHIG 'BYUNG BA SHES DGOS SO, ,DKYIL 'KHOR GYI 'KHOR LO'I BSKYED RIM BSGOMS PAS RGYUD SMIN PAR BYED PA'I GTZO BO NI 'DI NYID YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: theg pa 'di la gang snang lha'i 'khor lo dang, nyams myong bde ba chen po, rtog pa skye med kyis rgyas 'debs pa cig dgos pa yang rim pa dang po nas 'byung la, srog dhU tIr tshud pa las byung ba'i rdzogs rim pa'i bde chen skabs 'dir med kyang, yab yum dngos lta bu'i gsal snang shin tu brtan pa rnyed pas, de 'dra ba'i thabs shes mnyam par sbyar zhing, phaT yig gis byang chub kyi sems phyir 'pho ba bkag pa las byung ba'i bskyed rim pa'i bde chen du ma zhig 'byung ba shes dgos so, ,dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo'i bskyed rim bsgoms pas rgyud smin par byed pa'i gtso bo ni 'di nyid yin no
rows.english: Here in the way of the secret word, the need to see everything around you as a world of the divine, and to feel all that you experience as ecstasy, and to carve the mark of unborn emptiness into every thought you have, is something that applies to the first of the two stages too.  It is true that at this juncture in the practice there is not yet that experience of ecstasy which comes during the stage of completion, when you manage to get the life wind to enter the channel of vibration; suppose, nonetheless, that you are able to reach a point where you can maintain a very clear vision of a divine man and wife, as real as life itself.  And suppose that this wisdom/method couple join together, using the sacred word of phet to prevent the element of enlightenment from coming out. It's important that you realize that there are a great many different forms of ecstasy that can happen to you this way, at the stage of creation.  This is in fact the single most important point in following the practice of the stage of creation, the universe of a secret world, to prepare your mind for what comes further on.

rows.acip: DE LTAR MTSAN MAR 'DZIN PA BDEN 'DZIN GYI DMIGS GTAD RDUL TZAM YANG MA GRUB KYANG, LAS 'BRAS LA SOGS PA'I RGYU 'BRAS KYI 'KHOR 'DAS KYI BYA BYED THAMS CAD NYAMS PA MED PA SGYU MA DANG, RMI LAM DANG GZUGS BRNYAN GYI BYA BYED BZHIN DU 'CHAR BA YOD DO,,
rows.wylie: de ltar mtshan mar 'dzin pa bden 'dzin gyi dmigs gtad rdul tsam yang ma grub kyang, las 'bras la sogs pa'i rgyu 'bras kyi 'khor 'das kyi bya byed thams cad nyams pa med pa sgyu ma dang, rmi lam dang gzugs brnyan gyi bya byed bzhin du 'char ba yod do
rows.english: Now although it is true to say thus that there exists not even an atom of what our tendency to see things as real (our tendency to take the indications as the object) centers itself upon, this is not to imply at all that all the workings of things, whether they be in the circle of suffering or beyond it--that is, cause and effect itself, as expressed in phenomena such as deeds and their consequences--is in any way diminished.  There is something that appears as if it were the workings of things, albeit in the way of a magic trick, or a dream, or a reflection in a mirror.

rows.acip: RJE BTZUN MID LA'I GDAMS NGAG TU, GDAMS PA 'DI LA BSKYED RIM DANG, GTUM MO DANG LAS RGYA DANG, GNAS LUGS LTA BA'I DON GO BA DANG, MTSON BYED LAM GYI 'OD GSAL, MTSON BYED LAM GYI SGYU MA RMI LAM DANG DON DRUG TU BSDUS NAS, RJE LHO BRAG MAR PA'I THUGS KYI BCUD PHYUNG BA, SNYAN BRGYUD DON GYI NGO SPROD THABS LAM GNAD KYI MTHAR THUG KYANG DE LAS MED DO, ,RNAL 'BYOR PA DE'I DGONGS PA ZHE PHUGS BLO'I GDENG, 'PHRAL NYAMS SU BLANGS RGYU DE LAS MED,
rows.wylie: rje btsun mid la'i gdams ngag tu, gdams pa 'di la bskyed rim dang, gtum mo dang las rgya dang, gnas lugs lta ba'i don go ba dang, mtshon byed lam gyi 'od gsal, mtshon byed lam gyi sgyu ma rmi lam dang don drug tu bsdus nas, rje lho brag mar pa'i thugs kyi bcud phyung ba, snyan brgyud don gyi ngo sprod thabs lam gnad kyi mthar thug kyang de las med do, ,rnal 'byor pa de'i dgongs pa zhe phugs blo'i gdeng, 'phral nyams su blangs rgyu de las med
rows.english: The holy Milarepa's advices on this practice also organize the instructions into six parts: the stage of creation; inner fire and the actual consort; learning the meaning of the correct view of reality; the approximate clear light, that of the path; the approximate body of illusion, also during the path; and the practice of dreams.  And He said that there is nothing more than these: they are the very essence distilled from all the holy thoughts of the Lord of Hlodrak, Marpa; they are the ultimate keys of the skilful path, a direct introduction into the very pith of the oral lineage.  This is the ultimate idea within the heart of this deep practitioner, His ultimate affirmation.  And even in a short-term sense there is nothing better practiced than this.

rows.wylie: de tsam bsgoms pa yang bskyed rim pa'i bde chen 'bar ba'i thabs su 'gyur mod, 'on kyang lcang skya rin po ches rdzogs rim gyi bde chen 'dren pa la rtsa gsum 'khor lo bzhi sogs gsal btab nas 'bar 'dzag bsgom na shin tu legs par gsungs pa'i dgongs pa ltar bdag gi rje bla mas kyang rgyas par nyams su len tshul dang, bsre ba skor gsum sogs kyang skabs 'gar gsung ngo
rows.english: Admittedly, even if you only meditate on this, it becomes a means of igniting great bliss for a person on the stage of creation.  However, it has been stated by the Precious Chankya that in order to elicit the great bliss of the completion stage, it is extremely good if we meditate on the blazing and dripping, while visualizing the three channels, the four chakras, and so on.  And this thought is shared by our own Lord and Lama, who has extensively explained this on several occasions, in his topics such as how to put this into practice, and the three stages of mixing. *  *  *  *  * Our third selection is drawn from Lama Quicksilver's Secret Treasure of the Angels:

rows.acip: SLAR YANG ME CHER SONG HAm YIG LA PHOG BYANG SEMS 'O RKYAL MDUNG GIS PHUG PA BZHIN SKYA NAR GYIS BYUNG GTUM MO'I ME LA THIM PAS ME MAR SNON PA LTAR ME JE CHER SONG BYANG SEMS LA PHOG ,PHYIR 'GRO BA'I TSUL GYIS HAm YIG LA THIM, SLAR YANG CHER 'DZAG ME LA THIM PA YAR MAR DU 'DZING RAL BYED PA'I TSUL GYIS BYANG SEMS 'BAR 'DZAG LA SEMS 'DZIN, RGYAS PAR BYED NA BSRE BA BSKOR GSUM SOGS N'A RO CHOS DRUG NAS BSHAD PA LTAR NYAMS SU LEN NO,,
rows.wylie: slar yang me cher song haM yig la phog byang sems 'o rkyal mdung gis phug pa bzhin skya nar gyis byung gtum mo'i me la thim pas me mar snon pa ltar me je cher song byang sems la phog ,phyir 'gro ba'i tshul gyis haM yig la thim, slar yang cher 'dzag me la thim pa yar mar du 'dzing ral byed pa'i tshul gyis byang sems 'bar 'dzag la sems 'dzin, rgyas par byed na bsre ba bskor gsum sogs nA ro chos drug nas bshad pa ltar nyams su len no
rows.english: Then the fire rebounds in greater force; it blazes up and pierces the ham letter like a spear piercing a bag of milk.  A viscous stream of white element comes out and sinks into the flame of inner fire.  At first again the fire is suppressed, but then it blazes back even greater and penetrates the white element, pushing it back into the ham letter.  This causes the white element to drip down even more, sinking into the fire.  Hold your mind on this up-and-down, back-and-forth struggle between the two forces: on what we call the "blaze and drip."  If you want to do this in a more extensive way, you could also do the three rounds of mixing, or other practices, as taught in the Six Practices of Naropa. *  *  *  *  *  * Our final presentation is excerpted from Pabongka Rinpoche Dechen Nyingpo's Heart Essence of the Angels:

rows.acip: LCANG SKYA ROL RDOR GYI DGONGS PAR, ZHAR BYUNG RDZOGS RIM DANG PO LAS YID BZLAS DMIGS RTEN PHRA BA'I GNAD KYIS ZHAR BYUNG RDZOGS RIM DANG PO BSGOMS NAS YID BZLAS BYA BA RDZOGS RIM GYI RGYUD SMIN BYED MCHOG TU 'GYUR TSUL GSUNGS PA BDAG NYID CHEN POS THUGS NYAMS SU BZHES NAS RGYUD DON GDAMS NGAG TU SHAR BA'I GSUNG YIN PAS DNGUL CHU YAB SRAS KYIS KYANG DE BZHIN MDZAD LA,
rows.wylie: lcang skya rol rdor gyi dgongs par, zhar byung rdzogs rim dang po las yid bzlas dmigs rten phra ba'i gnad kyis zhar byung rdzogs rim dang po bsgoms nas yid bzlas bya ba rdzogs rim gyi rgyud smin byed mchog tu 'gyur tshul gsungs pa bdag nyid chen pos thugs nyams su bzhes nas rgyud don gdams ngag tu shar ba'i gsung yin pas dngul chu yab sras kyis kyang de bzhin mdzad la
rows.english: The visualization of the mental recitation though is more subtle than that of the first of the incidental practices of the stage of completion.  In the profound thinking of Changkya Rolpay Dorje, this is a crucial point which means that, if we carry out the former incidental practice of the completion stage first and then go on to the mental recitation, it will provide the very best possible means of ripening our mental stream for the stage of completion.  His statement to this effect, in the considered opinion of the Great Being, reflected a case where the intent of the secret teaching had shown itself to the author as private revelation.  As such, the great Father and Son--Ngulchu and His disciple--carried Their practice out in this same way as well.

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, MDUN GYI NAM MKHA' LA RTZA BA'I BLA MA BRGYUD PA'I BLA MA DANG BCAS PA, DPA' BO DANG MKHA' 'GRO'I TSOGS KYIS BSKOR BAR DMIGS LA, LUS LONGS SPYOD LTOS PA MED PAR MCHOD PA DBUL ZHING, SPYIR GSOL BA MANG DU GDAB, KHYAD PAR DU RLUNG BDE RTZA 'JAM, BDE STONG GI NYAMS RTOGS KHYAD PAR CAN SKYE PA'I GSOL BA DRAG TU GDAB,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, mdun gyi nam mkha' la rtsa ba'i bla ma brgyud pa'i bla ma dang bcas pa, dpa' bo dang mkha' 'gro'i tshogs kyis bskor bar dmigs la, lus longs spyod ltos pa med par mchod pa dbul zhing, spyir gsol ba mang du gdab, khyad par du rlung bde rtsa 'jam, bde stong gi nyams rtogs khyad par can skye pa'i gsol ba drag tu gdab
rows.english: Here is the first.  First picture, in mid-air, in front of you, your root Lama, along with the Lamas of the lineage.  See Them surrounded by a mass of Warriors and Angels.  Then imagine taking your body and your possessions and offering them as a gift to these beings, with no hesitation--no regard to how dear these objects might be to you. Be sure, as a general rule, to make many fervent requests to these beings for their assistance.  Most especially, bring your inner winds down to a very comfortable level, and your channels into a smooth state.  Make a particularly strong request for these beings' help in reaching a very high level of realizing bliss and voidness.

rows.acip: DE NAS NAM MKHA' DANG MNYAM PA'I SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI DON DU RDO RJE 'CHANG GI GO 'PHANG THOB PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR TZAndA LI NYAMS SU BLANG SNYAM DU BSAM ZHING, BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS RGYUD DANG 'DRES NGES PA BSGOM,
rows.wylie: de nas nam mkha' dang mnyam pa'i sems can thams cad kyi don du rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang thob par bya ba'i phyir tsaNDa li nyams su blang snyam du bsam zhing, byang chub kyi sems rgyud dang 'dres nges pa bsgom
rows.english: Then decide to yourself that you will attain the state of the Keeper of the Diamond, for the sake of all living beings, who are equal in extent to space itself.  "And for this," think to yourself, "I will now undertake the practice of chandali."  Go into your meditation with a state of mind which is completely melded together with the Wish for enlightenment.

rows.acip: MKHAN CHEN NGAG DBANG CHOS GRAGS KYIS BDE STONG SKYE TSUL 'DI DANG GO LDOG TU GSUNGS, BLA MA'I KHRID RGYUN GONG LTAR THOB CING, NGAG 'DON DU DMIGS RIM BKOD PA YANG MKHAN CHEN GYI GSUNG LA NYE CAR BA YOD, SKYES PAS MKHAN CHEN LTAR DANG, BUD MED KYIS GONG LTAR NYAMS SU BLANG NA CHOG GAM SNYAM PAS BRTAG GO, ,
rows.wylie: mkhan chen ngag dbang chos grags kyis bde stong skye tshul 'di dang go ldog tu gsungs, bla ma'i khrid rgyun gong ltar thob cing, ngag 'don du dmigs rim bkod pa yang mkhan chen gyi gsung la nye car ba yod, skyes pas mkhan chen ltar dang, bud med kyis gong ltar nyams su blang na chog gam snyam pas brtag go,
rows.english: Kenchen Ngawang Chudrak has said that the way in which the experiences of bliss and emptiness arises is the opposite as I have described above.  The way I've described it here though is the way in which I received this teaching from the Lamas of our lineage.  It is true however that the way this practice is written down in the recitation text is close to how Kenchen describes it.  I think it would be okay if men were to practice it in the way that Kenchen described, and if women were to do so as described here; but you should look into this and research it later  yourselves--it's a point to be further checked. *  *  *  *  *  * Our final presentation is excerpted from Pabongka Rinpoche Dechen Nyingpo's Heart Essence of the Angels:

rows.acip: RLUNG GI RNAM BZHAG LA BRTEN NAS NYAMS LEN GYI GNAD SHES TSUL NI, GSAL SGRON LAS, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR RANG BZHIN GYI RTOG PA G-YO MI G-YO BA'I 'TSAMS SU STONG PA BZHI 'CHAR BA SHES NAS RIM PA DE LTAR RGYUD LA SKYED PA'I PHYIR DU RDOR BZLAS LA SOGS PA'I SROL RTZOL BSGOM DGOS PAR SHES PA NI, RLUNG BSHAD PA LA RTEN NAS NYAMS LEN GYI GNAD SHES PA BLA NA MED PA'O,
rows.wylie: rlung gi rnam bzhag la brten nas nyams len gyi gnad shes tshul ni, gsal sgron las, sngar bshad pa ltar rang bzhin gyi rtog pa g-yo mi g-yo ba'i 'tshams su stong pa bzhi 'char ba shes nas rim pa de ltar rgyud la skyed pa'i phyir du rdor bzlas la sogs pa'i srol rtsol bsgom dgos par shes pa ni, rlung bshad pa la rten nas nyams len gyi gnad shes pa bla na med pa'o
rows.english: Suppose we do learn about the inner winds. How then shall we actually practice with them? Here there are a few crucial points you need to know. As the Lamp of Illumination puts it, You need to learn to reach that Dividing line, the place between Where the misperceptions of reality Are stirring and stopped. This is where the four forms of emptiness Make their appearance. Once you grasp this fact, you want To actually do something to bring These stages on. What you must understand here is that it is essential that you enter practices like the recitation of diamond: practices where you are working with the life-winds. This single understanding of how to proceed is an unsurpassed grasp of the crucial points of actual practice that we need to know, once we have learned about the structure of the inner winds. [Note: The phrase "working with the life-winds" here is a translation of the Sanskrit word pranayama.] The following translation is an excerpt from Master Chone Drakpa Shedrup--his explanation on the practice of the completion stage according to the system of the five stages that is found in the teachings of the Glorious Secret Collecion (Guhyasamaja), entitled: A Book to Please Those with the Core of Goodness.  This excerpt can be found in the ACIP database, text S0260, folios 5A-5B. *************** How the Winds First Form

rows.acip: SHIN TU 'TSER BA'I 'OD CAN BSGOMS NA, BYING BA GCOD SLA ZHING TING NGE 'DZIN GSAL NYAMS CHE'O,,
rows.wylie: shin tu 'tsher ba'i 'od can bsgoms na, bying ba gcod sla zhing ting nge 'dzin gsal nyams che'o
rows.english: If furthermore you picture them as sparkling in strong light, then you will find it easy to stop any mental dullness; you'll experience a much greater clarity of meditation.

rows.acip: DMIGS PA DE RNAMS LA SEMS 'DZIN TSUL NI, DMIGS RTEN PHRA MO'I NANG DU SEMS ZHUGS PA'I TSUL GYIS 'DZIN PAR GSUNGS PAS, TSUR NGOS NAS PHAR LA LTA BA'I RNAM PAR MI BYA'I, YUL CAN GYI SEMS YUL DE'I NANG DU 'DRES PA BZHIN DU BYA STE, SKYONG TSUL 'DI LTAR BYAS NA DA GZOD SEMS THIG LE DANG 'DRES PAR 'GYUR BA'I NYAMS SKYES NAS RLUNG 'DU BAR SHIN TU SLA'O,,
rows.wylie: dmigs pa de rnams la sems 'dzin tshul ni, dmigs rten phra mo'i nang du sems zhugs pa'i tshul gyis 'dzin par gsungs pas, tshur ngos nas phar la lta ba'i rnam par mi bya'i, yul can gyi sems yul de'i nang du 'dres pa bzhin du bya ste, skyong tshul 'di ltar byas na da gzod sems thig le dang 'dres par 'gyur ba'i nyams skyes nas rlung 'du bar shin tu sla'o
rows.english: Here is a note on how you keep your mind on these various objects of your meditation.  The scriptures say that you should do so in a way that allows your mind to actually enter these objects.  This means that you never imagine yourself over here looking over there; rather, you should think that your subject state of mind has flowed into the object it is focused upon and mixed with it. If you keep up the visualization this way, then you will begin to get the feeling that your mind is mixed even deeper within the tiny circle; and it will be that much easier to gather in the winds.

If you keep up the visualization this way, then you will begin to get the feeling that your mind is mixed even deeper within the tiny circle; and it will be that much easier to gather in the winds."}

rows.english: The actual process of putting this path of the central channel into practice is one idea, commonly expressed by means of three examples.5  This process has three stages: the original condition, the path, and the result.  For the path, there are two ways of teaching someone: teaching them the true nature of things directly, and teaching it through a medium.  For the latter way, teaching through a medium, there are two different methods: the path which is free of desire, and the path which embraces desire.

rows.acip: DE LTA BU'I SGO NAS NYAMS SU BLANG NA DBANG PO RAB KYIS ZHAG GSUM, 'BRING GIS ZHAG BDUN, THA MAS ZLA BA PHYED DU BSGOM NA SA CHU'I RLUNG STOBS BRI, ME RLUNG GI RLUNG STOBS RGYAS NAS LUS LA DROD CHE, GRANG SRAN CHE, LCE SKAM, SKOM DAD CHE BA SOGS 'BYUNG BAR GSUNGS SO,

rows.english: If you practice like this, the power of the earth and water elements decreases, and the power of the elements of fire and wind increases. rows.acip: 'ON KYANG BOD KYI BLA MA RNAMS KYIS GTUM MO'I MAN NGAG LA RTZA DANG YI GE SGOM PA RLUNG BUM PA CAN DANG SBRAGS NAS BYED PA MANG BAR BYUNG BA NI, GTUM MO'I NYAMS MYONG SKYE BA MYUR BA'I CHED DU MDZAD SNANG BA BZHIN 'DIR YANG BSHAD NA,

rows.english: There have though been many Lamas in Tibet who undertook the practice of inner fire along with the practices of the channels; picturing the syllables; and holding the capsule of wind.  The reason that They did so appears to be the fact that this allows you to gain experiences of inner fire much more quickly than otherwise; as such, we will cover the practice of the capsule here as well.

rows.english: When you undertake the practice of the capsule of wind, the important details of your bodily posture and so on are the same as before.  As for the time of day when you should do the practice, Pakmo Druppa's book of instructions says, Certain Lamas have said that one should do the practice at times of the day when the winds run equally by nature; but when you are really trying to carry this out in a practical way you should meditate all the time, night and day.

rows.english: If you are able to maintain this solid state of mind, you'll reach a state of meditation where the light from rays of inner fire fill your body, both inside and outside, and then your whole room, and more; see them shine as clearly as a pea in the palm of your hand.  It's extremely important at this point that you hold your mind on this vision, all from the fine, single tongue of flame.  Keep this up and you'll experience a higher level in the clarity of your concentration; you'll quickly reach the culmination of meditation.

rows.english: We move on now to our second part: how it is that the four kinds of bliss are brought on through the meltdown of the element of enlightenment.  Here is how the four types of bliss arise, coming down, as the element of enlightenment melts down and reaches different places.  The secret teaching called The String of Diamonds says: Following that we explain How they come going forward: It's said that what you get At the tip of the head, In the chakra of great bliss, Is what we call "ecstasy." At the chakra of experience Is the one called "high ecstasy"; At the chakra of the dharma Is the "ecstasy of abandonment," And the ecstasy that you come to experience In the chakra of emanation Is called the "simultaneous."

rows.english: These four sections can also be divided into three each: think of it as three separate experiences of pleasure, in either a lesser, a medium, or a greater form, as the droplets--of the blood--move.  Each of these seems to be a very subtle distinction.

rows.wylie: spyir lam bsgoms ma bsgoms gnyis ka la, byang sems zhu ba gsang gnas su babs pa las byung ba'i dga' ba nyams su myong ba la ni, nges par lte ba dang gsang gnas kyi gtum mo 'bar nas zhu ba cig 'ong bas, gtum mo 'bar nas byang sems 'ju ba la, srog dhU tIr thim pa sogs mi dgos so
rows.english: Generally speaking, an experience of bliss occurs both with those who have trained themselves in the path and with those who have not, as the element of enlightenment melts down and moves to the private place.  And it is always the case that this occurs because you have gotten the inner fire to burn at the navel and the private place.  As such, it is not the case that you necessarily have to get the life wind to dissolve into the central channel in order to get the inner fire to blaze up and melt down the element of enlightenment.

rows.acip: RLUNG 'DU SLA BA MIN PAR ZHU BDE'I NYAMS SKYE SLA BA 'GA' ZHIG LA 'BAR 'DZAG BSGOMS NA, BYANG SEMS ZHU BA MYUR DU 'BAB PA 'ONG BAS, DE LA NI ZHU BA SHAS CHUNG NA MA GTOGS PA GNAS MTHON PO NAS MA LDOG NA, DMA' MO NAS SHIN TU LDOG DKA' BA DANG,
rows.wylie: rlung 'du sla ba min par zhu bde'i nyams skye sla ba 'ga' zhig la 'bar 'dzag bsgoms na, byang sems zhu ba myur du 'bab pa 'ong bas, de la ni zhu ba shas chung na ma gtogs pa gnas mthon po nas ma ldog na, dma' mo nas shin tu ldog dka' ba dang
rows.english: Now there are certain individuals for whom gathering in the winds is no easy task, but who nonetheless readily feel sensations of bliss associated with the meltdown of the element.  If people like this do the practice of the flame-up and the drip-down, it can happen that the element of enlightenment melts and moves down quite quickly. rows.acip: GANG ZAG PHYI MA GNYIS KYIS NI 'CHI BA LA NYE BA'I SNGON RIG PA GSAL BA NA, ZANG ZING YONGS SU BZUNG BA THAMS CAD BSOD NAMS KYI ZHING GI PHYOGS SU LTOS PA MED PAR BLOS LINGS KYIS BTANG LA, CI LA YANG CHAGS PA MED PAR BYA, KHAS BLANGS PA'I SDOM PA DANG 'GAL BA'I NYES LTUNG RNAMS LA BSHAGS BSDAMS DANG, DAM TSIG NYAMS CHAG SOR GZHUG LA, DA NI SHI NA'ANG SHI MOD SNYAM DU YID LA GCAGS PA MED PAR BYA,
rows.wylie: gang zag phyi ma gnyis kyis ni 'chi ba la nye ba'i sngon rig pa gsal ba na, zang zing yongs su bzung ba thams cad bsod nams kyi zhing gi phyogs su ltos pa med par blos lings kyis btang la, ci la yang chags pa med par bya, khas blangs pa'i sdom pa dang 'gal ba'i nyes ltung rnams la bshags bsdams dang, dam tshig nyams chag sor gzhug la, da ni shi na'ang shi mod snyam du yid la gcags pa med par bya
rows.english: Now the latter two types of individuals, as they approach death (and assuming their minds are still clear), completely release mentally every single material object in their possession, dedicating them without the slightest hesitation to the gardens where we plant our virtues.  They thus free themselves from attachment to anything at all.  They openly admit, and then commit themselves to refrain from, every negative deed or transgression they have ever committed against the vows they have sworn to keep; and then they go about restoring whatever pledges they may have broken.  With this they are ready to die without any distress at all--mentally they are in a place where they can say to themselves, "Well, now if I die, I die; everything's fine."

rows.wylie: de'i phyir gnyid kyi 'od gsal la nyams dang rtogs pa'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, srab mo dang 'thug po'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, rmi lam gyi dus su rtog med kyi ting nge 'dzin gsal dvangs byung ba yang, gnyid kyi 'od gsal du 'jog pa'i rnam gzhag mang po snang yang sngar bshad pa ltar ma phyed par gnyid ting nge 'dzin du skyed nus pa tsam gyi steng nas bshad pa mang du byas par snang bas, yid brtan thub pa mi snang ngo
rows.english: And so it is that the clear light of sleep can be discussed in terms of the two of a feeling of clear light and an actual experience of clear light; and in terms of the two of a less deep state of clear light and a deeper state of it; and in terms of a clear and lucid state of non-conceptual concentration that comes in your dreams.  And despite the fact that many presentations on the clear light of sleep have been written, a great number of them give their explanation based on nothing more than teaching the ability to turn sleep into a state of meditative concentration, without making any of the distinctions we've just mentioned.  As such it does not appear that we should accept these words as authoritative.

rows.wylie: gnyis pa rnam shes gzhan gyi grong du 'jug pa ni, mig sogs kyi dbang po la grong dang, dbang po'i rten la grong khyer gyi sgras bstan pa ni, phar phyin nas 'byung la, gang zag gzhan shi ba'i lus ma nyams pa la'ang, grong khyer gyi sgra 'jug pas rnam shes der 'jug pa la grong 'jug ces gsungs so
rows.english: This brings us to the second division in this portion of the text: an explanation of bringing our consciousness to "enter" the "city" of another's body.  The custom of referring to the eyes and other sense organs as "the village," and to the bases of these powers as "the city," is something that has come from the teachings on the perfection of wisdom.  The body of another person who has died--a body which is still fresh and has not deteriorated--is also referred to here as a "city."  And so when we send our consciousness to enter this body, it is called "entering the city."

rows.wylie: ji ltar byed pa'i tshul la 'di pa'i bla ma rnams gsum du byed pa'i dang po skyang ba ni, rlung sems gnyis la dbang thob, tshe 'dir gzhan don 'grub par mthong zhing, sems can la snying rje tshad med dang ldan pa'i gang zag gis grong du 'jug pa'i man ngag nyams su blang bar bya ste
rows.english: As for the method that we use to carry out this practice, the Lamas have outlined three different steps.  The first of these is called "extending."  For this, we must first of all be someone who has attained mastery over their winds and mind.  We must as well perceive that if we do undertake the practice in this present life then it will be of benefit to others.  And finally we must be possessed of limitless compassion for all living beings.  This is the kind of person who can carry out the instructions for entering the city.

rows.acip: DE NAS BSAD PA NI MI RO GSAR PA MA NYAMS SHING, RMA 'BRAS SOGS MED PA, RIMS DANG 'BRUM BU SOGS KYIS SHI BA MIN PA'AM, YANG NA PHYUGS LA SOGS PA'I RO GTZANG ZHING MA NYAMS PA ZHIG BTZAL LA, CHU GTZANG MAS KHRUS BYAS, YID DU 'ONG BA'I RGYAN BTAGS LA, MDUN GYI MAndAL GYI STENG DU SKYIL KRUNG NGAM LUS LEGS PAR BCOS LA BZHAG,
rows.wylie: de nas bsad pa ni mi ro gsar pa ma nyams shing, rma 'bras sogs med pa, rims dang 'brum bu sogs kyis shi ba min pa'am, yang na phyugs la sogs pa'i ro gtsang zhing ma nyams pa zhig btsal la, chu gtsang mas khrus byas, yid du 'ong ba'i rgyan btags la, mdun gyi maNDal gyi steng du skyil krung ngam lus legs par bcos la bzhag
rows.english: This brings us to the second step, called "killing."  We are looking for a fresh, human corpse; one which has not deteriorated.  It should be without open sores, pustules, or anything of the like.  The person should not have died through something such as a contagion or pox.  Alternately you can seek out a very clean, dead body of for example a cow; again, the body should not have deteriorated.  Wash the body in water which is pure, and apply attractive ornaments to it.  Place the body upon the mandala platform in front of you, either putting it into a cross-legged position, or any other good position.

rows.acip: DE NAS RANG DANG RO GNYIS KA'I SNYING GAR SEMS KYI RTEN YI GE H'Um RE BSAMS LA, RANG GI SNYING KHA'I H'Um DE RLUNG PHYIR 'GRO BA DANG SDONGS NAS SNA BUG GA YAS NAS 'THON TE, RO'I SNA BUG GA YON NAS ZHUGS NAS SNYING KHA'I H'Um LA THIM PAR BSAM MO, ,DE LTAR YANG YANG BYAS PAS RO'I LUS LA DBUGS DANG, DRI LA SOGS PA BYUNG NA 'BYONGS PA YIN PAS NYAMS 'OG TU TSUD DO,,
rows.wylie: de nas rang dang ro gnyis ka'i snying gar sems kyi rten yi ge hUM re bsams la, rang gi snying kha'i hUM de rlung phyir 'gro ba dang sdongs nas sna bug ga yas nas 'thon te, ro'i sna bug ga yon nas zhugs nas snying kha'i hUM la thim par bsam mo, ,de ltar yang yang byas pas ro'i lus la dbugs dang, dri la sogs pa byung na 'byongs pa yin pas nyams 'og tu tshud do
rows.english: Now picture, at both your own heart and that of the corpse, a hung letter which serves as the support of the mind.  The hung letter at your own heart accompanies the wind during the exhale, passing out of the right nostril.  Picture that this then enters into the left nostril of the corpse, sinking into the hung letter at its own heart.  When you have repeated this over and over, and then the corpse begins to breathe--and begins emit the smells and so on of a living person--then you have completed this part of the practice, and the body takes on awareness.

rows.english: As such, we can say as well that--even though there is some period here between the time that our consciousness exits our old body and the time that it enters the city--neither is there any real "being during the time between death and rebirth."  And therefore it is not the case either that we have failed in our vows, with regard to our previous body, by rejecting our earlier spiritual intentions, or anything of the like.

rows.english: To the right of the central Angel Runs another mule, Yellow in color, And atop it comes a bhyoh. This then turns into The Goddess of Prosperity. rows.english: O Goddesses of Peace, of Prosperity, Of Power, of Ferocity, May it please Your precious heart. O Lady of Secret Practice, Secret more than secret, Woman of ferocity, May it please Your precious heart. And now that Your holy hearts are pleased, Now that I've restored the pledges I broke, Then come and clear my obstacles, And grant all my attainments. With these lines, you have offered the things which please Their hearts.

rows.english: If you are someone who has a liking for performing the rite of protection of the torma offering, then recite the following lines: Bhyoh! The high flesh is piled In masses like mountains; The rakta is gathered In pools like oceans. Accept then we beg You This torma cake Of the substances of pledge; Raise your armies of spirits And lead them to the foe-- Lead them against the enemy, Against those of broken pledges: Those who would try to prevent All of our spiritual progress, The multitude of fiends Who seek to do us harm. Bring in being your forces, Raise Your sword Of human bone.

rows.english: Out of a state of emptiness Comes a long, black hung letter; It melts, and transforms Into a demon pit, Complete in every respect. Down inside it appear, Before our very eyes, The enemies of practice Who have broken their pledges, Who have broken ni and tri. Their forms are tall and thin, They stand in a pose of pain, Limbs bound in iron shackles.

rows.acip: DE YANG GZHI LAM 'BRAS GSUM, NYAMS LEN GYI MTSAMS, LUS GNAD 'CHA' TSUL, STONG RA BSGOM TSUL, LUS NANG DU RTZA GSUM GSAL 'DEBS TSUL SOGS ZHIB PAR ZIN BRIS SU GSUNGS PA LTAR SHES PAR BYAS LA, DNGOS GZHI LTE BA'I THAD KYI RTZA GSUM SBUBS GCIG TU GYUR PA'I NANG GI DBUS SU GNAS PA'I ZLA TSES THIG LE N'A DA DANG BCAS PA'I Rm YIG DMAR NAG CHE CHUNG RIL MA TZAM GDAN MED PA,
rows.wylie: de yang gzhi lam 'bras gsum, nyams len gyi mtshams, lus gnad 'cha' tshul, stong ra bsgom tshul, lus nang du rtsa gsum gsal 'debs tshul sogs zhib par zin bris su gsungs pa ltar shes par byas la, dngos gzhi lte ba'i thad kyi rtsa gsum sbubs gcig tu gyur pa'i nang gi dbus su gnas pa'i zla tshes thig le nA da dang bcas pa'i rM yig dmar nag che chung ril ma tsam gdan med pa
rows.english: Now as for the instructions on the three of the original condition, path, and result; undertaking a deep retreat; the way to arrange the body for sitting; how to meditate on the empty shell; and how to visualize the three channels inside the body, these have all been described in detail in the Notes, and you can learn what to do from there.  Here is the main practice.  At the plane of the navel is the place where the three channels turn into one hollow tube.  In the center of this tube sits the letter ram [ram%], along with its crescent, sphere, and nada.  This letter is a mix of red and black, about the size of a rabbit pellet.  It is not supported by anything underneath.

rows.acip: DE LAS DGA' LDAN NAG TSANG BSTAN DAR BAS CHOS DRUG GI DMAR KHRID ZUR DU MDZAD PA'I THOG NAS NYAMS KHRID KYI RGYUN RJE NYID KYIS STAG PHU RDO RJE 'CHANG LAS GSAN GSUNGS,

rows.acip: GZHUNG DU 'GO'I SKYABS SEMS DANG 'DZIN MED DU 'JOG PA MU STEGS BYED KYI GTUM MO DANG KHYAD PAR 'BYED TSUL GSUNGS KYANG , DE LTAR NA GTUM MO DNGOS GZHI MU STEGS BYED DANG MNYAMS PAR 'GRO BAS RTZA GSAL 'DEBS PA SOGS KHYAD PAR DU 'PHAGS PA YOD PAS LAM GYI CHA PHYED PA GAL CHE'O,,
rows.wylie: gzhung du 'go'i skyabs sems dang 'dzin med du 'jog pa mu stegs byed kyi gtum mo dang khyad par 'byed tshul gsungs kyang , de ltar na gtum mo dngos gzhi mu stegs byed dang mnyams par 'gro bas rtsa gsal 'debs pa sogs khyad par du 'phags pa yod pas lam gyi cha phyed pa gal che'o
rows.english: In the text, it states that staying in our meditation at the outset, going over refuge and the Wish but not performing any retention at this point, is what distinguishes our practice of inner fire from that followed by those of the non-Buddhist schools.  That though would imply that when we did go on to the main stage of the practice of inner fire, it would be the same as that practiced by these schools.  The fact though is that even details such as how we visualize the channels are vastly superior to the way these schools perform the practice.  As such, it is important to distinguish between different ways of carrying out each aspect of this practice.

rows.acip: DE NAS BAR DO GRUB PA'I DOD LA MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS SU LANG YANG DE NGO MA SHES PAS BAR DO GRUB, DE NI RLUNG SEMS LAS GRUB PA'I LUS MA GTOGS RAGS PA MED LA, DE'I PHYIR GNAS PA RTZA MED PA'I RLUNG RANG KHA RGYAL NAS SEMS LA RANG DBANG MI THOB PAR MING GZHI 'KHYAMS PO PHYOGS KUN TU YUD YUD 'GRO ZHING , 'KHRUL SNANG GI SDUG BSNGAL DRAG PO 'BYUNG ,
rows.wylie: de nas bar do grub pa'i dod la ma dag pa'i sgyu lus su lang yang de ngo ma shes pas bar do grub, de ni rlung sems las grub pa'i lus ma gtogs rags pa med la, de'i phyir gnas pa rtsa med pa'i rlung rang kha rgyal nas sems la rang dbang mi thob par ming gzhi 'khyams po phyogs kun tu yud yud 'gro zhing , 'khrul snang gi sdug bsngal drag po 'byung
rows.english: At this juncture we can rise up in the impure form of the illusory body, in place of going into the intermediate being--which is what happens if we fail to recognize the clear light here.  With this illusory body, there is no gross aspect at all--nothing other than a body made of wind and thought itself.  So what happens is that the inner winds--freed from their normal habitat, the channels--suddenly obtain their freedom, and unless we have attained control of our mind then we become one of those "wanderers of the basis of the name"--we set off on our aimless wandering here and there.  Then too we undergo intense suffering of mistaken perceptions.

rows.acip: GANG ZAG PHYI MA GNYIS KYIS NI 'CHI BA LA NYE BA'I SNGON RIG PA GSAL BA NA, ZANG ZING YONGS SU BZUNG BA THAMS CAD BSOD NAMS KYI ZHING GI PHYOGS SU LTOS PA MED PAR BLOS LINGS KYIS BTANG LA, CI LA YANG CHAGS PA MED PAR BYA, KHAS BLANGS PA'I SDOM PA DANG 'GAL BA'I NYES LTUNG RNAMS LA BSHAGS BSDAMS DANG, DAM TSIG NYAMS CHAG SOR GZHUG LA, DA NI SHI NA'ANG SHI MOD SNYAM DU YID LA GCAGS PA MED PAR BYA,
rows.wylie: gang zag phyi ma gnyis kyis ni 'chi ba la nye ba'i sngon rig pa gsal ba na, zang zing yongs su bzung ba thams cad bsod nams kyi zhing gi phyogs su ltos pa med par blos lings kyis btang la, ci la yang chags pa med par bya, khas blangs pa'i sdom pa dang 'gal ba'i nyes ltung rnams la bshags bsdams dang, dam tshig nyams chag sor gzhug la, da ni shi na'ang shi mod snyam du yid la gcags pa med par bya
rows.english: Now the latter two types of individuals, as they approach death (and assuming their minds are still clear), completely release mentally every single material object in their possession, dedicating them without the slightest hesitation to the gardens where we plant our virtues.  They thus free themselves from attachment to anything at all.  They openly admit, and then commit themselves to refrain from, every negative deed or transgression they have ever committed against the vows they have sworn to keep; and then they go about restoring whatever pledges they may have broken.  With this they are ready to die without any distress at all--mentally they are in a place where they can say to themselves, "Well, now if I die, I die; everything's fine."

rows.acip: SA CHU LA THIM PA NA PHYI RTAGS LUS BSGUL BSKYOD MI NUS SHING, ZUNGS MI THUB PAR LHOD LHOD POR 'GRO, LUS SA LA BYING BA SNYAM BYED CING NGA THEN ZER BA 'BYUNG, NANG RTAGS NI SMIG RGYU LTA BU'I NYAMS 'BYUNG,
rows.wylie: sa chu la thim pa na phyi rtags lus bsgul bskyod mi nus shing, zungs mi thub par lhod lhod por 'gro, lus sa la bying ba snyam byed cing nga then zer ba 'byung, nang rtags ni smig rgyu lta bu'i nyams 'byung
rows.english: When the element of earth dissolves into that of water, the outer sign is that you become incapable of getting your body to move at all. The inner sign at this point is that you have the impression of something like a mirage.

rows.acip: DE NAS SNANG BA DE YANG BSDUS PA'I RJES SU STONG CHEN ZHES PA SNANG BA NYER THOB 'CHAR TE, NAM MKHA' GA-YA' DAG LA MTSAMS KYI SMAG GIS KHYAB PA BZHIN DU, NAG LAM PA 'BYUNG ZHING DRAN PA YANG NYAMS NAS 'GRO,

rows.english: At a certain point in the latter part of this stage you do lose consciousness, and enter a deep blackness; this is no problem though, because the deeper you leave the conscious state then the clear light which comes to you subsequent to the "attainment" stage is that much more strong and steady.  This stage then we refer to as "great voidness," or the "attainment vision."

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL LA NYAMS DANG RTOGS PA'I 'OD GSAL GNYIS DANG, SRAB MO DANG 'THUG PO'I 'OD GSAL GNYIS DANG, RMI LAM GYI DUS SU RTOG MED KYI TING NGE 'DZIN GSAL DVANGS BYUNG BA YANG, GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL DU 'JOG PA'I RNAM GZHAG MANG PO SNANG YANG SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR MA PHYED PAR GNYID TING NGE 'DZIN DU SKYED NUS PA TZAM GYI STENG NAS BSHAD PA MANG DU BYAS PAR SNANG BAS, YID BRTAN THUB PA MI SNANG NGO,,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir gnyid kyi 'od gsal la nyams dang rtogs pa'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, srab mo dang 'thug po'i 'od gsal gnyis dang, rmi lam gyi dus su rtog med kyi ting nge 'dzin gsal dvangs byung ba yang, gnyid kyi 'od gsal du 'jog pa'i rnam gzhag mang po snang yang sngar bshad pa ltar ma phyed par gnyid ting nge 'dzin du skyed nus pa tsam gyi steng nas bshad pa mang du byas par snang bas, yid brtan thub pa mi snang ngo
rows.english: And so it is that the clear light of sleep can be discussed in terms of the two of a feeling of clear light and an actual experience of clear light; and in terms of the two of a less deep state of clear light and a deeper state of it; and in terms of a clear and lucid state of non-conceptual concentration that comes in your dreams.  And despite the fact that many presentations on the clear light of sleep have been written, a great number of them give their explanation based on nothing more than teaching the ability to turn sleep into a state of meditative concentration, without making any of the distinctions we've just mentioned.  As such it does not appear that we should accept these words as authoritative.

rows.acip: GNYIS PA RNAM SHES GZHAN GYI GRONG DU 'JUG PA NI, MIG SOGS KYI DBANG PO LA GRONG DANG, DBANG PO'I RTEN LA GRONG KHYER GYI SGRAS BSTAN PA NI, PHAR PHYIN NAS 'BYUNG LA, GANG ZAG GZHAN SHI BA'I LUS MA NYAMS PA LA'ANG, GRONG KHYER GYI SGRA 'JUG PAS RNAM SHES DER 'JUG PA LA GRONG 'JUG CES GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa rnam shes gzhan gyi grong du 'jug pa ni, mig sogs kyi dbang po la grong dang, dbang po'i rten la grong khyer gyi sgras bstan pa ni, phar phyin nas 'byung la, gang zag gzhan shi ba'i lus ma nyams pa la'ang, grong khyer gyi sgra 'jug pas rnam shes der 'jug pa la grong 'jug ces gsungs so
rows.english: This brings us to the second division in this portion of the text: an explanation of bringing our consciousness to "enter" the "city" of another's body.  The custom of referring to the eyes and other sense organs as "the village," and to the bases of these powers as "the city," is something that has come from the teachings on the perfection of wisdom.  The body of another person who has died--a body which is still fresh and has not deteriorated--is also referred to here as a "city."  And so when we send our consciousness to enter this body, it is called "entering the city."

rows.acip: JI LTAR BYED PA'I TSUL LA 'DI PA'I BLA MA RNAMS GSUM DU BYED PA'I DANG PO SKYANG BA NI, RLUNG SEMS GNYIS LA DBANG THOB, TSE 'DIR GZHAN DON 'GRUB PAR MTHONG ZHING, SEMS CAN LA SNYING RJE TSAD MED DANG LDAN PA'I GANG ZAG GIS GRONG DU 'JUG PA'I MAN NGAG NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BYA STE,
rows.wylie: ji ltar byed pa'i tshul la 'di pa'i bla ma rnams gsum du byed pa'i dang po skyang ba ni, rlung sems gnyis la dbang thob, tshe 'dir gzhan don 'grub par mthong zhing, sems can la snying rje tshad med dang ldan pa'i gang zag gis grong du 'jug pa'i man ngag nyams su blang bar bya ste
rows.english: As for the method that we use to carry out this practice, the Lamas have outlined three different steps.  The first of these is called "extending."  For this, we must first of all be someone who has attained mastery over their winds and mind.  We must as well perceive that if we do undertake the practice in this present life then it will be of benefit to others.  And finally we must be possessed of limitless compassion for all living beings.  This is the kind of person who can carry out the instructions for entering the city.

rows.acip: DE NAS BSAD PA NI MI RO GSAR PA MA NYAMS SHING, RMA 'BRAS SOGS MED PA, RIMS DANG 'BRUM BU SOGS KYIS SHI BA MIN PA'AM, YANG NA PHYUGS LA SOGS PA'I RO GTZANG ZHING MA NYAMS PA ZHIG BTZAL LA, CHU GTZANG MAS KHRUS BYAS, YID DU 'ONG BA'I RGYAN BTAGS LA, MDUN GYI MAndAL GYI STENG DU SKYIL KRUNG NGAM LUS LEGS PAR BCOS LA BZHAG,
rows.wylie: de nas bsad pa ni mi ro gsar pa ma nyams shing, rma 'bras sogs med pa, rims dang 'brum bu sogs kyis shi ba min pa'am, yang na phyugs la sogs pa'i ro gtsang zhing ma nyams pa zhig btsal la, chu gtsang mas khrus byas, yid du 'ong ba'i rgyan btags la, mdun gyi maNDal gyi steng du skyil krung ngam lus legs par bcos la bzhag
rows.english: This brings us to the second step, called "killing."  We are looking for a fresh, human corpse; one which has not deteriorated.  It should be without open sores, pustules, or anything of the like.  The person should not have died through something such as a contagion or pox.  Alternately you can seek out a very clean, dead body of for example a cow; again, the body should not have deteriorated.  Wash the body in water which is pure, and apply attractive ornaments to it.  Place the body upon the mandala platform in front of you, either putting it into a cross-legged position, or any other good position.

rows.acip: DE NAS RANG DANG RO GNYIS KA'I SNYING GAR SEMS KYI RTEN YI GE H'Um RE BSAMS LA, RANG GI SNYING KHA'I H'Um DE RLUNG PHYIR 'GRO BA DANG SDONGS NAS SNA BUG GA-YAS NAS 'THON TE, RO'I SNA BUG GA-YON NAS ZHUGS NAS SNYING KHA'I H'Um LA THIM PAR BSAM MO, ,DE LTAR YANG YANG BYAS PAS RO'I LUS LA DBUGS DANG, DRI LA SOGS PA BYUNG NA 'BYONGS PA YIN PAS NYAMS 'OG TU TSUD DO,,
rows.wylie: de nas rang dang ro gnyis ka'i snying gar sems kyi rten yi ge hUM re bsams la, rang gi snying kha'i hUM de rlung phyir 'gro ba dang sdongs nas sna bug ga-yas nas 'thon te, ro'i sna bug ga-yon nas zhugs nas snying kha'i hUM la thim par bsam mo, ,de ltar yang yang byas pas ro'i lus la dbugs dang, dri la sogs pa byung na 'byongs pa yin pas nyams 'og tu tshud do
rows.english: Now picture, at both your own heart and that of the corpse, a hung letter which serves as the support of the mind.  The hung letter at your own heart accompanies the wind during the exhale, passing out of the right nostril.  Picture that this then enters into the left nostril of the corpse, sinking into the hung letter at its own heart.  When you have repeated this over and over, and then the corpse begins to breathe--and begins emit the smells and so on of a living person--then you have completed this part of the practice, and the body takes on awareness.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR 'DI NAS RNAM SHES 'THON NAS PHA ROL GYI GRONG DU MA ZHUGS PA'I BAR YOD KYANG, BAR SRID MTSAN NYID PA'ANG MIN NO, ,DES NA LUS SNGA MA LA BRTEN PA'I CHOS KYI DRAN PA LA SOGS PA SNGA MA DOR BA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS NYAMS PA YANG MED DO,,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir 'di nas rnam shes 'thon nas pha rol gyi grong du ma zhugs pa'i bar yod kyang, bar srid mtshan nyid pa'ang min no, ,des na lus snga ma la brten pa'i chos kyi dran pa la sogs pa snga ma dor ba'i rgyu mtshan gyis nyams pa yang med do
rows.english: As such, we can say as well that--even though there is some period here between the time that our consciousness exits our old body and the time that it enters the city--neither is there any real "being during the time between death and rebirth."  And therefore it is not the case either that we have failed in our vows, with regard to our previous body, by rejecting our earlier spiritual intentions, or anything of the like.

rows.acip: MDOR NA PHAR PHYIN GYI THEG PA'I LUGS LA THEG CHEN GYI TSOGS SBYOR SOGS YE SHES KYI TSOGS DANG, SNYING RJE CHEN PO DANG SEMS BSKYED SOGS BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS GNYIS ZUNG 'BREL DU BYAS TE, BSKAL PA GRANGS MED GSUM DU NYAMS SU BLANGS PA LA BRTEN NAS SANGS RGYAS THOB PAR 'DOD KYANG,
rows.wylie: mdor na phar phyin gyi theg pa'i lugs la theg chen gyi tshogs sbyor sogs ye shes kyi tshogs dang, snying rje chen po dang sems bskyed sogs bsod nams kyi tshogs gnyis zung 'brel du byas te, bskal pa grangs med gsum du nyams su blangs pa la brten nas sangs rgyas thob par 'dod kyang
rows.english: To put it briefly, we concentrate in the open teachings of the way of the perfections upon amassing the collection of wisdom represented for example by the paths of accumulation and preparation on the track of the greater way; and upon amassing the collection of merit represented for example by great compassion and the Wish for enlightenment.  We seek to achieve a union of these two, and then--it is said--we can reach enlightenment within the period of three "countless" eons, during which we have undertaken these practices.

rows.acip: DE YANG RGYUD SDE 'OG MA GSUM GYI LAM LA YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA LA BLTAS SHING BGOD PA DANG, LAG BCANGS LAS BYUNG BA'I BDE BAS STONG NYID BSGOM PA YE SHES KYI TSOGS DANG, THEG CHEN SEMS BSKYED DANG LHA'I 'KHOR LO BSGOM PA SOGS BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS ZUNG 'BREL DU NYAMS SU BLANGS PAS SANGS RGYAS THOB PAR 'DOD KYANG, KUN NAS NYON MONGS PHYOGS KYI SKYE SHI BAR DO GSUM DANG RNAM PA MTHUN PA'I LHA'I 'KHOR LO BSGOM PA MED PAS, DE TZAM LA BRTEN NAS SANGS RGYAS THOB PAR MI NUS SO,,
rows.wylie: de yang rgyud sde 'og ma gsum gyi lam la ye shes kyi phyag rgya la bltas shing bgod pa dang, lag bcangs las byung ba'i bde bas stong nyid bsgom pa ye shes kyi tshogs dang, theg chen sems bskyed dang lha'i 'khor lo bsgom pa sogs bsod nams kyi tshogs zung 'brel du nyams su blangs pas sangs rgyas thob par 'dod kyang, kun nas nyon mongs phyogs kyi skye shi bar do gsum dang rnam pa mthun pa'i lha'i 'khor lo bsgom pa med pas, de tsam la brten nas sangs rgyas thob par mi nus so
rows.english: Now in the path of the lower three groups of the secret teachings they do describe the collection of wisdom as using the pleasure derived from exchanging glances with an imaginary partner--and from flirting with them and holding hands with them--as a way of meditating upon emptiness.  They say then that the collection of merit consists for example of the Wish for enlightenment of the greater way, and meditating upon circles of Angels.  And they would say that we reach enlightenment by practicing a combination of these two collections. These three groups lack however the practice of meditating upon circles of Angels in a way which replicates the three experiences of rebirth, death, and the intermediate state, as these relate to that part of our reality tied up with mental afflictions.

rows.acip: DKA' THUB BSTEN NA BYANG SEMS NYAMS PA'I RGYU BYAS NAS BDE CHEN GYI YE SHES BSKYED MI NUS PAS MCHOG MYUR DU 'GRUB PA LA GEGS BYED PA'I PHYIR TE,

rows.english: If then we instead deprive ourselves of these pleasures, it causes the depletion of our element of enlightenment.  We are then unable to produce the wisdom of great bliss, which in turn acts as an obstacle to our achieving the highest goal swiftly.

rows.acip: BSKYED RIM LHA'I SKU LA DMIGS PA GSAL ZHING BRTAN PAR BYAS NAS SGYU MA'I GDAMS NGAG SBYONG BA DANG GROL LAM PAS GTUM MO DANG CHAGS LAM PAS LAS RGYA LA BRTEN NAS BDE STONG GI NYAMS DANG MI 'BRAL BAR BYED PA RJE MAR PA'I THUGS KYI BCUD PHYUNG BA'I GDAMS PA YIN ZHES, RJE BTZUN MID LA GSUNG NGO,,
rows.wylie: bskyed rim lha'i sku la dmigs pa gsal zhing brtan par byas nas sgyu ma'i gdams ngag sbyong ba dang grol lam pas gtum mo dang chags lam pas las rgya la brten nas bde stong gi nyams dang mi 'bral bar byed pa rje mar pa'i thugs kyi bcud phyung ba'i gdams pa yin zhes, rje btsun mid la gsung ngo
rows.english: The holy Milarepa once said: First we assure that our practice of the stage of creation, our visualization of the body of the Angel, is clear and firm.  Then we go on to train ourselves in the advices on the illusion, and those who are on the path which liberates us take up the practices of inner fire, while those following the path of desire practice with an actual partner, working never to lose the experience of bliss and emptiness.  This is the heart teaching, the very cream, of Lord Marpa's holy thought. * * * Je Tsongkapa has also composed a short piece entitled A Book on the Stages of Dissolution, Crucial Points Taught only by Word of Mouth (ACIP digital text S05309). rows.english: When we refer here to "every one of those Gone That Way," we are talking about that great being, the Keeper of the Diamond: Vajradhara.  He "engages His diamond in the practice of wisdom," meaning that He goes into union with His--the Keeper of the Diamond's--own wisdom partner. We see our partner as our Lama, and thus as a true Angel--a perfect being who has come to us in order to guide us to enlightenment.  And They see us the same way.  This practice is expressed by Je Tsongkapa himself in His Illumination of Every Secret Point (ACIP digital text S05316, ff. 165a-165b):

rows.acip: (KHA CIG SUN DBYUNG BAR MI BYA BA'I SKAD DOD LA 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BAR MI BYA ZHES PAR YOD PAS, THIG LE NYAMS PAS 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BAR MI BYA BA LA 'CHAD PA NI SKABS DON MA RTOGS PAR SNANG STE, THUGS KYI RDO RJE MI SMAD PA NI SMOD TSIG GIS BUD MED KYI SEMS MA DGA' BAR MI BYA BA'I DON YIN GYI, SGRUB PA PO RANG GI SEMS LA BYED PA MIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,)
rows.wylie: (kha cig sun dbyung bar mi bya ba'i skad dod la 'dod chags dang bral bar mi bya zhes par yod pas, thig le nyams pas 'dod chags dang bral bar mi bya ba la 'chad pa ni skabs don ma rtogs par snang ste, thugs kyi rdo rje mi smad pa ni smod tshig gis bud med kyi sems ma dga' bar mi bya ba'i don yin gyi, sgrub pa po rang gi sems la byed pa min pa'i phyir ro,,)
rows.english: Now some commentators have pointed out that the original Sanskrit for "don't upset the mind" can also mean "never lose your passion."  And so they explain this section as meaning that we should never lose our sexual passion, since this would then hurt the essential drops within our body. This interpretation though misses the context of the current line.  When it says that we should "never disparage the diamond of enlightened mind," what it's talking about is never displeasing the heart of our Lady.  It's not however a reference to the mind of the practitioner themselves.

rows.english: Here's how this works.  When the element does pour out of the body, then the person loses their feelings of passion; and thus their infinite thought of compassion dies. rows.english: With this He split off countless versions of himself, sending them to billions upon billions of worlds, to the ends of infinite space itself. rows.acip: BSHAD TSUL 'DI DANG MI MTHUN PAR MKHAS GRUB RJE'I BRTAG GNYIS RNAM BSHAD LAS, BYANG SEMS SRID PA THA MA PA DE LA DBANG GSUM PA DNGOS DBANG DU BSKUR BA'I TSE, PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS BDE CHEN MTSAN NYID TSANG BA BSKYED PAR NUS LA, STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS ZIN MA NYAMS PA SNGAR NAS YOD PAS,
rows.wylie: bshad tshul 'di dang mi mthun par mkhas grub rje'i brtag gnyis rnam bshad las, byang sems srid pa tha ma pa de la dbang gsum pa dngos dbang du bskur ba'i tshe, phyag rgya la brten nas bde chen mtshan nyid tshang ba bskyed par nus la, stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs zin ma nyams pa sngar nas yod pas
rows.english: There is a part in Kedrup Je's Treatise on the Secret Teaching in Two Sections which presents this in a way which conflicts with the explanation above.  It says, Suppose now that the third of the empowerments is given in its actual form to a bodhisattva who is in his or her final rebirth.  This bodhisattva, through practice with their partner, is able to give birth to a form of ecstasy which is complete in every aspect.  They are though still maintaining--they have still not lost--their direct perception of emptiness from before.

rows.english: [Scene number] 132B: During this time--at a point where he is recovering from his illness--a majestic form of Gentle Voice appears to Je Rinpoche.  He tells the Lord, "From this point on, you must throw yourself into practicing the stages of creation and completion.  If you do so, then you will quickly give birth to high realizations of the unsurpassed teachings of the secret word.  Seven of your disciples--those with the fortune that comes from good deeds--will as well achieve extraordinary realizations of the path."

rows.acip: RJE'I ZHAL NAS, NYAMS SNANG YIN, RTOGS LDAN PA LA DRIS GSUNGS PA'I LAN KHONG GI GSUNG NAS, BSKYAR MA ZHU DGOS BA MED, LAM DE RJE'I THUGS LA 'KHRUNGS PA'I RGYU, BDE STONG GI YE SHES KHYAD PAR BA SNGAR NAS 'KHRUNGS ZIN, DA PHYI'I RKYEN ZHING SKYES KYI PHO NYAS GROGS MDZAD PA'ANG MYUR DU 'ONG BAS, LAM DE MYUR DU 'KHRUNGS, RJE BTZUN GSUNG ZHUS PAS THUGS CHES PAR SNANG,
rows.wylie: rje'i zhal nas, nyams snang yin, rtogs ldan pa la dris gsungs pa'i lan khong gi gsung nas, bskyar ma zhu dgos ba med, lam de rje'i thugs la 'khrungs pa'i rgyu, bde stong gi ye shes khyad par ba sngar nas 'khrungs zin, da phyi'i rkyen zhing skyes kyi pho nyas grogs mdzad pa'ang myur du 'ong bas, lam de myur du 'khrungs, rje btsun gsung zhus pas thugs ches par snang
rows.english: Je Tsongkapa said, "This may just be an hallucination; we should consult with Tokdenpa."  Tokdenpa in turn replied, "There is no need to ask again about this vision.  There are certain causes that will bring this path to be born within Je Rinpoche's holy heart.  One is the extraordinary form of the wisdom of bliss and voidness, which he has already finished reaching.  Now the outer aid--a Messenger lady born of paradise who arrives to accompany Him on His quest--will soon come to Him, and with this that special path will quickly rise in His heart.  This," concluded Tokdenpa, "is what the Holy Gentle Voice is saying."  And then Je Tsonkapa believed what He had heard.

There are certain causes that will bring this path to be born within Je Rinpoche's holy heart.  One is the extraordinary form of the wisdom of bliss and voidness, which he has already finished reaching.  Now the outer aid--a Messenger lady born of paradise who arrives to accompany Him on His quest--will soon come to Him, and with this that special path will quickly rise in His heart.  This," concluded Tokdenpa, "is what the Holy Gentle Voice is saying."  And then Je Tsonkapa believed what He had heard.

rows.acip: CIS KYANG BYED DGOS NA RIGS MU STEGS PA'I RIGS YIN PA, 'DZIN RTOG GANG YANG MI BYED PA, GTZANG SBRA CHE BA, BYAMS SNYING RJES BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS DANG LDAN PA, NA TSOD LO BCU DRUG LON PA, MING DRI MED MA CES BYA BA GCIG RNYED NAS KHYIM THAB BYED ZER BA 'US DE 'DRA GANG NAS RNYED GSUNG ZHING, DE LA RTEN NAS KHO NI SDUG BSNGAL BAR GYUR TO GSUNG TSE,
rows.wylie: cis kyang byed dgos na rigs mu stegs pa'i rigs yin pa, 'dzin rtog gang yang mi byed pa, gtsang sbra che ba, byams snying rjes byang chub kyi sems dang ldan pa, na tshod lo bcu drug lon pa, ming dri med ma ces bya ba gcig rnyed nas khyim thab byed zer ba 'us de 'dra gang nas rnyed gsung zhing, de la rten nas kho ni sdug bsngal bar gyur to gsung tshe
rows.english: "But he did say that, if he had no choice but to do so, then it would only be under one condition: we would have to find for him a maiden who belongs to a Hindu line; who doesn't grasp reality in any mistaken manner at all; who observes absolute cleanliness; who possesses love, compassion, and the Wish for enlightenment; who is sixteen years of age; and whose name happens to be Immaculate.  How on earth will we ever be able to find a maiden like this? "And that," he added, "is the reason why I'm so miserable."

rows.acip: MI RNAMS GYIS SNYING RJE NAS TSOGS SOG BYED CING BRAM ZE LA, DRI MED MA KHO RANG GIS BTZUN MO BYED PA YIN ZER NGAN SMRAS SGROG PAS, BRAM ZE MA PHOD PAR BU MO STER BAR KHAS BLANGS NAS, BLON PO GNYIS SPRO NYAMS GYIS YUL DU 'ONGS TE, RGYAL PO ZHI BA'I GO CHA'I SPYAN SNGAR PHYIN NAS, SNGAR GYIS LO RGYUS RNAMS RGYAL PO LA PHUL BAS, RGYAL PO MCHOG TU THUGS DGYES NAS, BRAM ZE SKAR RGYAL LA LONGS SPYOD 'BYOR BA'I TSOGS DPAG TU MED PA, BLON PO MANG PO LA 'KHOR G-YOG DANG BCAS PA GSU RU BTANG BA LA,
rows.wylie: mi rnams gyis snying rje nas tshogs sog byed cing bram ze la, dri med ma kho rang gis btsun mo byed pa yin zer ngan smras sgrog pas, bram ze ma phod par bu mo ster bar khas blangs nas, blon po gnyis spro nyams gyis yul du 'ongs te, rgyal po zhi ba'i go cha'i spyan sngar phyin nas, sngar gyis lo rgyus rnams rgyal po la phul bas, rgyal po mchog tu thugs dgyes nas, bram ze skar rgyal la longs spyod 'byor ba'i tshogs dpag tu med pa, blon po mang po la 'khor g-yog dang bcas pa gsu ru btang ba la
rows.english: Crowds of people begin to gather there outside the door, in sympathy for the ministers.  The mob starts to shout out, demanding that the Brahmin allow Immaculate to take Her place as Queen.  Unable to bear it any longer, the Brahmin finally agrees to release his daughter. Overcome with joy, the two ministers return to their homeland.  They come to the king, Armor of Peace, and relate all these events to him.  The king is infinitely pleased, and sends forth a great many ministers, and members of the court, and palace servants to the Brahmin to greet his arrival, and bearing an infinite number of riches as gifts for him.
