rows.acip: LO KY'A DUN DU RNAL 'BYOR GYI DBANG PHYUG CHEN PO PHAM MTHING PA LAS RGYA LA BRTEN NAS MCHOG GI DNGOS GRUB BRNYES PA YAB YUM GNYIS KA'I SKU MA NYAMS PAR BZHUGS PA LA BDE MCHOG RANG BYON DU GRAGS PA DE'I MDUN DU
rows.wylie: lo kyA dun du rnal 'byor gyi dbang phyug chen po pham mthing pa las rgya la brten nas mchog gi dngos grub brnyes pa yab yum gnyis ka'i sku ma nyams par bzhugs pa la bde mchog rang byon du grags pa de'i mdun du
rows.english: He then continued to Lokya Dun, to the place they call the "Image of the Angel of Highest Bliss, which Occurred All on its Own."  This is where that great Lord among Yogis, Pamtingpa, attained the highest goal by practicing with His actual, physical partner.  The physical bodies of both this Lama and his Lady are entombed here, and the flesh has never decayed.

rows.english: Here secondly is our description of how to protect the vows, once you have been granted them.  Here there are two divisions: how to protect your vows by relying upon an outer aid--a spiritual guide; and by relying on an inner aid--your own perfect intentions. * * * Here again the idea of an outer aid, this time in the attempt to identify what it is that emptiness is empty of: the gakja. rows.acip: NANG GI RKYEN DAD SOGS 'PHAGS PA'I NOR BDUN, TSUL KHRIMS LA SPYOD PA SOGS BSLAB PA RIN PO CHE GSUM STE, MDOR NA BYAMS SNYING RJE'I RTZA BA CAN GYI BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS RGYUD LA SKYES
rows.wylie: nang gi rkyen dad sogs 'phags pa'i nor bdun, tshul khrims la spyod pa sogs bslab pa rin po che gsum ste, mdor na byams snying rje'i rtsa ba can gyi byang chub kyi sems rgyud la skyes
rows.english: So too we possess the inner aids of the Seven Riches of the Realized--faith and the rest; and the Three Precious Trainings--beginning with following an ethical way of life.  To state it briefly then, we are ready to give rise in our hearts to the Wish for enlightenment, which has as its own foundation both love and compassion. * * * Now that we have a picture of the distinction between an inner and outer aid, we can turn to their presentation in the secret teachings.  What better place to begin than in Chuje Ngawang Pelden's Presentation of the Secret Levels and Paths (ACIP digital text S00196, folio 22a)?

rows.acip: SGYU MA'I SKU DE PHUNG PO SNYING PA DAM TSIG SEMS DPAR BLTAS PA'I THUGS KHAR YE SHES SEMS DPA'I TSUL GYI ZHUGS NAS MNYAM RJES KYI NYAMS LEN RNAMS BYAS PAS RNAM DAG YE SHES KYI RNAL 'BYOR 'GRUB TU NYE BA'I MTSAN MA MTHONG BA NA,
rows.wylie: sgyu ma'i sku de phung po snying pa dam tshig sems dpar bltas pa'i thugs khar ye shes sems dpa'i tshul gyi zhugs nas mnyam rjes kyi nyams len rnams byas pas rnam dag ye shes kyi rnal 'byor 'grub tu nye ba'i mtshan ma mthong ba na
rows.english: This body of illusion enters into the the holy heart of our old heaps--which we are viewing as a pledge being--in the way that a wisdom being would.  We then go through the periods of the main meditation and the aftermath, with which we begin to see signs that we are close to attaining the deep practice of pure wisdom.

rows.english: (We can say then that both the newer translations work out to the same thing. rows.english: The root tantra points out here that-- You can partake of all The pleasures of the senses, And continue the recitation, Without losing any part Of the secret mantra. What this is saying is that it's no problem--for a certain number of very exceptional practitioners--to engage at this point as well in practice with an actual partner. * * * In the same text (ff. 306a-307a), Je Rinpoche examines in detail the interaction between practicing with an imaginary partner, and practicing with an actual one--

rows.acip: 'DI RIM GNYIS KYI SPYOD PA BYED PAS NYAMS SU LEN PA NA DGA' BA BZHI DANG STONG PA BZHI'I MCHOG DMAN GYI KHYAD MA GTOGS PA, GNYIS KAS MNYAM GZHAG TU YE RGYA DANG MNYAM PAR SBYAR BA LA BRTEN NAS LHAN SKYES DANG 'OD GSAL NYID SKYONG, DE LA GNAS MA NUS NAS LANGS PA NA SLAR YANG PHYAG RGYA DE LA BRTEN NAS SNGAR LTAR SGOM PA SPEL BAR BYED DO,,
rows.wylie: 'di rim gnyis kyi spyod pa byed pas nyams su len pa na dga' ba bzhi dang stong pa bzhi'i mchog dman gyi khyad ma gtogs pa, gnyis kas mnyam gzhag tu ye rgya dang mnyam par sbyar ba la brten nas lhan skyes dang 'od gsal nyid skyong, de la gnas ma nus nas langs pa na slar yang phyag rgya de la brten nas sngar ltar sgom pa spel bar byed do
rows.english: Now whether you are undertaking activities of one stage or the other, there's just that difference in the quality of the four forms of bliss, and the four forms of emptiness.  In both of them, we are engaging in union with an imagined partner, in deep meditation.  And through this union we try to maintain our experience of the simultaneous and of the clear light.  When we find that we can no longer stay in these two, then we come up out of them and once again practice with our partner, alternating between these two practices, as we described it before.

rows.acip: DES NA SNGAR BSHAD PA'I SNGAGS KYI RNAL 'BYOR NYAMS SU BLANGS PAS SNYING GA'I RTZA MDUD LHOD PAR SONG BA NA LAS RGYA BSTEN DGOS SHING,
rows.wylie: des na sngar bshad pa'i sngags kyi rnal 'byor nyams su blangs pas snying ga'i rtsa mdud lhod par song ba na las rgya bsten dgos shing
rows.english: Follow then the deep practice of the mantra, as we have described it before, which will loosen up the knot in the channels of the heart.  At this point we must next move on to practice with an actual partner.

rows.acip: ,NYAMS PA MED PA DAM TSIG YIN, ,LHAN SKYES YE SHES MNGON GYUR PA, ,DE NI PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'O,

rows.english: Never allowing it to degenerate Is the partner of the pledge; And bringing forth simultaneous wisdom Is the Great Seal of Mahamudra.

rows.acip: 'GOS LO CHEN PO GZHON NU DPAL NI, STONG NYID NGES PA'I RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA'I YE SHES DE NYID PHYAG RGYA CHEN POR BZHED DE, DEB SNGON GYI PHYAG CHEN LO RGYUS THOG MAR, DA NI SANGS RGYAS KYI BSTAN PA GZHI SO SO THAR PA NAS DPAL GSANG BA 'DUS PA'I BAR GYI SGRUB PA DANG NYAMS LEN THAMS CAD LA RGYAS 'DEBS PAR BYED PA PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'I GTAM BRJOD PAR BYA STE, ZHES BSHAD PAS SO,,
rows.wylie: 'gos lo chen po gzhon nu dpal ni, stong nyid nges pa'i rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes de nyid phyag rgya chen por bzhed de, deb sngon gyi phyag chen lo rgyus thog mar, da ni sangs rgyas kyi bstan pa gzhi so so thar pa nas dpal gsang ba 'dus pa'i bar gyi sgrub pa dang nyams len thams cad la rgyas 'debs par byed pa phyag rgya chen po'i gtam brjod par bya ste, zhes bshad pas so
rows.english: The great Gu Lotsawa, Shunnu Pel, takes the position that the Great Seal is nothing other than that non-conceptual wisdom with which we perceive emptiness.  In the opening section of the account of the tradition of the Great Seal found in His Blue Annals, He says-- And now we will turn to the subject of the story of the Great Seal, which acts to seal or mark all these spiritual endeavors and practices--everything from the foundation of all these practices, the teachings on discipline, or individual freedom, up to the secret teachings of the glorious Secret Collection.

rows.acip: 'DOD CHAGS LHAG PAR CHE ZHING DE KHO NA NYID KYI BLO CHE BA MA YIN PA THABS DE LAS GZHAN GYIS SEMS MNYAM PAR 'JOG MI NUS PA LA LAS RGYA GSUNGS TE, DER YANG RJES SU MTHUN PA'I LAS SU BYED PA NYID KYIS NYAMS SU LEN PA'O,,
rows.wylie: 'dod chags lhag par che zhing de kho na nyid kyi blo che ba ma yin pa thabs de las gzhan gyis sems mnyam par 'jog mi nus pa la las rgya gsungs te, der yang rjes su mthun pa'i las su byed pa nyid kyis nyams su len pa'o
rows.english: The actual partner is recommended in scripture for those who possess a high degree of desire--for people who have no great understanding of suchness, and who cannot put their minds into balanced meditation by using any other method.  And they do the rest of their practice exclusively following types of deeds which are consistent with this.

rows.acip: YE SHES GRAGS PAS, ,GANG ZHIG YE SHES PHYAG RGYA SOGS, ,SGOM LA MNGON DGA' MED GYUR PA, ,SHES RAB NYAMS CHUNG NYID YIN PHYIR, ,PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO SGOM PA MIN, ,DE LA KUN MKHYEN PHAN BZHED PAS, ,PHYAG RGYA CHEN PO'I MING GIS NI, ,RDO RJE SEMS DPA' LA SOGS PA'I, ,GZUGS DE NYID NI NGES PAR BSTAN,
rows.wylie: ye shes grags pas, ,gang zhig ye shes phyag rgya sogs, ,sgom la mngon dga' med gyur pa, ,shes rab nyams chung nyid yin phyir, ,phyag rgya chen po sgom pa min, ,de la kun mkhyen phan bzhed pas, ,phyag rgya chen po'i ming gis ni, ,rdo rje sems dpa' la sogs pa'i, ,gzugs de nyid ni nges par bstan
rows.english: As Jnana Kirti puts it, Anyone who has no attraction Towards practicing with an imagined partner Or any other one of the like Is a person whose wisdom is truly endowed With little power; and as such They cannot meditate on the Great Seal. To help this type of person, the All-Knowing One Was sure to teach that very form Of an Angel such as the Warrior of Diamond, Giving them the name of the Seal Great.

rows.acip: SRING MO DANG BU MO (ZHES PA YANG SNGAR BSHAD PA) DE BZHIN TE,:- ^ (SA STON TE, DE NYID SPYOD PA DANG PO GNYIS KYI SKABS KYI LAS RGYA LA'ANG 'DRA BAS DER YANG SBYAR RO,,) ^ DES NA MA LTAR BYAMS PA DANG, SRING MO LTAR BRTZE BA DANG, BU MO LTAR GDUNG SEMS CHE BA DANG, 'DRA BA'I SGO NAS MA DANG SRING MO DANG BU MO ZHES BSHAD KYI DE DAG DNGOS MA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: sring mo dang bu mo (zhes pa yang sngar bshad pa) de bzhin te,:- ^ (sa ston te, de nyid spyod pa dang po gnyis kyi skabs kyi las rgya la'ang 'dra bas der yang sbyar ro,,) ^ des na ma ltar byams pa dang, sring mo ltar brtse ba dang, bu mo ltar gdung sems che ba dang, 'dra ba'i sgo nas ma dang sring mo dang bu mo zhes bshad kyi de dag dngos ma yin no
rows.english: The references to a "sister" and a "daughter" are also similar (to what we have said before; the references are also meant to be applied to an actual partner at the point where we are practicing the first two types of activity).  And so we can say that our partner should be someone who loves us in the same way that our own Mother does; and that we should love each other with the same intensity that sisters and brothers love each other; and that we should feel the same deep affection for them that one would towards their own daughter.  Partner are referred to then with the words "mother" and "sister" and "daughter," but of course this is not to say that our mother and the rest would actually be our partner. * * * Je Rinpoche waxes further on the love that a partner should feel in the same text at ff. 120b-121a:

rows.acip: LO CHEN GYI 'GYUR LAS, MAN NGAG RNAM PAR BSTAN MI BYA, ZHES 'BYUNG NGO, ,BHA BAS, MAN NGAG RNAM PAR NYAMS MI BYA, ZHES 'DON PA'I DON LAN CIG TZAM GSOL BA BTAB PA LA, SRED PA'I DBANG GIS DBANG BSKUR BA SOGS MI BYA BA LA BSHAD DO,,
rows.wylie: lo chen gyi 'gyur las, man ngag rnam par bstan mi bya, zhes 'byung ngo, ,bha bas, man ngag rnam par nyams mi bya, zhes 'don pa'i don lan cig tsam gsol ba btab pa la, sred pa'i dbang gis dbang bskur ba sogs mi bya ba la bshad do
rows.english: Lochen's translation at this point says "Never grant the oral advices."  When Bhava here says "Don't let the oral advices be degraded," it's explained as meaning that one should never--out of hope for some reward--grant empowerment and such to someone who has made a proper request, but only a single time.

rows.acip: DE LTA BUS DAM TSIG NYAMS NA, DE LAS LDANG BA'I THABS DAM TSIG GSO BA'I SGRUB THABS DANG, BZLAS PA LVA BA PA DANG LHA SBAS KYI 'GREL PAR BSHAD DO,,
rows.wylie: de lta bus dam tshig nyams na, de las ldang ba'i thabs dam tshig gso ba'i sgrub thabs dang, bzlas pa lva ba pa dang lha sbas kyi 'grel par bshad do
rows.english: The commentaries of Master Kambala and Master Deva Rakshita say at this point that--in the case that our pledges are broken in this way--then we should undertake means of recovering ourselves, through rituals for reaching Angels that include a section on restoring the pledges, or else through the recitation of mantras.

rows.acip: LAS KYI PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS 'JUG PA'I TSUL LA PHYAG RGYA'I MTSAN NYID BRTAG THABS, DE 'KHOR BA LA ZHEN PA LOG NAS THAR PA THOB 'DOD KYI BLO BCOS MA MA YIN PA BSKYED DE, BYAMS SNYING RJE BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSKYED,
rows.wylie: las kyi phyag rgya la brten nas 'jug pa'i tshul la phyag rgya'i mtshan nyid brtag thabs, de 'khor ba la zhen pa log nas thar pa thob 'dod kyi blo bcos ma ma yin pa bskyed de, byams snying rje byang chub kyi sems bskyed
rows.english: Concerning the method where we get the winds to enter by practicing with an actual partner, there are first of all certain ways of examining a potential partner to see if they possess the requisite characteristics.  They must have gained an aversion for this cycle of pain; they must have reached an uncontrived state of mind where they truly hope to attain freedom from this suffering.  And they must as well have developed within themselves the attitudes of love, compassion, and the Wish for enlightenment.

rows.acip: DE LTA BU'I ZAB MO'I LTA BA DANG SBYOR RGYU MED PAR LHA'I RNAL 'BYOR DANG RTZA RLUNG SOGS SNGAGS KYI NYAMS LEN ZAB MOR GRAGS PA JI 'DRA'I ZHIG 'BAD PAS NYAMS SU BLANGS KYANG GZUGS BRNYAN TZAM LAS MI 'ONG STE,
rows.wylie: de lta bu'i zab mo'i lta ba dang sbyor rgyu med par lha'i rnal 'byor dang rtsa rlung sogs sngags kyi nyams len zab mor grags pa ji 'dra'i zhig 'bad pas nyams su blangs kyang gzugs brnyan tsam las mi 'ong ste
rows.english: Oh we can exert ourselves in other deep practices of the Angel, or in practices of the channels and winds, or anything else you might hear people say are especially profound methods of the secret word; but if they don't relate to the deep view of emptiness such as that we've just described, then you will get nothing more than a shadow of the result that you should be reaching.

rows.acip: ZHES NGES 'BYUNG BYANG SEMS YANG DAG PA'I LTA BA GSUM MED PAR SNGAGS KYI NYAMS LEN BSKYANGS KYANG SA CHOD SHIN TU CHUNG BAR GSUNGS LA,
rows.wylie: zhes nges 'byung byang sems yang dag pa'i lta ba gsum med par sngags kyi nyams len bskyangs kyang sa chod shin tu chung bar gsungs la
rows.english: What this is saying is that someone who lacks the three attitudes of renunciation, the Wish for enlightenment, and the pure view of reality will make very few breakthroughs in their practice, even if they try to maintain a practice of the way of the secret word.

rows.acip: BDE BA DE RANG BZHIN MED PA'I DON LA MNYAM PAR BZHAG PAS BDE BA STER BA NI STONG PHYOGS KYI PHYAG RGYA CHEN MO DRIL BU ZHABS KYIS LHAN SKYES KYI GTUM MOR BSHAD PA'ANG 'DI NYID DO, ,'DI GNYIS SPEL MAR NYAMS SU BLANGS PAS 'BRAS BU MYUR DU 'THOB CES GSUNGS SO,,

rows.english: We use this bliss to go into a deep meditation upon the fact that nothing has any nature of its own; and so the thing which gives us bliss is the Great Partner or Seal of the emptiness side of things. And it has been stated that--if we can alternate between a practice of the two--then we quickly achieve our goal.

rows.acip: LHAN SKYES KYI BDE BA LA BRTAN PA MA THOB BAR DU LAS SAM YE SHES KYI PHYAG RGYA MI 'DOR BA NI LNGA PA DANG, PHO NYA SOGS PHYI NANG GI THABS KYIS LHAN SKYES 'DREN PA LA NYAMS LEN GTZO BOR BYED PA NI DRUG PA DANG,
rows.wylie: lhan skyes kyi bde ba la brtan pa ma thob bar du las sam ye shes kyi phyag rgya mi 'dor ba ni lnga pa dang, pho nya sogs phyi nang gi thabs kyis lhan skyes 'dren pa la nyams len gtso bor byed pa ni drug pa dang
rows.english: The fifth pledge states that we should never set aside our actual, or our imagined, partner without having attained a firm state of simultaneous bliss.  And the sixth pledge is that we make, as our principal practice, the attempt to bring on simultaneous bliss through the various outer and inner methods: through a Messenger or the like.

rows.acip: ,GAL TE DBANG BSKUR DE 'DZIN NA, ,TSANGS SPYOD DKA' THUB LA GNAS PAS, ,BKAG PA SPYAD PAR GYUR PA'I PHYIR, ,DKA' THUB SDOM PA DE NYAMS TE,

rows.english: If they were to be offered, And accept this empowerment, Then those maintaining the spiritual challenge Of celibacy would be engaging in something Which was prohibited, and thus their commitment To this challenge would be broken.

rows.acip: BKAG PA'I DGOS PA NI, GAL TE TSANGS SPYOD LA GNAS PA DAG GIS PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN NAS DBANG BSKUR DE GNYIS LEN CING 'DZIN NA NI, TSANGS SPYOD DKA' THUB LA GNAS PA DE TSANGS SPYOD KYI DKA' THUB KYI SDOM PA DE NYAMS TE,

rows.english: The reason for this prohibition is as follows. rows.acip: DE YANG GTZO BO'I DBANG DU BYAS KYI, BLA MED KYI GDUL BYAS CHAGS BRAL GYI SPYOD PA BSTEN MI RUNG BA YANG MA YIN TE, BLA MED KYI LAM NYAMS SU LEN PA'I RAB BYUNG GI RTEN KHYAD PAR CAN YOD PA'I PHYIR TE,
rows.wylie: de yang gtso bo'i dbang du byas kyi, bla med kyi gdul byas chags bral gyi spyod pa bsten mi rung ba yang ma yin te, bla med kyi lam nyams su len pa'i rab byung gi rten khyad par can yod pa'i phyir te
rows.english: This statement is made to describe the primary types of disciples of this group; it is not however meant to say that it is somehow wrong if disciples of this group also wish to engage in the activities which do not involve desire.  We can for example give the example of an exceptional ordained person who is practicing the path of the unsurpassed teachings.

rows.acip: ,ZHES GSUNGS TE CHAGS BRAL GYI LAM GYIS 'DUL BA'I RAB BYUNG NI CHAGS CAN GYI LAM LA MOS PAR MI NUS PA DANG, SA BON NYAMS PA'I RGAN PO NI BDE STONG SBYOR BA'I NUS PA MED PA DANG, PHYI ROL GYI RTOG GE LHUR LEN PA NI CHOS 'DI LA MI 'JUG PAS, LAM MCHOG GI SNOD MIN PAR BSHAD DO,,
rows.wylie: zhes gsungs te chags bral gyi lam gyis 'dul ba'i rab byung ni chags can gyi lam la mos par mi nus pa dang, sa bon nyams pa'i rgan po ni bde stong sbyor ba'i nus pa med pa dang, phyi rol gyi rtog ge lhur len pa ni chos 'di la mi 'jug pas, lam mchog gi snod min par bshad do
rows.english: What this verse is saying is that the type of ordained person who responds to the path where we do not use desire as a path will not be able to come to an appreciation of the path where we do use desire.  An elderly person--one whose seed has declined--will not have the ability to come to a union of bliss and emptiness.  And someone who is all wrapped up in the academics of it, a non-Buddhist, will never undertake this form of Dharma in the first place.  And so these types, it is stated, are not proper vessels for the supreme path.

rows.acip: DE RNAMS BSTEN PA'I GDUNGS BZHIN PAS BYANG CHUB MI 'GRUB PA NI, DE RNAMS KYIS LUS SKAMS PA STE RGUD PAS SDUG BSNGAL BAR 'GYUR LA, DES NI KUN DA LTA BU'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS NYAMS PAS, BDE BA CHEN PO'I TING NGE 'DZIN LAS GZHAN DU GA-YENGS PAS NA, TSE 'DIR DNGOS GRUB MCHOG MI 'GRUB BO,,
rows.wylie: de rnams bsten pa'i gdungs bzhin pas byang chub mi 'grub pa ni, de rnams kyis lus skams pa ste rgud pas sdug bsngal bar 'gyur la, des ni kun da lta bu'i byang chub kyi sems nyams pas, bde ba chen po'i ting nge 'dzin las gzhan du ga-yengs pas na, tshe 'dir dngos grub mchog mi 'grub bo
rows.english: You can torture yourself with practices like these, but they will never bring you to enlightenment.  Rather, they only emaciate and hurt your body, bringing you pain.  This then causes the element of enlightenment within you--the one which resembles semen--to decline.  Due to this, in turn, you become distracted and wander off to something other than the single-point mind of great bliss.  And because of this you fail to reach the ultimate goal here in this life.

rows.acip: DE NAS BDE MI BDE'AM STONG MI STONG LA SOGS PA THAMS CAD LA 'DAS PA'I NYAMS SKYE ZHING, LUS THAMS CAD KYANG RTZA DBU MA LA 'JUG PA SNYAM BYED, RTZA GA-YAS GA-YON GNYIS KYANG DBU MAR 'JUG PA SNYAM BYED PA 'BYUNG STE, DE'I TSE RLUNG RTZA LA TSUD PA'I DUS ZHES BYA,
rows.wylie: de nas bde mi bde'am stong mi stong la sogs pa thams cad la 'das pa'i nyams skye zhing, lus thams cad kyang rtsa dbu ma la 'jug pa snyam byed, rtsa ga-yas ga-yon gnyis kyang dbu mar 'jug pa snyam byed pa 'byung ste, de'i tshe rlung rtsa la tshud pa'i dus zhes bya
rows.english: After this you get a sensation that is above and beyond all pleasure or pain, all emptiness or absence of emptiness, anything of the like.  You think to yourself that your entire body must have entered into your central channel; and that the left and right channels too must have entered this same channel.  At this point you have reached what we call the "stage where winds are entering the channel."

rows.acip: STENG 'OG GI RLUNG KHA SBYAR, LUS CUNG ZAD BSGUL ZHING BSGOM, DES DROD LA SOGS PA HA CHANG CHE NAS DE BAS KLOD LA BSGOM, DE LTAR BSGOMS PAS DANG PO DROD 'BYUNG, DE NAS TSOR BA BDE BA SKYE, DE NAS MI RTOG PA'I BDE BA SKYE, DE NAS MTSON BYED DPE'I YE SHES RNAMS NYAMS SU MYONG BA SKYE,
rows.wylie: steng 'og gi rlung kha sbyar, lus cung zad bsgul zhing bsgom, des drod la sogs pa ha chang che nas de bas klod la bsgom, de ltar bsgoms pas dang po drod 'byung, de nas tshor ba bde ba skye, de nas mi rtog pa'i bde ba skye, de nas mtshon byed dpe'i ye shes rnams nyams su myong ba skye
rows.english: Now make a capsule of the upper and lower winds.  Let your body shake a little, a go into a meditation.  If the warmth and such produced by this meditation is too great, then loosen up the meditation. If you continue this meditation, then first you will get a sensation of warmth.  After that you will have a feeling of pleasure, and then non-conceptual bliss.  This then brings on experiences of what we call the "representative wisdom, the approximate wisdom."

rows.acip: DE LTAR DGA' BA DANG, MCHOG DGA' BA DANG, DGA' BRAL SNGON DU SONG NAS, SKAD CIG MA BZHI PA LA LHAN SKYES RTOGS NAS, 'KHOR LOR BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BZUNG, HRIm NGAM, RnnIm NGAM, H'Um BRJOD CING NYAMS SU DOGS NA GYEN LA BZLOG, BDE BA CHUNG NA BSRUBS PAS THUR LA DBAB PO,
rows.wylie: de ltar dga' ba dang, mchog dga' ba dang, dga' bral sngon du song nas, skad cig ma bzhi pa la lhan skyes rtogs nas, 'khor lor byang chub kyi sems bzung, hriM ngam, rNNiM ngam, hUM brjod cing nyams su dogs na gyen la bzlog, bde ba chung na bsrubs pas thur la dbab po
rows.english: Continuing this way you get experiences of bliss, highest bliss, and beyond bliss; this is followed in the fourth moment by a realization of the spontaneous. At this point you should hold the element of enlightenment within the circle.  Speak out the syllable hring, or else irnning or huung.  If you feel like you might lose it, push it back up; if the bliss is too little, rub and send it downwards.

rows.english: Finally then do obeisance to the Lama, and rise out of the meditation.  You undertake this kind of experiential meditation on a regular basis, keeping up your practice in a steady stream, always utilizing a concrete example close at hand; and thus we refer to it as the "instructions on the great seal, imparted through direct means." With this we have concluded the crucial point of deep practice, which is meditation upon the path.

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, BLA MA BSTEN DGOS PA'I (RGYU MTSAN) LUNG GIS 'GRUB PA (DE LTAR NA,) MDO SNGAGS KYI (LAM GYI GNAD TSANG BA'I BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR) TE SGRUB THABS (BSGOM PA NI, DAL 'BYOR LA SNYING PO LEN PA'I THABS MCHOG TU GYUR BA YIN PAS) 'OG TU 'CHAD PA'I CHO GA ('DI LTAR NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BYA'O,) ,ZHES SO,,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, bla ma bsten dgos pa'i (rgyu mtshan) lung gis 'grub pa (de ltar na,) mdo sngags kyi (lam gyi gnad tshang ba'i bla ma'i rnal 'byor) te sgrub thabs (bsgom pa ni, dal 'byor la snying po len pa'i thabs mchog tu gyur ba yin pas) 'og tu 'chad pa'i cho ga ('di ltar nyams su blang bar bya'o,) ,zhes so
rows.english: Here is the first.  Thus we have described, proving our point through scriptural authority, why--the reason why--we must take ourselves to our Lama.  Thus, undertaking a ritual for reaching our Angel, a deep practice of the Lama--a version of this practice which includes all the crucial points of the path of both the open and secret teachings--is the highest way of getting the very essence out of the leisure and opportunity we have found in this life.  As such, says the text, we should do this practice--that is, the ritual which we shall describe in the sections to come--as follows. Preparing our Motivation

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, GNAS GANG BABS SU, BLA MA'I BRIS 'BUR GYI SKU LEGS PAR BSHAMS, MCHOD PA CI NUS SU BKOD PA MDZES PAR BYAS TE, GZHAN GYI G-YAM LA BRGYUGS PA'I KHA PHYIR BLTAS DANG, TSE 'DI TZAM GYI CHED DU MA YIN PAR SANGS RGYAS THOB PA'I PHYIR, (DGE SEMS KHYAD PAR CAN GYI NGANG NAS) NYAMS SU LEN PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, gnas gang babs su, bla ma'i bris 'bur gyi sku legs par bshams, mchod pa ci nus su bkod pa mdzes par byas te, gzhan gyi g-yam la brgyugs pa'i kha phyir bltas dang, tshe 'di tsam gyi ched du ma yin par sangs rgyas thob pa'i phyir, (dge sems khyad par can gyi ngang nas) nyams su len par bya'o
rows.english: Here is the first.  Choose an appropriate spot in your home and set up, in a beautiful way, an image of your Lama--either painted or carved.  Before your Lama place as many lovely offerings as you can, according to your means.  Begin the ritual then by putting your mind into an exceptional state of virtue, meaning that you avoid focusing on things around you--you avoid doing these practices just so you can follow the crowd, or simply get something in this present life.  Rather, you do them so you can attain enlightenment. Going for Shelter, and the Wish for Enlightenment

rows.acip: SEMS CAN THAMS CAD BDE BA DANG LDAN PAR GYUR CIG SNYAM PA'I BYAMS PA 'TSAD MED DANG, SDUG BSNGAL DANG BRAL BAR GYUR CIG SNYAM PA'I SNYING RJE TSAD MED DANG, BDE BA DANG MI 'BRAL BAR GYUR CIG SNYAM PA'I DGA' BA TSAD MED DANG, NYE RING GNYIS DANG BRAL BAR GYUR CIG SNYAM PA'I BTANG SNYOMS TSAD MED DE (TSAD MED BZHI) BSGOM PAR BYA BA (SNGON DU BTANG) BA RGYAS BSDUS RANG GIS SKABS DANG BSTUN PA DANG,
rows.wylie: sems can thams cad bde ba dang ldan par gyur cig snyam pa'i byams pa 'tshad med dang, sdug bsngal dang bral bar gyur cig snyam pa'i snying rje tshad med dang, bde ba dang mi 'bral bar gyur cig snyam pa'i dga' ba tshad med dang, nye ring gnyis dang bral bar gyur cig snyam pa'i btang snyoms tshad med de (tshad med bzhi) bsgom par bya ba (sngon du btang) ba rgyas bsdus rang gis skabs dang bstun pa dang
rows.english: Meditate now upon the four infinite thoughts.  The first is the infinite thought of love, where we think to ourselves, "May every living being find happiness."  Then comes the infinite thought of compassion: "May every living being be freed from pain."  After that, the infinite thought of joy: "May they never be without happiness," and then the infinite thought of equanimity--"May they be free of any feeling that some are closer to them, and some less close."  Do these practices before you do anything else, in a more extensive or else briefer form, depending on your own circumstances.

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, RANG LHA'I (RNAL 'BYOR) RGYAS BSDUS GANG RUNG (DANG LDAN PA'I SKU LAS 'OD ZER 'PHROS, SNOD BCUD THAMS CAD KYI MA DAG PA)'I NYES SKYON THA MAL GYI SNANG ZHEN DANG MI GTZANG BA BGEGS DANG BCAS PA RNAMS (SBYANG STE SNOD) KYI 'JIG RTEN THAMS CAD (GZHAL YAS KHANG DANG, BCUD) KYI SEMS CAN (THAMS CAD LHA DANG LHA MO'I RANG BZHIN GYI DAG PA RAB 'BYAMS 'BA' ZHIG TU GYUR) PA STE DAG PA KHO NAR GYUR BAR (BSAM) PA'O,,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, rang lha'i (rnal 'byor) rgyas bsdus gang rung (dang ldan pa'i sku las 'od zer 'phros, snod bcud thams cad kyi ma dag pa)'i nyes skyon tha mal gyi snang zhen dang mi gtsang ba bgegs dang bcas pa rnams (sbyang ste snod) kyi 'jig rten thams cad (gzhal yas khang dang, bcud) kyi sems can (thams cad lha dang lha mo'i rang bzhin gyi dag pa rab 'byams 'ba' zhig tu gyur) pa ste dag pa kho nar gyur bar (bsam) pa'o
rows.english: Here is the first.  We begin with a deep practice of the Angel which is either extensive or else briefer.  From our holy body fly forth rays of light.  They go and clean every world, and every being that lives upon every world, of each and every impurity; that is, of every fault or problem--such as the belief that things are just normal, and everything else which is unclean, or an obstacle to our spiritual progress.  Watch as each of the worlds--each of the planets that there are--becomes a celestial mansion, and all the beings (all the suffering beings) become man and woman Angels--a veritable universe of total purity.  That is, they become nothing other than absolutely pure. Blessing the Inner Offering and Other Substances

rows.english: This brings us to the second major part: the main part of the ritual.  This is more easily performed if we recite it in verses of poetry, rather than in prose.  And so we should speak out the following lines, without allowing ourselves to be distracted to something else, in any way.  That is, we go through the ceremony even as we reflect upon its--the ritual's--meaning.  These lines are presented in the way of a bridge to the next section.

rows.english: This in turn recalls references which speak of the bodhisattva named "Essence of the Earth" being located at the eyes, and so on.  And so we must see how the final purification of our eyes is, in reality, the bodhisattva Essence of the Earth; of our ears, the bodisattva named "Holder of the Diamond"; of our nose, "Essence of the Sky"; of our tongue, Loving Eyes; of our mind, Glorious Gentle Voice; of our body, Remover of Obstacles; of our tendons and ligaments, Loving One; and of our joints, Total Excellence.

rows.acip: 'O NA BLA MA DE NGO BO'I KHYAD PAR THA MAL PA ZHIG YIN NAM SNYAM NA, DE NI MA YIN TE, (RAB 'BYAMS) TE DE LA RAB 'BYAMS MTSAMS SBYOR, RAB 'BYAMS RGYUD, RAB 'BYAMS RGYUD BAR MA, RAB 'BYAMS RGYA MTSO'I ZHING RNAMS NA BZHUGS PA'I (RGYAL BA) STE MI MTHUN PA'I PHYOGS THAMS CAD LAS RGYAL BA'I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS (KUN GYI) THUGS GNYIS SU MED PA'I (YE SHES) DE NI,
rows.wylie: 'o na bla ma de ngo bo'i khyad par tha mal pa zhig yin nam snyam na, de ni ma yin te, (rab 'byams) te de la rab 'byams mtshams sbyor, rab 'byams rgyud, rab 'byams rgyud bar ma, rab 'byams rgya mtsho'i zhing rnams na bzhugs pa'i (rgyal ba) ste mi mthun pa'i phyogs thams cad las rgyal ba'i sangs rgyas rnams (kun gyi) thugs gnyis su med pa'i (ye shes) de ni
rows.english: "Well then," one may ask.  "Is this Lama, in Their very nature, someone who is a normal person?"  Indeed They are not, for They are the wisdom of billions of Victors--which is to say, the wisdom of those Buddhas who are living in billions of paradises, where "billions" is actually just a word for billions of billions, or zillions, or jillions, or superjillions.  These Buddhas are "Victors" in that They have prevailed over each and every thing that could ever work against a person's spiritual progress.  And we are talking about the indivisible wisdom in the holy hearts of all these Buddhas
rows.raw: {"course": "TCS18Commentary", "acip": "'O NA BLA MA DE NGO BO'I KHYAD PAR THA MAL PA ZHIG YIN NAM SNYAM NA, DE NI MA YIN TE, (RAB 'BYAMS) TE DE LA RAB 'BYAMS MTSAMS SBYOR, RAB 'BYAMS RGYUD, RAB 'BYAMS RGYUD BAR MA, RAB 'BYAMS RGYA MTSO'I ZHING RNAMS NA BZHUGS PA'I (RGYAL BA) STE MI MTHUN PA'I PHYOGS THAMS CAD LAS RGYAL BA'I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS (KUN GYI) THUGS GNYIS SU MED PA'I (YE SHES) DE NI,", "wylie": "'o na bla ma de ngo bo'i khyad par tha mal pa zhig yin nam snyam na, de ni ma yin te, (rab 'byams) te de la rab 'byams mtshams sbyor, rab 'byams rgyud, rab 'byams rgyud bar ma, rab 'byams rgya mtsho'i zhing rnams na bzhugs pa'i (rgyal ba) ste mi mthun pa'i phyogs thams cad las rgyal ba'i sangs rgyas rnams (kun gyi) thugs gnyis su med pa'i (ye shes) de ni", "english": "\"Well then,\" one may ask.  \"Is this Lama, in Their very nature, someone who is a normal person?\"  Indeed They are not, for They are the wisdom of billions of Victors--which is to say, the wisdom of those Buddhas who are living in billions of paradises, where \"billions\" is actually just a word for billions of billions, or zillions, or jillions, or superjillions. rows.english: But it doesn't need to end with that: we can just as well picture worlds equal in number to the drops of water in trillions of vast oceans, along with however many enlightened realms there may be in every corner of the universe, and offer all of them. rows.english: What does it mean then to possess the qualifications of a spiritual friend of the greater way?  These are qualities that make one worthy to teach, to ones disciples, the steps which one undertakes on the path that we travel to the level of an Enlightened Being--that we use to go to that highest place of bliss, a bliss where we have succeeded in eliminating each and every undesirable characteristic within ourselves.

rows.acip: REG BYA RDO RJE MA SOGS YUM LNGA LA YANG DE LTAR PHYE BAS NYER LNGA, 'DOD YON GYI LHA MO GZUGS RDO RJE MA SOGS BZHI LA YANG DE LTAR LNGA LNGAR PHYE BAS NYI SHU, BYAMS PA KUN BZANG GNYIS MA GTOGS PA'I SA SNYING SOGS DRUG LA'ANG DE LTAR PHYE BAS SUM CU STE,

rows.acip: SEMS CAN (GZHAN BDE) BA DANG DE'I RGYU RNAMS DANG LDAN NA CI MA RUNG SNYAM PA'I BYAMS PA DANG, DE DANG MA BRAL NA SNYAM PA'I (DGA' BA) KHYAD PAR CAN RGYUD LA (SKYE BAR) RO,,
rows.wylie: sems can (gzhan bde) ba dang de'i rgyu rnams dang ldan na ci ma rung snyam pa'i byams pa dang, de dang ma bral na snyam pa'i (dga' ba) khyad par can rgyud la (skye bar) ro
rows.english: And we are asking then to be blessed to develop an extraordinary form of joy, which begins with feelings of love where we hope that every other living being might come to have happiness, and the things that cause this happiness, and then goes on to a hope that they never come to lose this happiness.

rows.acip: 'DI DAG GI SNGA MAS NI SNYING RJE DANG 'DIS NI BYAMS PA DANG DGA' BA GNYIS BSTAN LA, BDAG GZHAN MNYAM PAR BRJE BAS NI BTANG SNYOMS BSTAN TO,,
rows.wylie: 'di dag gi snga mas ni snying rje dang 'dis ni byams pa dang dga' ba gnyis bstan la, bdag gzhan mnyam par brje bas ni btang snyoms bstan to
rows.english: In the earlier part of this section we were describing compassion; and then here we have covered love and joy.  The practice of seeing ourselves and others as equal, and then exchanging each other, represents equanimity, [thus including all four of the infinite thoughts].

rows.acip: GZHAN YANG RJE BTZUN BLA MA KHYOD KYIS, BDAG LA SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI (BDAG GZHAN BRJE BA'I RNAL 'BYOR) DE LTA BU (NYAMS LEN SNYING POR) TE GTZO BOR (BYED PAR BYIN GYIS RLOBS) SHIG CES GSOL BA LTAR MDZAD RIGS PA'ANG YIN TE,
rows.wylie: gzhan yang rje btsun bla ma khyod kyis, bdag la sngar bshad pa ltar gyi (bdag gzhan brje ba'i rnal 'byor) de lta bu (nyams len snying por) te gtso bor (byed par byin gyis rlobs) shig ces gsol ba ltar mdzad rigs pa'ang yin te
rows.english: It is appropriate as well at this point if we make the supplication as follows: "Bless me then, o Holy Lama, that for me this deep practice of exchanging others for myself, as it was just described, might become the very heart or principal focus of my daily path."

rows.acip: (CHOS KUN) GYI (SNYING PO) GCIG TU DRIL BA (STOBS LNGA'I NYAMS LEN) SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR (GYI) SGO NA(S,) KUN RDZOB DANG, DON DAM (BYANG CHUB) KYI (SEMS GNYIS 'PHEL BA'I LAM) DU (BSGYUR TE) YID MI BDE BA MED PAR (YID BDE 'BA' ZHIG SGOM PAR) RO,,
rows.wylie: (chos kun) gyi (snying po) gcig tu dril ba (stobs lnga'i nyams len) sngar bshad pa ltar (gyi) sgo na(s,) kun rdzob dang, don dam (byang chub) kyi (sems gnyis 'phel ba'i lam) du (bsgyur te) yid mi bde ba med par (yid bde 'ba' zhig sgom par) ro
rows.english: We are asking then to be blessed that we can use a practice of the five powers (the ones just explained), which combines within it the essence of all the Dharma there is, for changing events into a path for increasing the two forms of the Wish--in both its deceptive and ultimate forms.  And with this then we experience only joy, and never any sense of feeling upset.

rows.acip: (BLO SBYONG) GI (DAM TSIG) DANG, (BSLAB BYA'I) RIM PA RNAMS RANG RANG GI GZHUNG BLO SBYONG SOGS NAS 'BYUNG BA LTAR (NYAMS LEN GYI) BYA BA LA BRTZON PA(S DAL 'BYOR) GYI MI LUS RIN PO CHE 'DI NI, GTAN GYI BDE BA THOB PAR BYED PA'I 'DUN MA SOGS KYI (DON CHEN) DU (BYED PAR RO,,)
rows.wylie: (blo sbyong) gi (dam tshig) dang, (bslab bya'i) rim pa rnams rang rang gi gzhung blo sbyong sogs nas 'byung ba ltar (nyams len gyi) bya ba la brtson pa(s dal 'byor) gyi mi lus rin po che 'di ni, gtan gyi bde ba thob par byed pa'i 'dun ma sogs kyi (don chen) du (byed par ro,,)
rows.english: We ask next that our Lama bless us to be able to make great efforts in practicing the teachings on developing the good heart--all the various commitments within these teachings, and the different kinds or steps of the trainings found there, just as they are found in the scriptures on developing the good heart and so forth that treat each of them.  By using these, I will bring great meaning to this life--this precious body--of leisure and fortune.  This meaning would be reflected for example in a strong desire to attain ultimate happiness.

rows.acip: DE RNAMS KYANG SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYIS THOB PAS BDE BA DANG LONGS SPYOD PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DANG LDAN PAR BSAM LA BYAMS PA BSGOM PAR BYA ZHING DE BZHIN TU RLUNG RANG GI SNA BUG TU TSUR 'JUG PA'I TSE DE LA SEMS CAN GYI SDUG BSNGAL MI 'DOD PA THAMS CAD BSKYON NAS RANG LA BSTIM PAS, SEMS CAN RNAMS SDUG BSNGAL RGYU DANG BCAS PA THAMS CAD DANG BRAL BAR BSAM LA SNYING RJE BSGOM PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: de rnams kyang sems can thams cad kyis thob pas bde ba dang longs spyod phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan par bsam la byams pa bsgom par bya zhing de bzhin tu rlung rang gi sna bug tu tshur 'jug pa'i tshe de la sems can gyi sdug bsngal mi 'dod pa thams cad bskyon nas rang la bstim pas, sems can rnams sdug bsngal rgyu dang bcas pa thams cad dang bral bar bsam la snying rje bsgom par bya'o
rows.english: We meditate thus upon thoughts of love, where we see every suffering being receiving the things we have sent forth--and they become possessed of the most excellent happiness and possessions.  In the same way, we watch our breath too as it enters back in through our two nostrils.  All the pain of every living creature--everything they never wanted to happen to them--comes riding back in on the breath, and melts down into us.  With this we meditate upon thoughts of compassion, where we watch as every one of these beings is free from all pain, and all the causes of this pain.

rows.acip: DER MA ZAD (THEG PA MCHOG) GI (TSUL KHRIMS GSUM GYI) STE DE YANG, BYANG SEMS KYI SO SO THAR PA NI NYES SPYOD SDOM PA'I TSUL KHRIMS DANG, BSDU BA'I DNGOS PO BZHI NI SEMS CAN DON BYED KYI TSUL KHRIMS DANG, PHYIN DRUG GI NYAMS LEN NI DGE BA CHOS SDUD KYI TSUL KHRIMS TE GSUM MO, ,DE DAG GI (NYAMS LEN LA BRTZON PA LHUR LEN) TE GTZO BOR (BYED PAR) RO,,
rows.wylie: der ma zad (theg pa mchog) gi (tshul khrims gsum gyi) ste de yang, byang sems kyi so so thar pa ni nyes spyod sdom pa'i tshul khrims dang, bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhi ni sems can don byed kyi tshul khrims dang, phyin drug gi nyams len ni dge ba chos sdud kyi tshul khrims te gsum mo, ,de dag gi (nyams len la brtson pa lhur len) te gtso bor (byed par) ro
rows.english: But this is not all; we are also asking blessings for our practice of all three forms of the morality of the highest way.  This would be the following three: (1) the morality where we refrain from negative actions--the bodhisattva's practice of the vows of individual freedom; (2) the morality where we work for the goals of others--the bodhisattva's practice of the four methods of gathering disciples; and (3) the morality where we gather goodness--their practice of the six perfections.  And we are asking to be blessed to devote ourselves to--to concentrate primarily upon--the practice of these three.

rows.acip: DE YANG THAR 'DOD RNAMS KYI PHUN SUM TSOGS PA THAMS CAD KYI GZHI RTEN, LEGS TSOGS MA LUS PA'I 'BYUNG GNAS, MCHOG DANG THUN MONG GI DNGOS GRUB MTHA' YAS PA KUN GYI RTZA BA, THEG PA MCHOG GI RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS KYIS NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BYA BA'I MAN NGAG MTHA' DAG GI GNAD BSDUS PA NI,

rows.english: There is but one thing which is the very foundation for all the wondrous things that will ever come to those who seek for freedom.  It is the very source from which each and every good thing springs forth.  It is the very root of infinite attainments--both those which are supreme, and those which are held in common.  It is an instruction which combines every crucial point found in all the spiritual advices put into practice by deep practitioners of the ultimate path.

rows.english: The all-knowing Lord has said as well, See that the very root For setting in motion the forces That will bring to you every good thing In this life and those beyond it Is to take yourself, and properly, To a supreme spiritual guide, Striving to serve Them in both Your thoughts and actions too. Never give Them up then, Even if it should cost you your life; Please Them with the offering Of carrying out Their every instruction. This is what I, in my deep practice, Have carried out myself; Those of you who hope for freedom Should seek to do the same.

rows.acip: BDAG NYID GSANG BDE 'JIGS GSUM SOGS LHAG PA'I LHA GANG RUNG GI RNAL 'BYOR DANG LDAN PA'I SKU LAS 'OD ZER 'PHROS, SNOD BCUD THAMS CAD KYI MA DAG PA SBYANGS, SNOD THAMS CAD GZHAL YAS KHANG DANG, BCUD THAMS CAD LHA DANG LHA MO'I RANG BZHIN GYI DAG PA RAB 'BYAMS 'BA' ZHIG TU BSAM,
rows.wylie: bdag nyid gsang bde 'jigs gsum sogs lhag pa'i lha gang rung gi rnal 'byor dang ldan pa'i sku las 'od zer 'phros, snod bcud thams cad kyi ma dag pa sbyangs, snod thams cad gzhal yas khang dang, bcud thams cad lha dang lha mo'i rang bzhin gyi dag pa rab 'byams 'ba' zhig tu bsam
rows.english: Start off then with a deep practice where you see yourself as a god among gods--it could for example be any one of the three Angels of the Secret Collection, Highest Bliss, or the Lord of Terror.  Now, from your holy body, fly forth rays of light.  They go and clean every world, and every being that lives upon every world, of each and every impurity.  Watch as each of the worlds becomes a celestial mansion, and all the beings become man and woman Angels--a veritable universe of total purity.

rows.acip: LAM GYI RIM PA'AM THEG PA CHEN PO BLO SBYONG GI GNAD YONGS SU RDZOGS PA LA BLO SBYONG BA RNAMS YA MA BRAL BA'I NYAMS LEN LA BRTZON PAR BYA ZHING, MJUG TU DGE BA RNAMS BZANG PO SPYOD PA LA SOGS PA SMON LAM GYI RGYAS 'DEBS SHING,
rows.wylie: lam gyi rim pa'am theg pa chen po blo sbyong gi gnad yongs su rdzogs pa la blo sbyong ba rnams ya ma bral ba'i nyams len la brtson par bya zhing, mjug tu dge ba rnams bzang po spyod pa la sogs pa smon lam gyi rgyas 'debs shing

rows.acip: GNOD SEMS KYI NI, YAMS DANG GNOD PA DANG NAD 'GO BA DANG 'KHRUG PA DANG PHA ROL GYI DMAG TSOGS LAS 'KHRUG LONG MANG BA DANG SENG GE DANG STAG LA SOGS PA DANG SBRUL GDUG DANG SDIG PA DANG SRIN GYI ME MANG BA DANG GNOD SBYIN GDUG PA DANG CHOM RKUN LA SOGS PA MANG BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: gnod sems kyi ni, yams dang gnod pa dang nad 'go ba dang 'khrug pa dang pha rol gyi dmag tshogs las 'khrug long mang ba dang seng ge dang stag la sogs pa dang sbrul gdug dang sdig pa dang srin gyi me mang ba dang gnod sbyin gdug pa dang chom rkun la sogs pa mang ba dang
rows.english: Because you have wished bad things on others, you live in a world of chaos, where diseases spread, and evil is everywhere, and plague, and conflict, and fear from the armies of other nations; where there are many lions or leopards or other dangerous animals; where there are everywhere venomous snakes or scorpions or poison biting worms; you live surrounded by harmful spirits, and thieves or muggers, and the like.

rows.acip: GANG ZAG DE NI ZHE SDANG LAS BYUNG BA'I NGANG TSUL NGAN PA DANG LDAN PAS NGAN SONG RNAMS SU SKYES PA STE, 'DI LTA STE, SENGGE DANG, STAG DANG, BYA ROG DANG, WA DANG, DRED MO DANG, SBRUL NAG PO DANG, YI DVAGS DANG, SHA ZA LA SOGS PA LTA BU'O,,
rows.wylie: gang zag de ni zhe sdang las byung ba'i ngang tshul ngan pa dang ldan pas ngan song rnams su skyes pa ste, 'di lta ste, sengge dang, stag dang, bya rog dang, wa dang, dred mo dang, sbrul nag po dang, yi dvags dang, sha za la sogs pa lta bu'o
rows.english: There are people who possess an undesirable character born from constant thoughts of anger.  They are thus born into the lower realms, becoming creatures such as the lion; the tiger; crow, fox, bear, or cobra—or else something like a craving spirit, or a hungry ghost.

rows.acip: ,JI LTAR GSUNGS ZHE NA LAG BZANG GIS ZHUS PA LAS, GZHAN YANG BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' 'DI LTAR YANG DAG PAR RJES SU SLOB STE GANG DAG SENG GE DANG , STAG DANG , KHYI DANG , CE SPYANG DANG , BYA RGOD DANG KHRUNG KHRUNG DANG BYA ROG DANG 'UG PA DANG SRIN BU DANG , SBRANG MA DANG SBRANG BU DANG SHA SBRANG DU GYUR PA DE DAG KYANG BLA NA MED PAR BYANG CHUB TU 'TSANG RGYA BAR 'GYUR NA BDAG MIR GYUR BZHIN DU SROG GI PHYIR YANG BYANG CHUB THOB PA'I BRTZON 'GRUS RTZOM PAR BYED SNYAM MO, , ZHES PA DANG , DKON MCHOG SPRIN LAS KYANG GSUNGS SO,
rows.wylie: ji ltar gsungs zhe na lag bzang gis zhus pa las, gzhan yang byang chub sems dpa' 'di ltar yang dag par rjes su slob ste gang dag seng ge dang , stag dang , khyi dang , ce spyang dang , bya rgod dang khrung khrung dang bya rog dang 'ug pa dang srin bu dang , sbrang ma dang sbrang bu dang sha sbrang du gyur pa de dag kyang bla na med par byang chub tu 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur na bdag mir gyur bzhin du srog gi phyir yang byang chub thob pa'i brtson 'grus rtsom par byed snyam mo, , zhes pa dang , dkon mchog sprin las kyang gsungs so
rows.english: And what are the words which they spoke? They come from the Sutra Requested by Subahu-- Bodhisattvas must, moreover, master the following way of thinking: "Even those beings who are lions, or tigers, or dogs, or wolves, or vultures, or cranes, or crows, or owls, or worms, or flies, or bees, or gnats can bring about the matchless state of enlightenment. And here am I, someone who is living the life of a human--now, no matter what, even if it costs me my life, I will put forth whatever effort is needed to reach enlightenment. This same point is made in the sutra known as The Cloud of the Jewels as well.

rows.english: You'll need to whirl A spear around, And wear some armor; And ornaments made Of bone, and such. You've got to have A yogi's staff, With a little box Hanging from it. And remember To get yourself together Things like a Skirt of tiger skin Hanging down, As you jump around; And with all this Assemble as well A human skull, And a thighbone trumpet. Again a reference to apparently fake practitioners of the secret teachings—which in recent times in Asia has included oracles who claim to be able to tell the future, in a seance in which they act wildly and say strange things.  There are of course genuine oracles, but as usual their behavior is typically very sincere and moral.

rows.english: In future days, when I reach total enlightenment—when I reach my own matchless, perfect, and complete Buddhahood—there will be certain beings who have no one to help them.  Their bodies will be threatened by fires; or they will be thrown in among wild beasts like lions, or tigers; brown bears, snow bears, or poisonous snakes.  Their lives will be in danger; they will feel terrified…no one will be there to protect them, they will cry out, over and over.

rows.english: In the year called Goodness then--that is, in the male water tiger year 1662--on the 13th day of the month of Fragrance, the time for him to withdraw his holy form came upon us.  He folded his legs in the lotus posture, passed into meditation, and transformed himself into the body of reality: to clear light itself. * * * Give the Dharma Our preparation for entering the path of the secret teachings continues, in the third course of the Tantric Series, through the various vows that form the foundation for successful secret practice.  So far, we have covered the refuge commitments; the vows of individual liberation; and the root bodhisattva vows.  We now turn to the secondary offenses against the vows of a bodhisattva. Again, we are using as our source The String of Shining Jewels (ACIP digital text S0201), by Geshe Tsewang Samdrup (c. 1835), tutor to His Holiness the Tenth Dalai Lama.  The selection is drawn from folios 18a-18b.

rows.acip: RANG NYID KYI BRJED BYANG DANG , SKAL MNYAM GZHAN LA'ANG PHAN 'DOD KYI BSAM PAS KUN NAS BLANGS TE, LAM 'DI LA SNYING NAS MOS PA'I BTZUN GZUGS DAM TSIG RDO RJES 'JAM MGON CHOS KYI RGYAL PO'I LEGS BSHAD RNAMS LAS NYE BAR BSDUS TE GSAL ZHING GO BDE BAR LHA LDAN SPRUL PA'I GTZUG LAG KHANG CHEN PO'I NYE 'DABS SU SA STAG LO'I DBYAR ZLA 'BRING PO'I TSES BCU'I NYIN TSOGS KYI 'KHOR LO'I MCHOD PA DANG BCAS LEGS PAR SBYAR BA'I YI GE PA NI DAM GTZANG DGE SLONG BLO BZANG NAM MKHA' RDO RJE'O,,

rows.english: I have set this work down so that I myself would never forget the points contained in it, and also with the hope that it would be of some help to others as fortunate as myself.  My name is Damtsik Dorje, and I am a mere shadow of a monk who nonetheless believes in this particular path from the very bottom of his heart.  I wrote the text by collecting together the relevant explanations by our Gentle Protector, the King of the Dharma [Je Tsongkapa], and by putting them into a form that would be clear and easy to understand. The work has been completed, in a fitting way, on the tenth day of the month, and we have concluded it with an offering of the secret feast.  This is in the middle month of summer in the earth tiger year [probably 1818], in a place very close to the Great Temple of the Emanation, in Lhasa.  The scribe for the text was that monk of pure pledges, Lobsang Namka Dorje. *** C. How to Restore the Vows, And the Benefits of Honoring Them Lord Atisha begins this section, with strangely encouraging words for those of us who are vow-challenged. rows.acip: KUN 'DUS NOR BU'I LUGS LA GCER BU'ANG STAG SHAM CAN LAS DAR GYI NA BZA' BYED PA GTAN MIN PAS PHYAG GA-YAS d'A MA RU PHYI DKAR BA THABS DANG NANG DMAR BA SHES RAB, DE GNYIS GCIG LA TSANG BA BDE STONG DBYER MED GYI CHOS SGRA SGROG PA GSUNG CHOS DKON MCHOG ,
rows.wylie: kun 'dus nor bu'i lugs la gcer bu'ang stag sham can las dar gyi na bza' byed pa gtan min pas phyag ga-yas DA ma ru phyi dkar ba thabs dang nang dmar ba shes rab, de gnyis gcig la tshang ba bde stong dbyer med gyi chos sgra sgrog pa gsung chos dkon mchog
rows.english: In the system of the all encompassing jewel you shouldn't ever visualize your Lama dressed in clothes of beautiful silken cloth; they are, rather, naked as a yogi, or wearing a loincloth of tiger skin.  In Their right hand They hold a damaru drum.  On the outside it is colored white, which represents method; and on the inside it is colored red, which represents wisdom.  The drum is sounding out a clamour of teachings on how indivisible bliss and emptiness are complete then in a single object.  This sound represents the Dharma Jewel.

rows.english: Because you have wished bad things on others, you live in a world of chaos, where diseases spread, and evil is everywhere, and plague, and conflict, and fear from the armies of other nations; where there are many lions or leopards or other dangerous animals; where there are everywhere venomous snakes or scorpions or poison biting worms; surrounded by harmful spirits, and thieves or muggers, and the like.

rows.english: They say that, from among these, earth, water, plants, fire, and wind only possess a single sense power; conches, worms, and oysters have two; creatures like ants and fireflies have three; those like bees, flies, and mosquitos have four senses; while humans, birds, and four-legged animals possess five sense powers.

rows.acip: DGAG BYA LA SPYIR 'DOD TSUL MANG YANG 'DIR DBU MA THAL 'GYUR BA'I LUGS LTAR BSHAD PAR BYA'O, , DE YANG MDO LAS, DE DAG RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PA YIN, , ZHES DANG , BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS, RTOG PA YOD PA KHO NAS YOD PA NYID DANG ZHES SOGS DANG , RJES DGONGS PA RAB GSAL LAS, CHOS RNAMS RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PAR GSUNGS TE, CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM DANG RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PAR GSUNGS PA MANG NGO ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR,
rows.wylie: dgag bya la spyir 'dod tshul mang yang 'dir dbu ma thal 'gyur ba'i lugs ltar bshad par bya'o, , de yang mdo las, de dag rtog pa'i dbang gis bzhag pa yin, , zhes dang , bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel pa las, rtog pa yod pa kho nas yod pa nyid dang zhes sogs dang , rjes dgongs pa rab gsal las, chos rnams rtog pa'i dbang gis bzhag par gsungs te, chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa tsam dang rtog pa'i dbang gis bzhag par gsungs pa mang ngo zhes gsungs pa ltar
rows.english: Generally speaking there are a great number of different positions that exist about what the object we deny exactly is. Here though I will give my explanation according to the position of the Consequence section of the Middle Way school. A certain sutra says that "They are all established through concepts." The Commentary to the Four Hundred too contains lines such as the one which says, "It is only due to the existence of concepts that existence itself can exist, and..." The Lord, in his Illumination of the True Thought, says as well that "These lines [from sutra] are describing how all existing things are established by force of concepts; and we see many other such statements, that all existing objects are simply labelled with our concepts, and are established only by force of concepts."

rows.acip: RNAM BSHAD DGONGS PA RAB GSAL LAS, RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PAR MYANG 'DAS KUN RDZOB BDEN PAR GSUNGS PA'I DON, MYANG 'DAS DON DAM PA'I BDEN PAR YOD PA BLO KUN RDZOB PA LA BLTOS NAS 'JOG DGOS PA'I DON DU GSUNGS PA DANG , DRANG NGES RNAM 'BYED LAS KYANG CHOS NYID CHOS NYID DU GRUB PAR GSUNGS PA DANG , BSKAL BZANG MIG 'BYED LAS KYANG GNAS LUGS SU GRUB PA TZAM GYIS DON DAM PAR GRUB MI DGOS PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: rnam bshad dgongs pa rab gsal las, rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel par myang 'das kun rdzob bden par gsungs pa'i don, myang 'das don dam pa'i bden par yod pa blo kun rdzob pa la bltos nas 'jog dgos pa'i don du gsungs pa dang , drang nges rnam 'byed las kyang chos nyid chos nyid du grub par gsungs pa dang , bskal bzang mig 'byed las kyang gnas lugs su grub pa tsam gyis don dam par grub mi dgos par gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: And this is true first of all because the Perfect Explanation, an Illumination of the True Thought, states that--when the commentary to the Sixty Verses of Reasoning describes nirvana as deceptive reality--what it means is that nirvana must be established as existing as ultimate reality with reference to a deceived state of mind. Distinguishing between the Figurative and the Literal also states that the real nature of things exists as the real nature of things; and Opening the Eyes of the Good and Fortune states that it doesn't automatically mean that something exists ultimately just because it exists as the real nature of things.

rows.english: And this is true first of all because the Perfect Explanation, an Illumination of the True Thought, states that--when the commentary to the Sixty Verses of Reasoning describes nirvana as deceptive reality--what it means is that nirvana must be established as existing as ultimate reality with reference to a deceived state of mind. rows.english: Now as for the three qualities of activity, darkness, and light, the pleasant feeling of things that you like relates to light. rows.wylie: mchims mdzod nas, mdo las las dge mi dge lung ma bstan gsum gsungs pa las dus re zhig las kyi rnam smin yid du 'ong ba bde ba myong ba dang gtan du sdug bsngal las skyob pa myang 'das thob byed ni dge ba dang , rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba mi bde ba myong ba ni mi dge ba dang , yid du 'ong mi 'ong skyed pa de gnyis las gzhan pa'i las ni dge mi dge las gzhan pa lung ma bstan yin no
rows.english: The Treasure House of Chim [Chim Jampey Yang's commentary to the Abhidharmakosha] states: Sutra describes three kinds of karma: virtuous karma, non-virtuous karma, and neutral karma. Virtue is that karma which, in the short term, brings you a karmic ripening which is desirable (that is, a feeling of pleasure), and ultimately protects you from suffering (that is, helps you achieve nirvana). Non-virtue is that karma which brings you a karmic ripening which is undesirable (that is, a feeling of pain). A neutral deed, something neither virtuous nor non-virtuous, is that karma which brings you something which is neither desirable nor undesirable. 49 The Asian Classics Institute Course V: How Karma Works Reading Four: The Correlation of Deeds and Their Results

rows.english: What does it mean to help those who are not of a higher kind? The act of assisting many beings refers to helping beings to avoid developing non-virtues that they don't already have, and giving up those which they do; that is, it refers to protecting them, in the meantime, from the lower realms.

You realize that there is no one to protect you, No one in any direction at all, And the darkness then comes and envelops you. In this place, there is no one at all who can protect you; At that moment nothing you can do for yourself.

rows.acip: ,BZHI PA NI, DMYAL BAR SKYES NAS DMYAL SRUNGS RNAMS MTHONG BA'I TSE KYI HUD SKYES BU SU ZHIG GIS 'JIGS PA CHEN PO 'DI LAS BDAG LEGS PAR SKYOB PAR BYED PAR 'GYUR ZHES SHIN TU SKRAG CING BRED SHA 'THON PA'I MIG BGRAD NAS PHYOGS BZHIR SKYABS DAG TSOL BAR BYED LA DE LTAR BTZAL YANG PHYOGS BZHIR SKYABS MED PAR MTHONG NAS NI DE NAS KUN TU YI MUG 'GYUR BAS DA LTA NYID NAS DKON MCHOG GSUM LA SKYABS SU 'GRO BAR BYA'O, , DES NA DMYAL BA'I GNAS DER 'JIGS PA LAS SKYOB PA'I SKYABS YOD PA MA YIN NA DUS DE'I TSE BDAG GIS JI LTAR BYA THABS CI YANG MED PAS DA LTA NYID NAS 'JIGS PA DANG BRAL BA'I RGYU LA 'BAD PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: bzhi pa ni, dmyal bar skyes nas dmyal srungs rnams mthong ba'i tshe kyi hud skyes bu su zhig gis 'jigs pa chen po 'di las bdag legs par skyob par byed par 'gyur zhes shin tu skrag cing bred sha 'thon pa'i mig bgrad nas phyogs bzhir skyabs dag tshol bar byed la de ltar btsal yang phyogs bzhir skyabs med par mthong nas ni de nas kun tu yi mug 'gyur bas da lta nyid nas dkon mchog gsum la skyabs su 'gro bar bya'o, , des na dmyal ba'i gnas der 'jigs pa las skyob pa'i skyabs yod pa ma yin na dus de'i tshe bdag gis ji ltar bya thabs ci yang med pas da lta nyid nas 'jigs pa dang bral ba'i rgyu la 'bad par bya'o
rows.english: Here now is the fourth part: the description of how, in your future life, you will be tormented by pain. And once you have taken your birth in the hells, and you see the hellguards coming for you, then will you be overcome with fear, and scream out, "Ah! Where is there now anyone who can save me completely from this horror?" Your face takes on a look of terror, your eyes open wide with panic, and you turn in every direction to look for someone who can help. You can look, but then you realize that there is no one to protect you, no one in any direction at all, and then the darkness comes and envelops you. Thus it is that you must, from this very moment, take refuge in the Three Jewels. Once you are in this place, in the hells, there is no one at all who can protect you from the terrors of the hells, there is at that moment absolutely nothing that you can do for yourself. And so you should, right now, make efforts in those practices which can save you from the terror later.

rows.english: Here is the third. So too I rejoice in the total enlightenment which has been reached by those who protect all other living beings; and in the ten levels which the different sons and daughters of the victorious Buddhas have attained. I rejoice as well in the causes for all these states, in the veritable ocean of the goodness of the wish for enlightenment: the thought to attain highest enlightenment in order to bring every living being to happiness. Beyond this I rejoice in the actual deeds of the beings with this wish: in the activities they undertake to help all living kind. I rejoice, with gladness, and I dwell in the faith of admiration, which is mixed in my mind with feelings of great happiness.

rows.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, BDAG GIS DE RING RGYAL BA SRAS DANG BCAS PA'I SKYOB PA THAMS CAD KYI SPYAN SNGAR 'GRO BA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD MTHAR THUG PHAN BDE THAMS CAD RDZOGS PA'I BDE BAR GSHEGS PA NYID DANG NI DE MA THOB KYI BAR DU'ANG LHA MI'I BDE BA LA TSIM PAR LONGS SPYAD PAS CHOG PA'I MGRON DU BOS ZIN GYIS DENG PHYIN CHAD LHA DANG LHA MIN DANG LTO 'PHYE LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYANG DGA' BAR GYIS SHIG CES GZHAN LA DGA' BA BSKYED DU GZHUG PA'O,

rows.english: With this we have reached how to bring joy to others. I stand today in the presence of all the Protectors: the victorious Buddhas, and their sons and daughters. And in your presence I invite every living creature, every being, to come here as my guest, for I will serve them to their heart's content the very state of Those Who have Gone to Bliss: the ultimate culmination of every kind of help and happiness. And until they reach this state I offer them as well to partake, to their own satisfaction, all the happiness that can be found among humans and pleasure beings. And once I have made this invitation, I ask others to take joy as well: I call on every pleasure being, and near pleasure being, and serpent-like naga, and all such creatures to feel gladness.

rows.acip: MDO LAS LAS DGE MI DGE LUNG MA BSTAN GSUM GSUNGS PA LAS DUS RE ZHIG LAS KYI RNAM SMIN YID DU 'ONG BA BDE BA MYONG BA DANG GTAN DU SDUG BSNGAL LAS SKYOB PA MYANG 'DAS THOB BYED NI DGE BA DANG , RNAM SMIN YID DU MI 'ONG BA MI BDE BA MYONG BA NI MI DGE BA DANG , YID DU 'ONG MI 'ONG SKYED PA DE GNYIS LAS GZHAN PA'I LAS NI DGE MI DGE LAS GZHAN PA LUNG MA BSTAN YIN NO,
rows.wylie: mdo las las dge mi dge lung ma bstan gsum gsungs pa las dus re zhig las kyi rnam smin yid du 'ong ba bde ba myong ba dang gtan du sdug bsngal las skyob pa myang 'das thob byed ni dge ba dang , rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba mi bde ba myong ba ni mi dge ba dang , yid du 'ong mi 'ong skyed pa de gnyis las gzhan pa'i las ni dge mi dge las gzhan pa lung ma bstan yin no
rows.english: Sutra describes three kinds of karma: virtuous karma, non- virtuous karma, and neutral karma. Virtue is that karma which, in the short term, brings you a karmic ripening which is desirable (that is, a feeling of pleasure), and ultimately protects you from suffering (that is, helps you achieve nirvana). Non-virtue is that karma which brings you a karmic ripening which is undesirable (that is, a feeling of pain). A neutral deed, something neither virtuous nor non-virtuous, is that karma which brings you something which is neither desirable nor undesirable. We return next to the commentary of His Holiness the First Dalai Lama: 16 Deeds according to Result
